The research in primatology not only aims to enhance our understanding of primate species but also addresses critical issues related to their conservation and the impact of human activities on their habitats. By studying primates, scientists gain insights into evolutionary processes, social dynamics, and the origins of human behavior.

sublevels.name: Animal Science
sublevels.description: An animal scientist applies principles of the biological, physical, and social sciences to the problems associated with livestock production and management.

sublevels.name: Animal Agriculture
sublevels.description: Animal Agriculture is the branch of agriculture concerned with animals that are raised for meat, fibre, milk, or other products. It includes day-to-day care, selective breeding, and the raising of livestock.

sublevels.name: Animal Anatomy
sublevels.description: Animal Histology, Animal Morphology.  Animal anatomy is the study of the structure of animals, including the internal structure of organs, muscles, bones, and other tissues.

sublevels.name: Veterinary Science
sublevels.description: Veterinary medicine and sciences comprise medical subsections and accompanying research concerned with the prevention, control, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases, disorders or injuries affecting the health and welfare of domestic and wild animals. The discipline includes monitoring, management and prevention of zoonotic diseases and advances research under the One Health approach. It further covers laboratory animal science and translational research. Veterinarians ensure a safe food supply for people by maintaining the health and welfare of food-producing animals and monitoring product quality. (Adopted and revised from ENCYCLOPÆDIA BRITANNICA)

sublevels.name: Animal Ethics
sublevels.description: Animal ethics is a branch of ethics which examines human-animal relationships, the moral consideration of animals and how nonhuman animals ought to be treated.

sublevels.name: Veterinary Clinical Medicine
sublevels.description: Veterinary Clinical Medicine is the branch of medicine that deals with the causes, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases and injuries of animals, especially domestic animals.

sublevels.name: Veterinary Microbiology
sublevels.description: Veterinary Microbiology is the study of the agents responsible for causing animal infections: bacteria, viruses, fungi or parasites.

sublevels.name: Cancer Biology
sublevels.description: Cancer biology is the field of study that focuses on understanding the mechanisms behind the development and progression of cancer. It encompasses various aspects of cancer research, including the cellular and molecular processes involved in tumor formation, growth, and metastasis.

sublevels.name: Cancer Therapy
sublevels.description: Cancer therapy describes the treatment of cancer in a patient, often with surgery, chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy. Targeted therapies are also available for some cancer types. A cancer patient might receive many different types of therapy, including those aimed at relieving the symptoms of cancer, such as pain.

sublevels.name: Radiation Oncology
sublevels.description: Radiotherapy, or radiation therapy, is the clinical use of high energy rays (ionizing radiation) to induce DNA damage in all exposed cells to ultimately kill cancer cells or prevent cancer growth. Radiotherapy may be used to eradicate some cancers, to reduce recurrence or as palliative treatment.

sublevels.name: Chemotherapy
sublevels.description: Chemotherapy is a treatment used to kill cancer cells. It involves taking one or more of a type of drug that interferes with the DNA of fast-growing cells. These drugs are subdivided into specific classes such as alkylating agents, antimetabolites, anthracyclines and topoisomerase inhibitors.

sublevels.name: Cancer Microenvironment
sublevels.description: The cancer microenvironment, or tumour microenvironment, describes the non-cancerous cells present in the tumour. These include fibroblasts, immune cells and cells that comprise the blood vessels. It also includes the proteins produced by all of the cells present in the tumour that support the growth of the cancer cells.

sublevels.name: Cancer Staging
sublevels.description: Neoplasm staging is a system for describing the extent of spread of tumours in patients. For example, the TNM classification of malignant tumours is a staging system used for describing the size of the primary tumour (T), if regional lymphnodes are involved (N) and the presence of metastasis (M).

sublevels.name: Cancer Genetics and Genomics
sublevels.description: Cancer genomics is the study of the totality of DNA sequence and gene expression differences between tumour cells and normal host cells. It aims to understand the genetic basis of tumour cell proliferation and the evolution of the cancer genome under mutation and selection by the body environment, the immune system and therapeutic interventions..Cancer genetics is the study in humans and other animals of heritable gene variants that cause or confer altered risk of tumour or hematological malignancy. Individual cancer risk varies and is influenced by familial and sporadic oncogene or tumour suppressor gene mutations as well as rare and common constitutional variants present in the population.

sublevels.name: Tumour Biomarkers
sublevels.description: Tumour biomarkers is a term used to describe many different potential markers of cancer development and progression. These markers can come in many forms – for example, proteins, biochemicals, DNA and RNA – and ideally they should be specific to a particular type of cancer and not present in normal tissues or in healthy individuals.

sublevels.name: Metastasis
sublevels.description: Metastasis is the spread of cancer to a part of the body distant from the original primary cancer. This occurs through the transfer of malignant or cancerous cells via lymph or blood. The new occurrences of cancer are called metastases.

sublevels.name: Tumour Immunology
sublevels.description: Tumour immunology describes the interaction between cells of the immune system with tumour cells. Understanding these interactions is important for the development of new therapies for cancer treatment.

sublevels.name: Cancer Imaging
sublevels.description: Cancer imaging is an umbrella term that covers the many approaches used to research and diagnose cancer. Originally used to diagnose and stage the disease, cancer imaging is now also used to assist with surgery and radiotherapy, to look for early responses to cancer therapies and to identify patients who are not responding to treatment.

sublevels.name: Tumour Angiogenesis
sublevels.description: Tumour angiogenesis describes the formation of new blood vessels in a tumour. This process makes use of the existing surrounding blood vessels and occurs as a result of signals sent by tumour cells and cells in the tumour microenvironment.

sublevels.name: Cancer Screening
sublevels.description: Cancer screening describes any procedure that aims to detect precancerous changes, such that cancer can be treated before it becomes malignant. Mammography and cervical smear tests are routine cancer-screening procedures. Ideally, the benefits of any screening procedure should outweigh the risks.

sublevels.name: Oncogenes
sublevels.description: An oncogene is a gene that will transform a cell in culture. Oncogenes were initially identified in cancer-causing retroviruses. Genes involved in the regulation of cell division, movement and signalling for example can function as oncogenes under specific conditions.

sublevels.name: Cancer Models
sublevels.description: Cancer models are naturally existing or artificially induced systems that share features with human cancers. Experimental systems for studying human cancer include cell lines and organisms such as fruit flies and genetically modified mice to investigate cancer biochemical or genetic pathways and pathology.

sublevels.name: Cancer Nanotechnology
sublevels.description: Cancer nanotechnology is a branch of nanotechnology concerned with the application of both nanomaterials (such as nanoparticles for tumour imaging or drug delivery) and nanotechnology approaches (such as nanoparticle-based theranostics) to the diagnosis and treatment of cancer.

sublevels.name: Tumour Heterogeneity
sublevels.description: Tumour heterogeneity describes differences between tumours of the same type in different patients, and between cancer cells within a tumour. Both can lead to different responses to therapy. Genetic and epigenetic differences between cancer cells within a tumour might explain why some tumour cells remain present in the patient after cancer treatment has finished.

sublevels.name: Tumour Virus Infections
sublevels.description: Tumour virus infections are caused by oncogenic DNA or RNA viruses. They can cause cancer by two different processes: directly through the expression of viral proteins that disrupt tissue cells and result in their transformation; and indirectly through mutation of the host cell DNA through viral integration (also known as insertional mutagenesis).

sublevels.name: Cancer Prevention
sublevels.description: Cancer prevention includes treatments, procedures and lifestyle changes that aim to reduce the risk that cancer will develop in an individual. Some cancer prevention strategies are well known and government-funded; for example, stopping smoking, eating a healthy diet and undergoing a specific screening procedure, such as mammography.

sublevels.name: Cancer Metabolism
sublevels.description: Cancer metabolism refers to the alterations in cellular metabolism pathways that are evident in cancer cells compared with most normal tissue cells. Metabolic alterations in cancer cells are numerous and include aerobic glycolysis, reduced oxidative phosphorylation and the increased generation of biosynthetic intermediates needed for cell growth and proliferation.

sublevels.name: Cancer Epidemiology
sublevels.description: Cancer epidemiology is the study of the distribution, determinants, and frequency of cancer in populations

sublevels.name: Cancers
sublevels.description: Cancer is a complex disease in which cells in a specific tissue are no longer fully responsive to the signals within the tissue that regulate cellular differentiation, survival, proliferation and death. As a result, these cells accumulate within the tissue, causing local damage and inflammation. There are over 200 different types of cancer.

sublevels.name: Breast Cancer
sublevels.description: Breast cancer is caused by the development of malignant cells in the breast. The malignant cells originate in the lining of the milk glands or ducts of the breast (ductal epithelium). Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women, but it can also appear in men.

sublevels.name: Urological Cancer
sublevels.description: Urological cancer refers to a group of cancers that originate in the urinary system and male reproductive organs. The urinary system includes the kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra, while the male reproductive organs consist of the prostate gland, testicles, and related structures.

sublevels.name: Prostate Cancer
sublevels.description: Prostate cancer is a type of malignancy that arises in the prostate gland. Prostate cancer tends to develop in older men, aged 50 and over. In many cases prostate cancer develops slowly, although in some cases it can be aggressive and metastasize to other parts of the body.

sublevels.name: Head and Neck Cancer
sublevels.description: Head and neck cancer comprises a group of biologically similar cancers that start in the lip, oral cavity (mouth), nasal cavity (inside the nose), paranasal sinuses, pharynx and larynx. Most head and neck cancers are squamous cell carcinomas that originate from the epithelium of these regions.

sublevels.name: Skin Cancer
sublevels.description: Skin cancer can involve melanocytes, leading to melanoma, but there are other non-melanoma skin cancers. These include basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma and, less commonly, Merkel cell carcinoma, Kaposi's sarcoma and T-cell lymphoma of the skin.

sublevels.name: Testicular Cancer
sublevels.description: Testicular cancer is a cancer that starts in the testis. The majority (95%) of testicular cancers are germ cell tumours. Treatment for testicular cancer is highly effective, with 5-year overall survival rates approaching 100% for localized disease.

sublevels.name: Lung Cancer
sublevels.description: Lung cancer arises in tissues of the lung, usually in the cells lining air passages. The two main types are small-cell lung cancer and non-small-cell lung cancer, according to the shape of cells under a microscope. The most common symptoms are coughing, shortness of breath and chest pains.

sublevels.name: Bone Cancer
sublevels.description: Bone cancer is characterized by uncontrolled growth of cells of the bone. Primary bone cancer (that arises directly in the bone), is relatively rare. Different types of bone tissue give rise to different types of primary bone cancer: osteosarcoma develops from cells that form the bone and Ewing sarcoma develops from immature nerve tissue within the bone.

sublevels.name: Paediatric Cancer
sublevels.description: Paediatric cancers are malignancies that occur in young children.The most common childhood cancers are leukaemia and brain tumors, such as gliomas.

sublevels.name: Cancer Stem Cells
sublevels.description: Cancer stem cells are rare immortal cells within a tumour that can both self-renew by dividing and give rise to many cell types that constitute the tumour, and can therefore form tumours. Such cells have been found in various types of human tumours and might be attractive targets for cancer treatment.

sublevels.name: Tumour-suppressor Proteins
sublevels.description: Tumour-suppressor proteins act to alleviate the potential for cancer and tumour formation by modulating cell growth either through negative regulation of the cell cycle or by promoting apoptosis. Mutation or dysregulation of tumour-suppressor proteins can lead to unregulated cell growth and tumour development.

sublevels.name: Food Science
sublevels.description: Food Science is a multi-disciplinary field involving chemistry, biochemistry, nutrition, microbiology and engineering to give one the scientific knowledge.

sublevels.name: Food Chemistry
sublevels.description: Chemistry of food constituents

sublevels.name: Nutrition
sublevels.description: Nutrition or Dietetics is the organic process of nourishing or being nourished, including the processes by which an organism assimilates food and uses it for growth and maintenance.

sublevels.name: Food Security
sublevels.description: Food security is the availability of food in a country (or geography) and the ability of individuals within that country (geography) to access, afford, and source adequate foodstuffs.

sublevels.name: Sports Nutrition
sublevels.description: Sports Nutrition is an interdisciplinary field of study concerned with the understanding of the body's use of nutrients during athletic competition (and the need for nutritional supplements), as well as the practical use of proper nutrition and dietary supplements to enhance athletic performance. Works in the field of Sports Nutrition commonly apply knowledge nutrition science, dietology, biochemistry, exercise physiology, cell and molecular biology. For instance, studies in Sports Nutrition focus on the different types and quantities of fluids and food taken by an athlete, and also deals with the consumption of nutrients such as vitamins, minerals, supplements and organic substances that include carbohydrates, proteins and fats.

sublevels.name: Food Microbiology
sublevels.description: Food microbiology is the scientific study of microorganisms, both in food and used for the production of food. This includes microorganisms that contaminate food, as well as those used in its production; for example to produce yoghurt, cheese, beer and wine.

sublevels.name: Food Analysis
sublevels.description: Food analysis is a diverse and interdisciplinary field of research that has a significant health, societal and economic impact. It aims to characterize food products in terms of chemical composition, traceability, safety, quality, sensory perception and nutritional value.

sublevels.name: Food Engineering
sublevels.description: Food engineering is a scientific, academic, and professional field that interprets and applies principles of engineering, science, and mathematics to food manufacturing and operations, including the processing, production, handling, storage, conservation, control, packaging and distribution of food products.

sublevels.name: Food Safety
sublevels.description: Food safety is used as a scientific discipline describing handling, preparation, and storage of food in ways that prevent food-borne illness.

sublevels.name: Sensory Evaluation
sublevels.description: Sensory evaluation is a scientific discipline used to evoke, measure, analyze, and interpret reaction to those characteristics of food material as they are perceived by the senses of sight, smell, taste, touch, and hearing (sound).

sublevels.name: Food Studies
sublevels.description: Food science is the study of the physical, biological (including microbiological) and chemical makeup of food. Food studies is an interdisciplinary field of study that examines various aspects of food, including its production, consumption, culture, history, sustainability, nutrition, and impact on society. It encompasses a wide range of disciplines, including anthropology, sociology, geography, history, nutrition, public health, environmental studies, and agriculture.

sublevels.name: Food Security
sublevels.description: Food security is the availability of food in a country (or geography) and the ability of individuals within that country (geography) to access, afford, and source adequate foodstuffs.

sublevels.name: Oenology
sublevels.description: Oenology is the scientific discipline concerned with the production, chemistry, microbiology, and quality evaluation of wine. It focuses on the processes involved in transforming grapes into wine, including fermentation, maturation, stabilization, and sensory assessment.

sublevels.name: Health Sciences
sublevels.description: The health sciences study all aspects of health, disease and healthcare. This field of study aims to develop knowledge, interventions and technology for use in healthcare to improve the treatment of patients.

sublevels.name: Clinical Medicine
sublevels.description: Clinical medicine is the branch of medical science that focuses on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of diseases and disorders in individual patients. It involves the application of medical knowledge and skills in a clinical setting, where healthcare professionals interact directly with patients. Clinical medicine integrates various disciplines, including anatomy, physiology, pathology, pharmacology, and medical ethics.

sublevels.name: Diseases
sublevels.description: Diseases are abnormal conditions that have a specific set of signs and symptoms. Diseases can have an external cause, such as an infection, or an internal cause, such as autoimmune diseases.

sublevels.name: Oral Diseases
sublevels.description: Oral diseases are inflammations of the teeth, gums or facial bones in the oral cavity.

sublevels.name: Haematological Diseases
sublevels.description: Haematological diseases are pathological conditions primarily affecting the blood or blood-producing organs. This group of disorders includes, but is not limited to, various types of anaemia, blood cancers and haemorrhagic conditions.

sublevels.name: Cardiovascular Diseases
sublevels.description: Cardiovascular diseases are pathological conditions affecting the heart and/or blood vessels, that is, the cardiovascular system.

sublevels.name: Rheumatic Diseases
sublevels.description: Rheumatic diseases is an umbrella term that encompasses the spectrum of musculoskeletal, arthritic and connective tissue disorders.

sublevels.name: Urogenital Disorders
sublevels.description: Urogenital disorders are diseases and abnormalities affecting the urinary system (kidneys, ureters, bladder, urethra) and the reproductive organs, including infectious, congenital, neoplastic, inflammatory, and functional conditions.

sublevels.name: Kidney Diseases
sublevels.description: Kidney diseases are hereditary and nonhereditary disorders that affect the kidney. Diabetes mellitus and high blood pressure are important risk factors for kidney disease.

sublevels.name: Immunological Disorders
sublevels.description: Immunological disorders are diseases or conditions caused by a dysfunction of the immune system and include allergy, asthma, autoimmune diseases, autoinflammatory syndromes and immunological deficiency syndromes.

sublevels.name: Gastrointestinal Diseases
sublevels.description: Gastrointestinal diseases are those that affect any section of the gastrointestinal tract, from the oesophagus to the rectum, and the accessory digestive organs, i.e. liver, gall bladder and pancreas. The term encompasses acute, chronic, recurrent or functional disorders and covers a wide range of diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease and functional dyspepsia.

sublevels.name: Eye Diseases
sublevels.description: Eye diseases are disorders affecting the structures of the human eye, including the cornea, lens, retina, optic nerve, conjunctiva, sclera, and uveal tract, encompassing infectious, inflammatory, degenerative, congenital, neoplastic, and functional conditions.

sublevels.name: Reproductive Disorders
sublevels.description: Reproductive disorders are diseases involving the reproductive system, including reproductive tract infections, congenital abnormalities, cancers of the reproductive system and sexual dysfunction.

sublevels.name: Metabolic Disease
sublevels.description: Metabolic disorders occur when the body's usual metabolic processes are disrupted. These diseases can be congenital or acquired, for example, diabetes and phenylketonuria.

sublevels.name: Nutrition Disorder
sublevels.description: Nutrition disorders are diseases that occur when a person's dietary intake does not contain the right amount of nutrients for healthy functioning, or when a person cannot correctly absorb nutrients from food. Nutrition disorders can be caused by undernutrition, overnutrition or an incorrect balance of nutrients.

sublevels.name: Obesity
sublevels.description: Obesity is a condition in which excess fat has accumulated in the body, such that it can have an adverse effect on health. Obesity is defined as a body mass index (BMI) of greater than 30 kg/m2.

sublevels.name: Respiratory Tract Diseases
sublevels.description: Respiratory tract diseases are illnesses that affect components of the respiratory system, including the nasal passages, the bronchi and the lungs. They range from acute infections, such as pneumonia and bronchitis, to chronic conditions such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

sublevels.name: Skin Diseases
sublevels.description: Skin diseases are pathologic conditions that affect the body's surfaces (also called the integument), including skin, hair, nails and associated glands. They can involve all layers of the skin and have numerous aetiologies such as infections, tumours or inflammation.

sublevels.name: Infectious Diseases
sublevels.description: Infectious diseases are caused by pathogenic microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, parasites or fungi, that infect a host organism and can be spread, directly or indirectly, from one organism to another. An infectiologist manages nosocomial (healthcare-acquired) or community-acquired infections.

sublevels.name: Sexually Transmitted Diseases
sublevels.description: Sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) are infections transmitted through sexual contact, caused by bacteria, viruses, or parasites, and include conditions such as chlamydia, gonorrhea, and HIV/AIDS.

sublevels.name: Diabetes
sublevels.description: Diabetes describes a group of metabolic diseases characterized by high blood sugar levels. Diabetes can be caused by the pancreas not producing insulin (type 1 diabetes) or by insulin resistance (cells do not respond to insulin; type 2 diabetes).

sublevels.name: Psychiatric Disorder
sublevels.description: Obsessive compulsive disorder is a psychiatric disease that is characterized by anxiety, fear and repetitive behaviour. Possible symptoms are excessive cleaning, repeated checking or hoarding.

sublevels.name: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
sublevels.description: Obsessive compulsive disorder is a psychiatric disease that is characterized by anxiety, fear and repetitive behaviour. Possible symptoms are excessive cleaning, repeated checking or hoarding.

sublevels.name: Autism Spectrum Disorders
sublevels.description: Autism spectrum disorders are a group of neurodevelopmental disorders that are characterized by impaired social interaction and communication skills, and are often accompanied by other behavioural symptoms such as repetitive or stereotyped behaviour and abnormal sensory processing. Individual symptoms and cognitive functioning vary across the autism spectrum disorders.

sublevels.name: Schizophrenia
sublevels.description: Schizophrenia is a severe and debilitating psychiatric disorder that involves psychotic symptoms such as hallucinations and delusions, accompanied with regressive behaviour.

sublevels.name: Depression
sublevels.description: Depression refers to a state of low mood that can be accompanied with loss of interest in activities that the individual normally perceived as pleasurable, altered appetite and sleep/wake balance. Its severe form, major depression is classified as a mood disorder.

sublevels.name: Anxiety
sublevels.description: Anxiety is characterized by excessive uneasiness, apprehension or dread. It can be generalized or be directed towards specific, usually imagined or exaggerated threat.

sublevels.name: Bipolar Disorder
sublevels.description: Bipolar disorder is a mood disorder that includes at least one manic episode, characterized by elevated or agitated mood and often reduced need for sleep accompanied by episodes of major depression.

sublevels.name: Neurology
sublevels.description: Neurology is a medical specialty that is concerned with the study of structure, function and disorders of the nervous system.

sublevels.name: Neurological Disorders
sublevels.description: Neurological disorders are disorders that affect the central nervous system or the peripheral nervous systems and can impair the brain, spinal cord, peripheral nerve or neuromuscular function.

sublevels.name: Epilepsy
sublevels.description: Epilepsy refers to a group of neurological disorders of varying aetiology, characterized by recurrent brain dysfunction that result from sudden excessive and disordered neuronal discharge. These episodes can manifest as epileptic seizures, but they can also occur with subtle or no behavioural signs.

sublevels.name: Dementia
sublevels.description: Dementia is a syndrome that involves severe loss of cognitive abilities as a result of disease or injury. Dementia caused by traumatic brain injury is often static, whereas dementia caused by neurodegenerative disorders, such as Alzheimer's disease, is usually progressive and can eventually be fatal.

sublevels.name: Sleep Disorders
sublevels.description: Sleep disorders are a group of conditions in which the normal sleep pattern or sleep behaviours are disturbed. Primary sleep disorders include insomnia, hypersomnia, obstructive sleep apnoea and parasomnias (abnormal sleep behaviours, such as sleepwalking and rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder).

sublevels.name: Parkinson's Disease
sublevels.description: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder, which is characterized by motor symptoms such as tremor, rigidity, slowness of movement and problems with gait. Motor symptoms are often accompanied with fatigue, depression, pain and cognitive problems.

sublevels.name: Movement Disorders
sublevels.description: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder, which is characterized by motor symptoms such as tremor, rigidity, slowness of movement and problems with gait. Motor symptoms are often accompanied with fatigue, depression, pain and cognitive problems.

sublevels.name: Parkinson's Disease
sublevels.description: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder, which is characterized by motor symptoms such as tremor, rigidity, slowness of movement and problems with gait. Motor symptoms are often accompanied with fatigue, depression, pain and cognitive problems.

sublevels.name: Neurodegeneration
sublevels.description: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder, which is characterized by motor symptoms such as tremor, rigidity, slowness of movement and problems with gait. Motor symptoms are often accompanied with fatigue, depression, pain and cognitive problems.

sublevels.name: Parkinson's Disease
sublevels.description: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder, which is characterized by motor symptoms such as tremor, rigidity, slowness of movement and problems with gait. Motor symptoms are often accompanied with fatigue, depression, pain and cognitive problems.

sublevels.name: Diagnosis
sublevels.description: Medical and clinical diagnostics is the practice of detecting, identifying and monitoring a disease or medical disorder..Diagnosis is the procedure through which the nature of a phenomenon, such as a disease, is determined. The term diagnosis also refers to the opinion reached though this process. Assessment can be made though tests, such as physical examination and laboratory techniques and procedures, to find signs and symptoms of a disease.

sublevels.name: Biomarkers
sublevels.description: A biomarker is a biological characteristic that is objectively measured and evaluated as an indicator of normal biological or pathological processes, or a response to a therapeutic intervention. Examples include patterns of gene expression, levels of a particular protein in body fluids, or changes in electrical activity in the brain.

sublevels.name: Pathology
sublevels.description: Pathology is the precise study of the causes and consequences of a disease. The two major components of pathology are anatomical studies of structure and function at levels ranging from the whole organism to the subcellular level, and laboratory techniques and procedures to analyse bodily fluids.

sublevels.name: Endocrinology
sublevels.description: Endocrinology is the branch of medicine that deals with disorders of the endocrine system.

sublevels.name: Endocrine System and Metabolic Diseases
sublevels.description: Diabetes describes a group of metabolic diseases characterized by high blood sugar levels. Diabetes can be caused by the pancreas not producing insulin (type 1 diabetes) or by insulin resistance (cells do not respond to insulin; type 2 diabetes).

sublevels.name: Diabetes
sublevels.description: Diabetes describes a group of metabolic diseases characterized by high blood sugar levels. Diabetes can be caused by the pancreas not producing insulin (type 1 diabetes) or by insulin resistance (cells do not respond to insulin; type 2 diabetes).

sublevels.name: Internal Medicine
sublevels.description: Internal medicine or general internal medicine is the medical specialty dealing with the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of internal diseases.

sublevels.name: Clinical Genetics
sublevels.description: Clinical genetics involves the study, counselling and treatment of individuals and families with heritable disorders and disease predisposition. Diagnostic tools include standard ontologies for describing dysmorphology and traits, pedigree analysis, disease locus mapping by linkage or homozygosity, karyotyping, genome sequencing and genotyping.

sublevels.name: Gene Therapy
sublevels.description: Gene therapy involves the introduction of new genes into cells, to restore or add gene expression, for the purpose of treating disease. Most commonly a mutated gene is replaced with DNA encoding a functional copy. Alternatively DNA encoding a therapeutic protein drug may be introduced.

sublevels.name: Therapeutics
sublevels.description: Therapeutics are treatments used to alleviate or prevent a particular disease. Examples of therapeutics include drug therapy, medical devices, nutrition therapy and stem-cell therapies. Therapeutics can be used in patients with active disease - to treat the disease itself or its signs and symptoms -, in preventive medicine, or as palliative care.

sublevels.name: Gene Therapy
sublevels.description: Gene therapy involves the introduction of new genes into cells, to restore or add gene expression, for the purpose of treating disease. Most commonly a mutated gene is replaced with DNA encoding a functional copy. Alternatively DNA encoding a therapeutic protein drug may be introduced.

sublevels.name: Drug Therapy
sublevels.description: Drug therapy (or pharmacotherapy) involves the administration of drugs to treat or prevent disease. In some cases - often in the treatment of disease such as cancer, HIV infection and diabetes - multiple drugs with different active ingredients may be administered, which is known as combination therapy.

sublevels.name: Immunotherapy
sublevels.description: Immunotherapy is the treatment of disease by inducing, enhancing or suppressing an immune response. Activation immunotherapies induce or amplify an immune response and are used in vaccines and as cancer immunotherapies. Suppression immunotherapies reduce or suppress an immune response and are used to prevent graft rejection and treat autoimmunity and allergy.

sublevels.name: Biological Therapy
sublevels.description: Biological therapy is a type of therapeutic treatment. The agents used for biological therapy are designed to specifically target a biological phenomenon, gene, protein, or group of genes or proteins thought to be involved in the disease.

sublevels.name: Palliative Care
sublevels.description: Palliative care is the set of medical interventions to alleviate symptoms, most frequently pain, associated with a medical condition. The main goal of palliative care is to reduce and prevent patient suffering. Unlike therapeutics, palliative care does not aim to cure the underlying disease. Palliative care is an interdisciplinary medical caregiving  approach that improves the quality of life of patients and their families facing the problems associated with life-threatening illness, through the prevention and relief of suffering by means of early identification and impeccable assessment and treatment of pain and other problems, physical, psychosocial, and spiritual.

sublevels.name: Dentistry
sublevels.description: is the study, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of diseases, disorders, and conditions of the oral cavity, commonly in the dentition, the oral mucosa, and adjacent and related structures and tissues.

sublevels.name: Dental Radiology
sublevels.description: Dental radiology is a branch of dentistry concerned with the use of radiant energy (such as X-rays and other high-energy radiation) or radioactive material in the diagnosis and treatment of dental and oral diseases. Dental radiographs assist in detecting hidden painful pathology, estimating the severity of dental conditions, assessing treatment options, providing intraoperative guidance, and also serve to monitor success of prior treatments.

sublevels.name: Dental Treatments
sublevels.description: Oral and maxillofacial surgery is a surgical specialty focusing on reconstructive surgery of the face, facial trauma surgery, the oral cavity, head and neck, mouth, and jaws, as well as facial cosmetic surgery/facial plastic surgery including cleft lip and cleft palate surgery.

sublevels.name: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
sublevels.description: Oral and maxillofacial surgery is a surgical specialty focusing on reconstructive surgery of the face, facial trauma surgery, the oral cavity, head and neck, mouth, and jaws, as well as facial cosmetic surgery/facial plastic surgery including cleft lip and cleft palate surgery.

sublevels.name: Otorhinolaryngology
sublevels.description: Otorhinolaryngology is a medical specialty focusing on the diagnosis, evaluation and management of diseases of head and neck and principally the ears, nose and throat.

sublevels.name: Pediatrics
sublevels.description: Paediatrics is a medical discipline focused on individuals from birth to the end of adolescence. The care of paediatric patients is different to that of adults, as many drugs are processed differently in these two groups. Growth and development are also more important in paediatric patients than in adults.

sublevels.name: Adolescent Medicine
sublevels.description: Adolescent Medicine is a specialized field of healthcare focused on the physical, mental, and emotional well-being of individuals during the adolescent years (typically ages 10-19) and young adulthood, encompassing a wide range of health concerns and promoting healthy transitions into adulthood.

sublevels.name: Nephrology
sublevels.description: Nephrology is specialty of medicine concerned with kidney physiology, kidney disease, the treatment of kidney problems and renal replacement therapy. Systemic conditions that affect the kidneys (e.g. diabetes and autoimmune disease) and systemic problems that occur as a result of kidney problems (e.g. metabolic bone disease and hypertension) are also studied in nephrology.

sublevels.name: Gastroenterology
sublevels.description: Gastroenterology is a medical specialty focusing on the structure, function, pathology and disorders of the gastrointestinal system.

sublevels.name: Psychiatry
sublevels.description: The study and treatment of mental illness, emotional disturbance, and abnormal behaviour.

sublevels.name: Psychopharmacology
sublevels.description: Psychopharmacology is the scientific study of the effects drugs have on mood, sensation, thinking, and behavior. It is distinguished from neuropsychopharmacology, which emphasizes the correlation between drug-induced changes in the functioning of cells in the nervous system and changes in consciousness and behavior.

sublevels.name: Behavioral Medicine
sublevels.description: Behavioral Medicine is a multidisciplinary field that combines principles and knowledge from psychology, medicine, and behavioral sciences to understand the complex relationship between behavior and health. It focuses on the application of behavioral and psychological principles to prevent and treat illness, promote health, and enhance well-being. Behavioral Medicine recognizes that human behavior plays a crucial role in the development, maintenance, and treatment of various physical and mental health conditions. It integrates psychological interventions, behavior change strategies, and lifestyle modifications with medical treatments to optimize health outcomes and improve quality of life.

sublevels.name: Child and Adolescence Psychiatry
sublevels.description: A branch of psychiatry that focuses on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of mental disorders in children, adolescents, and their families.

sublevels.name: Prognosis
sublevels.description: Prognosis is the prediction of the probable outcome of an individual's current medical condition. A prognosis is made on the basis of the normal course of a disease, the individual's physical and psychological condition, and additional factors such as therapeutic approach.

sublevels.name: Orthopaedics
sublevels.description: Orthopaedics is a medical specialty concerned with the prevention and treatment of disorders of the musculoskeletal system by use of surgical and non-surgical methods.

sublevels.name: Surgical Orthopedics
sublevels.description: Orthopedic surgery, also known as orthopedics, is a branch of surgery dealing with the musculoskeletal system. Orthopedic surgeons use various surgical and non-surgical procedures such a hip replacement surgery and spinal fusion to treat all problems relating to one's bones and joints.

sublevels.name: Oncology
sublevels.description: Oncology is the branch of medicine that deals with the diagnosis and treatment of cancer. It includes medical oncology (the use of chemotherapy, hormone therapy, and other drugs to treat cancer), radiation oncology (the use of radiation therapy to treat cancer), and surgical oncology (the use of surgery and other procedures to treat cancer).

sublevels.name: Emergency Medicine
sublevels.description: Emergency medicine, also known as accident and emergency medicine, is the medical specialty concerned with the care of illnesses or injuries requiring immediate medical attention.  Emergency physicians’ primary responsibility is to initiate resuscitation and stabilization and to start investigations and interventions to diagnose and treat illnesses in the acute phase; they generally practise in hospital emergency departments, pre-hospital settings via emergency medical services, and intensive care units, but may also work in primary care settings such as urgent care clinics. Sub-specializations of emergency medicine include disaster medicine, medical toxicology, ultrasonography, critical care medicine, hyperbaric medicine, sports medicine, palliative care, or aerospace medicine.

sublevels.name: Trauma Psychology
sublevels.description: Trauma is a physiological wound, which can be penetrating or nonpenetrating, caused directly or indirectly by external physical force.

sublevels.name: Gynecology
sublevels.description: Is the branch of medicine that deals with the diseases and routine physical care of the reproductive system of women

sublevels.name: Obstetrics
sublevels.description: The branch of medical science that deals with problems and difficulties of pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period. To be distinguished from midwifery which emphasizes the normalcy of pregnancy while acknowledging the vulnerability associated with the reproductive process.

sublevels.name: Anesthesiology
sublevels.description: Anesthesiology is the medical speciality concerned with the total perioperative care of patients before, during and after surgery. It encompasses anesthesia, intensive care medicine, critical emergency medicine, and pain medicine.

sublevels.name: Sports Medicine
sublevels.description: Sports Medicine is a subfield of medicine dealing with physical fitness and the treatment and prevention of injuries in sports and exercise. Although its origins lie in the clinical treatment of athletes, Sports Medicine traditionally also encompasses matters of performance physiology and methods of training control.

sublevels.name: Physiotherapy
sublevels.description: Physiotherapy is a health profession as well as a treatment method that focuses on the science of movement and helps people to restore, maintain and maximize their physical strength, function, motion and overall well-being by addressing the underlying physical issues. Physiotherapy aims at preventing injury and disability, managing acute and chronic conditions, Improving and maintaining optimal physical performance, Rehabilitating injury and the effects of disease or disability and Educating patients to prevent re-occurrence of an injury. For these purposes, Physiotherapy applies a variety of techniques, such as manual manipulation, electrical nerve stimulation, acupuncture, functional testing or provision of assistive, adaptive, supportive and protective devices and equipment.

sublevels.name: Urology
sublevels.description: Urology is a part of health care that deals with diseases of the male and female urinary tract (kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra). It also deals with the male organs that are able to make babies (penis, testes, scrotum, prostate, etc.).

sublevels.name: Urological Surgery
sublevels.description: Urology (from Greek ????? ouron "urine" and -????? -logia "study of"), also known as genitourinary surgery, is the branch of medicine that focuses on surgical and medical diseases of the urinary-tract system and the reproductive organs.

sublevels.name: Andrology
sublevels.description: The branch of medicine concerned with the anatomy, functions, and disorders (such as infertility or impotence) of the male reproductive system

sublevels.name: Cardiology
sublevels.description: Cardiology is a medical specialty that is concerned with the structure and function of the heart and vasculature, and the diagnosis and treatment of patients with cardiovascular diseases.

sublevels.name: Cardiovascular Physiology
sublevels.description: Cardiovascular biology is the study of the mechanisms of cardiovascular physiology and pathophysiology.

sublevels.name: Angiogenesis
sublevels.description: Angiogenesis is the formation and remodelling of new blood vessels from pre?existing ones. It occurs normally in processes such as wound healing and embryonic development, but is also active in diseases such as tumour growth and diabetic eye disease.

sublevels.name: Cardiac Surgery
sublevels.description: Cardiac surgery is surgery on the heart and the large blood vessels in the chest performed by cardiac surgeons and the perioperative management of these patients

sublevels.name: Rheumatology
sublevels.description: Rheumatology is a subspecialty of internal medicine focusing on the diagnosis, treatment and medical management of patients with rheumatic diseases that affect the musculoskeletal system.

sublevels.name: Osteoimmunology
sublevels.description: Osteoimmunology is the study of how the immune and skeletal systems interact.

sublevels.name: Allergology
sublevels.description: Study of allergy and hypersensitivity of the immune system.

sublevels.name: Dermatology
sublevels.description: The diagnosis, treatment and management of skin, hair and nail diseases and conditions, including aesthetic procedures

sublevels.name: Tropical Medicine
sublevels.description: Tropical medicine is a medical science applied to diseases that occur primarily in countries with tropical or subtropical climates. Tropical medicine is a critical part of global health, particularly because it encompasses preventable diseases that affect impoverished communities and regions.

sublevels.name: Primary Care Medicine
sublevels.description: Primary care is the day-to-day healthcare given by a health care provider. It is the initial point of contact between a patient and the healthcare system that provides individuals with access to the information and resources they need for optimal health outcomes.

sublevels.name: Ophthalmology
sublevels.description: Ophthalmology is a surgical subspecialty within medicine that deals with the diagnosis and treatment of eye disorders.

sublevels.name: Geriatrics
sublevels.description: Geriatrics is a medical discipline focused on elderly individuals. Issues such as physical mobility and stability, memory loss, and neurodegenerative diseases are central to geriatric medicine. It aims to promote health by preventing and treating diseases and disabilities in older adults.

sublevels.name: Phlebology
sublevels.description: The term phlebology refers to the study of disorders that affect the veins (Greek: phlebos = vein, blood vessel). Based on a survey of the World Health Organization (WHO), vein problems rank among the most common diseases worldwide. Venous leg disorders are some of the earliest documented illnesses suffered by mankind.

sublevels.name: Proctology
sublevels.description: Proctology is the medical specialty that focuses on diseases of the colon, rectum and anus.

sublevels.name: Colorectal Surgery
sublevels.description: Colorectal surgery is the management of conditions of the colon, rectum, and anus.

sublevels.name: General Practice and Family Medicine
sublevels.description: General practice / family medicine is defined as the medical specialty that manages common and long-term illnesses in children and adults, focusing on overall health and well-being.

sublevels.name: Medical Education
sublevels.description: Medical education is education related to the practice of being a medical practitioner, including the initial training to become a physician (i.e., medical school and internship) and additional training thereafter (e.g., residency, fellowship, and continuing medical education).  Medical education and training varies considerably across the world. Various teaching methodologies have been used in medical education, which is an active area of educational research.

sublevels.name: Occupational Medicine
sublevels.description: Occupational medicine is the branch of medicine which is concerned with the maintenance of health in the workplace, including prevention and treatment of diseases and injuries, with secondary objectives of maintaining and increasing productivity and social adjustment in the workplace. It is the branch of clinical medicine active in the field of occupational health and safety. OM specialists work to ensure that the highest standards of occupational health and safety are achieved and maintained in the workplace, and manage illness, injury, and disability related to the workplace.

sublevels.name: Angiology
sublevels.description: Angiology studies the circulatory and lymphatic system of the human body, i.e., arteries, veins and lymphatic vessels. It also deals with the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of vascular and blood vessel related diseases.

sublevels.name: History of Medicine
sublevels.description: The history of medicine is the study and documentation of the evolution of medical treatments, practices, and knowledge over time.

sublevels.name: Complementary and Alternative Medicine
sublevels.description: Complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) is a term for medical products and practices that are not part of standard medical care. Alternative medicine is any practice that aims to achieve the healing effects of medicine despite lacking biological plausibility, testability, repeatability or evidence of effectiveness.

sublevels.name: Acupuncture
sublevels.description: Acupuncture is a form of alternative medicine and a component of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in which thin needles are inserted into the body. Acupuncture is a pseudoscience the theories and practices of TCM are not based on scientific knowledge, and it has been characterized as quackery.

sublevels.name: Intensive Care Medicine
sublevels.description: Intensive Care Medicine, also called Critical Care medicine, is a medical specialty that deals with seriously or critically ill patients who have, are at risk of, or are recovering from conditions that may be life-threatening.

sublevels.name: Psychosomatic Medicine
sublevels.description: Psychosomatic medicine is an interdisciplinary medical field exploring the relationships among social, psychological, and behavioral factors on bodily processes and quality of life in humans and animals.

sublevels.name: Pain Medicine
sublevels.description: Pain management is an aspect of medicine and health care involving relief of pain in various dimensions, from acute and simple to chronic and challenging.

sublevels.name: Hematology
sublevels.description: Hematology is the science or study of blood, blood-forming organs and blood diseases.

sublevels.name: Pneumology
sublevels.description: Pulmonology is a medical speciality that deals with diseases involving the respiratory tract.

sublevels.name: Medical Toxicology
sublevels.description: Medical toxicology is a branch of toxicology that focuses on the diagnosis, management and prevention of adverse health effects resulting from medications or from exposure to toxic chemical or biological agents. Medical toxicologists assess and treat poisoning and substance abuse, for example.

sublevels.name: Reproductive Medicine
sublevels.description: The branch of medicine that specializes in fertility preservation, diagnosing and treating infertility, and other reproductive problems. Reproductive medicine also deals with issues related to puberty, menopause, and contraception (birth control)

sublevels.name: Biomedical Devices and Instrumentation
sublevels.description: Biomedical devices and instrumentation refer to the tools, equipment, and systems used in the field of biomedical engineering and healthcare to diagnose, monitor, treat, or assist in the management of medical conditions. These devices and instruments are designed to interface with biological systems, provide accurate measurements, deliver therapeutic interventions, or aid in the analysis of biological samples.

sublevels.name: Medical Imaging
sublevels.description: Medical imaging is the technique and process of imaging the interior of a body for clinical analysis and medical intervention, as well as visual representation of the function of some organs or tissues (physiology). Medical imaging seeks to reveal internal structures hidden by the skin and bones, as well as to diagnose and treat disease. Medical imaging also establishes a database of normal anatomy and physiology to make it possible to identify abnormalities.  (Although imaging of removed organs and tissues can be performed for medical reasons, such procedures are usually considered part of pathology instead of medical imaging.)

sublevels.name: Radiography
sublevels.description: Radiography is the use of X-rays or gamma rays to examine non-uniformly composed material; images are recorded on a sensitized surface, such as photographic film or a digital detector. Medical radiography includes examination of any part of the body for diagnostic purposes, such as detecting fractures or a bowel obstruction.

sublevels.name: Tomography
sublevels.description: Tomography is a technique whereby a subject is imaged in 'slices' or sections. Typically the imaging modality is X-ray radiography, and the slices can be viewed separately or in combination. Except for health sciences and medicine the method is also used in other areas of science, such as archaeology, biology, atmospheric science, geophysics, oceanography, plasma physics, materials science and astrophysics.

sublevels.name: Nuclear Medicine
sublevels.description: Nuclear medicine is a specialized area of radiology that uses very small amounts of radioactive materials, or radiopharmaceuticals, to examine organ function and structure. Nuclear medicine imaging is a combination of many different disciplines. These include chemistry, physics, mathematics, computer technology, and medicine. This branch of radiology is often used to help diagnose and treat abnormalities very early in the progression of a disease, such as thyroid cancer.

sublevels.name: Forensic Medicine
sublevels.description: The branch of medicine dealing with the application of medical knowledge to establish facts in civil or criminal legal cases, such as an investigation into the cause and time of a suspicious death.

sublevels.name: Metabolic Disease
sublevels.description: Metabolic disorders occur when the body's usual metabolic processes are disrupted. These diseases can be congenital or acquired, for example, diabetes and phenylketonuria.

sublevels.name: Pathology
sublevels.description: Pathology is the precise study of the causes and consequences of a disease. The two major components of pathology are anatomical studies of structure and function at levels ranging from the whole organism to the subcellular level, and laboratory techniques and procedures to analyse bodily fluids.

sublevels.name: Medical and Health Technologies
sublevels.description: Health technology is defined as the "application of organized knowledge and skills in the form of devices, medicines, vaccines, procedures, and systems developed to solve a health problem and improve quality of lives". This includes pharmaceuticals, devices, procedures, and organizational systems used in the healthcare industry, as well as any technology, including medical devices, IT systems, algorithms, artificial intelligence (AI), cloud and blockchain, designed to support healthcare organizations.

sublevels.name: e-Health
sublevels.description: eHealth describes healthcare services which are supported by digital processes, communication or technology such as electronic prescribing, Telehealth, or Electronic Health Records.

sublevels.name: Rehabilitation Robotics
sublevels.description: Rehabilitation robotics is a field of research dedicated to understanding and augmenting rehabilitation through the application of robotic devices.

sublevels.name: Palliative Care
sublevels.description: Palliative care is the set of medical interventions to alleviate symptoms, most frequently pain, associated with a medical condition. The main goal of palliative care is to reduce and prevent patient suffering. Unlike therapeutics, palliative care does not aim to cure the underlying disease. Palliative care is an interdisciplinary medical caregiving  approach that improves the quality of life of patients and their families facing the problems associated with life-threatening illness, through the prevention and relief of suffering by means of early identification and impeccable assessment and treatment of pain and other problems, physical, psychosocial, and spiritual.

sublevels.name: Radiology
sublevels.description: Radiology, Medical Imaging or Diagnostic Radiology: comprises different imaging modalities and processes to image human body for diagnostic and treatment purposes. It is also used to follow the course of a disease already diagnosed and/or treated.

sublevels.name: Bone Scintigraphy
sublevels.description: Bone Scintigraphy, Bone Imaging or Bone Scan is a study that uses various quantitative and qualitative methods to visually assess the composition, structure and metabolism of skeletal bone.

sublevels.name: Interventional Radiology
sublevels.description: Interventional radiology (IR) is a medical sub-specialty of radiology utilizing minimally-invasive image-guided procedures to diagnose and treat diseases in nearly every organ system. These procedures have less risk, less pain and less recovery time in comparison to open surgery. IR refers to a range of techniques which rely on the use radiological image guidance (X-ray fluoroscopy, ultrasound, computed tomography [CT] or magnetic resonance imaging [MRI]) to precisely target therapy.

sublevels.name: Cardiography
sublevels.description: Cardiography or Cardiac Imaging

sublevels.name: Radiation Oncology
sublevels.description: Radiotherapy, or radiation therapy, is the clinical use of high energy rays (ionizing radiation) to induce DNA damage in all exposed cells to ultimately kill cancer cells or prevent cancer growth. Radiotherapy may be used to eradicate some cancers, to reduce recurrence or as palliative treatment.

sublevels.name: Dental Radiology
sublevels.description: Dental radiology is a branch of dentistry concerned with the use of radiant energy (such as X-rays and other high-energy radiation) or radioactive material in the diagnosis and treatment of dental and oral diseases. Dental radiographs assist in detecting hidden painful pathology, estimating the severity of dental conditions, assessing treatment options, providing intraoperative guidance, and also serve to monitor success of prior treatments.

sublevels.name: Endoscopy
sublevels.description: Endoscopy is an optical imaging technique that uses a rigid or flexible small diameter light guide inserted into an organ, cavity or tissue for light delivery and collection.

sublevels.name: Radiography
sublevels.description: Radiography is the use of X-rays or gamma rays to examine non-uniformly composed material; images are recorded on a sensitized surface, such as photographic film or a digital detector. Medical radiography includes examination of any part of the body for diagnostic purposes, such as detecting fractures or a bowel obstruction.

sublevels.name: Tomography
sublevels.description: Tomography is a technique whereby a subject is imaged in 'slices' or sections. Typically the imaging modality is X-ray radiography, and the slices can be viewed separately or in combination. Except for health sciences and medicine the method is also used in other areas of science, such as archaeology, biology, atmospheric science, geophysics, oceanography, plasma physics, materials science and astrophysics.

sublevels.name: Nuclear Medicine
sublevels.description: Nuclear medicine is a specialized area of radiology that uses very small amounts of radioactive materials, or radiopharmaceuticals, to examine organ function and structure. Nuclear medicine imaging is a combination of many different disciplines. These include chemistry, physics, mathematics, computer technology, and medicine. This branch of radiology is often used to help diagnose and treat abnormalities very early in the progression of a disease, such as thyroid cancer.

sublevels.name: Public Health
sublevels.description: Public health is the medical discipline concerned with the prevention and control of disease through population surveillance and the promotion of healthy behaviours. Strategies used to promote public health include patient education, the administration of vaccines, and other components of preventive medicine.

sublevels.name: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention
sublevels.description: Health promotion enables people to increase control over their own health. It covers a wide range of social and environmental interventions that are designed to benefit and protect individual people’s health and quality of life by addressing and preventing the root causes of ill health, not just focusing on treatment and cure. 1. Good governance for health; 2. Health literacy; 3. Healthy cities Disease prevention focuses on specific efforts aimed at reducing the development and severity of chronic diseases and other morbidities.

sublevels.name: Drug Safety and Pharmacovigilance
sublevels.description: Pharmacovigilance is the science and activities relating to the detection, assessment, understanding and prevention of adverse effects or any other medicine/vaccine related problem.

sublevels.name: Drug Regulation
sublevels.description: Drug regulation is the control of drug use by international agreement and/or by regulatory authorities such as the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the European Medicines Agency (EMA) and the Japanese Pharmaceutical and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA). This includes regulations concerned with the development, approval, manufacturing and marketing of drugs.

sublevels.name: Health Administration
sublevels.description: Health administration, healthcare administration, healthcare management or hospital management is the field relating to leadership, management, and administration of public health systems, health care systems, hospitals, and hospital networks in all the primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors.

sublevels.name: Premedical Education
sublevels.description: Pre-medical (often referred to as pre-med) is an educational track that undergraduate students pursue prior to becoming medical students. It involves activities that prepare a student for medical school, such as pre-med coursework, volunteer activities, clinical experience, research, and the application process.

sublevels.name: Health Policy and Systems Research
sublevels.description: Health policy and systems research (HPSR) is an interdisciplinary field that studies how societies organize to achieve their health goals, focusing on the policies, organizations, people, and interactions that make up a health system.

sublevels.name: Health Policy
sublevels.description: Health policy is the set of decisions and plans, developed by governmental or nongovernmental agencies, designed to promote specific health-care objectives. Policies can be directed at individuals, physicians, pharmaceutical companies, or health-care systems. Examples include tobacco control policies and those designed to promote equal opportunites to access care.

sublevels.name: Health Economics
sublevels.description: Health economics is a branch of economics concerned with issues related to efficiency, effectiveness, value and behavior in the production and consumption of health and healthcare.

sublevels.name: Biomedical Research
sublevels.description: Medical research involves research in a wide range of fields, such as biology, chemistry, pharmacology and toxicology with the goal of developing new medicines or medical procedures or improving the application of those already available. It can be viewed as encompassing preclinical research (for example, in cellular systems and animal models) and clinical research (for example, clinical trials).

sublevels.name: Genetics Research
sublevels.description: Genetics research is the scientific discipline concerned with the study of the role of genes in traits such as the development of disease. It has a key role in identifying potential targets for therapeutic intervention and also in understanding genetically based variations in response to therapeutic interventions.

sublevels.name: Stem Cell Biology
sublevels.description: Stem-cell research or Stem Cell Biology is the area of research that studies the properties of stem cells and their potential use in regenerative medicine. As stem cells are the source of all tissues and have the potential to develop into different cell types, understanding their properties helps in our understanding of the healthy and diseased body's development and homeostasis.

sublevels.name: Cancer Stem Cells
sublevels.description: Cancer stem cells are rare immortal cells within a tumour that can both self-renew by dividing and give rise to many cell types that constitute the tumour, and can therefore form tumours. Such cells have been found in various types of human tumours and might be attractive targets for cancer treatment.

sublevels.name: Pathogenesis
sublevels.description: Pathogenesis is the term that is used to describe the origin and development of a disease.

sublevels.name: Infection
sublevels.description: Infectious diseases are caused by pathogenic microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, parasites or fungi, that infect a host organism and can be spread, directly or indirectly, from one organism to another. An infectiologist manages nosocomial (healthcare-acquired) or community-acquired infections.

sublevels.name: Infectious Diseases
sublevels.description: Infectious diseases are caused by pathogenic microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, parasites or fungi, that infect a host organism and can be spread, directly or indirectly, from one organism to another. An infectiologist manages nosocomial (healthcare-acquired) or community-acquired infections.

sublevels.name: Sexually Transmitted Diseases
sublevels.description: Sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) are infections transmitted through sexual contact, caused by bacteria, viruses, or parasites, and include conditions such as chlamydia, gonorrhea, and HIV/AIDS.

sublevels.name: Clinical Research
sublevels.description: Clinical research is the study of health and illness in people. Clinical research is a branch of healthcare science that determines the safety and effectiveness of medications, devices, diagnostic products and treatment regimens intended for human use.

sublevels.name: Clinical Trials
sublevels.description: Biostatistics is the application of statistical methods in studies in life and health sciences, and encompasses the design of experiments, the collection of data from them, and the analysis and interpretation of data. The data come from a wide range of sources, including genomic studies, experiments with cells and organisms, and clinical trials.

sublevels.name: Biostatistics
sublevels.description: Biostatistics is the application of statistical methods in studies in life and health sciences, and encompasses the design of experiments, the collection of data from them, and the analysis and interpretation of data. The data come from a wide range of sources, including genomic studies, experiments with cells and organisms, and clinical trials.

sublevels.name: Pharmacology
sublevels.description: Pharmacology is a branch of biomedical science, encompassing clinical pharmacology, that is concerned with the effects of drugs/pharmaceuticals and other xenobiotics on living systems, as well as their development and chemical properties.

sublevels.name: Pharmaceutics
sublevels.description: Pharmaceutics is the scientific discipline concerned with the process of creating the dosage form (such as a pill for oral administration or a powder for intravenous injection) of a therapeutic that is to be used by patients. It encompasses drug formulation and manufacturing.

sublevels.name: Vaccines
sublevels.description: Vaccines are a clinical product that is composed of live or dead material from an infectious agent – bacterium, virus, fungus or parasite – that elicit protective immunity against the pathogen when administered. These substances are used to prevent the spread of infectious diseases.

sublevels.name: Drug Development
sublevels.description: Drug development describes the process of developing a new drug that effectively targets a specific weakness in a cell. This process involves specific pre-clinical development and testing, followed by trials in humans to determine the efficacy of the drug.

sublevels.name: Small Molecules
sublevels.description: Chemical tools are small molecules used as probes of a chemical or biological process. Studying the effects of chemical tools on a system can lead to new insight into the molecular target of the small molecule and the pathways it acts in. Chemical probes with defined targets can be attractive as drugs in clinical pharmacology..Small molecules are low molecular weight molecules that include lipids, monosaccharides, second messengers, other natural products and metabolites, as well as drugs and other xenobiotics. They are distinct from macromolecules such as proteins. In chemical biology, this term also covers metal ions and in this discipline small molecules may play the role of a chemical tool.

sublevels.name: Epidemiology
sublevels.description: Epidemiology is a field of medicine that studies the incidence, causes and effects of diseases in populations, and patterns within these. It has a key role in protecting public health and can provide valuable information for developing new medicines, such as revealing risk factors for a particular disease.

sublevels.name: Preclinical Research
sublevels.description: Preclinical research involves the evaluation of potential therapeutic interventions in cells and animals. Candidates for entry into clinical trials can then be selected based on their effectiveness and safety in disease models. All drugs require data from various toxicological preclinical studies to support their potential safety in humans before clinical trials can begin.

sublevels.name: Medical Microbiology
sublevels.description: Pathological processes in the human body caused by viruses, bacteria and parasites.

sublevels.name: Veterinary Microbiology
sublevels.description: Veterinary Microbiology is the study of the agents responsible for causing animal infections: bacteria, viruses, fungi or parasites.

sublevels.name: Infectious Diseases
sublevels.description: Infectious diseases are caused by pathogenic microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, parasites or fungi, that infect a host organism and can be spread, directly or indirectly, from one organism to another. An infectiologist manages nosocomial (healthcare-acquired) or community-acquired infections.

sublevels.name: Sexually Transmitted Diseases
sublevels.description: Sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) are infections transmitted through sexual contact, caused by bacteria, viruses, or parasites, and include conditions such as chlamydia, gonorrhea, and HIV/AIDS.

sublevels.name: Antimicrobials
sublevels.description: Antibiotics are substances that inhibit the growth of bacteria. They work by killing bacteria or preventing their reproduction, and may be synthesized chemically or by naturally-occurring or engineered organisms.

sublevels.name: Antibiotics
sublevels.description: Antibiotics are substances that inhibit the growth of bacteria. They work by killing bacteria or preventing their reproduction, and may be synthesized chemically or by naturally-occurring or engineered organisms.

sublevels.name: Toxicology
sublevels.description: Toxicology is a scientific discipline, overlapping with biology, chemistry, pharmacology, and medicine, that involves the study of the adverse effects of chemical substances on living organisms and the practice of diagnosing and treating exposures to toxins and toxicants.

sublevels.name: Medical Biochemistry
sublevels.description: Medical Biochemistry is the application of biochemical principles to the understanding, diagnosis, and treatment of human diseases. It focuses on the biochemical basis of pathology, clinical biomarkers, metabolic disorders, molecular diagnostics, and therapeutic interventions relevant to human health. The field supports clinical decision?making through biochemical diagnostics, laboratory testing, and the interpretation of molecular and metabolic abnormalities in patients.

sublevels.name: Translational Research
sublevels.description: Translational research involves the application of knowledge gained through basic research to studies that could support the development of new products. For example, translational research in the field of medicine may involve using knowledge of the biology of a disease to identify and evaluate chemical compounds in disease models, with a view to selecting potential candidate drugs to advance into clinical trials.

sublevels.name: Biomarkers
sublevels.description: A biomarker is a biological characteristic that is objectively measured and evaluated as an indicator of normal biological or pathological processes, or a response to a therapeutic intervention. Examples include patterns of gene expression, levels of a particular protein in body fluids, or changes in electrical activity in the brain.

sublevels.name: Surgery
sublevels.description: Surgery is a procedure in which incision and physical manipulation are used to treat a patient with an injury or a disease. The patient's tissues are cut during this technique to permit the manipulation of tissues that are otherwise inaccessible.

sublevels.name: Transplantation
sublevels.description: Transplantation is the procedure of transferring a tissue or organ from one individual to another or from one site to another within a single individual. The transplanted tissue or organ replaces damaged or absent tissue, and is functional in the recipient.

sublevels.name: Minimally Invasive Surgery
sublevels.description: Minimally invasive procedures (also known as minimally invasive surgeries) encompass surgical techniques that limit the size of incisions needed, thereby reducing wound healing time, associated pain, and risk of infection.

sublevels.name: Neurosurgery
sublevels.description: Neurosurgery is a surgical procedure that uses invasive techniques to diagnose, investigate and/or treat a neurological disorder, disease or injury. For example, to remove a brain tumour or insert a deep brain stimulation device.

sublevels.name: Pediatric Surgery
sublevels.description: Pediatric surgery is a subspecialty of surgery involving the surgery of fetuses, infants, children, adolescents, and young adults.

sublevels.name: Vascular Surgery
sublevels.description: Vascular surgery refers to open surgeries and minimally-invasive procedures that treat a range of blood vessel problems. These include aortic aneurysms, peripheral artery disease, carotid artery disease and chronic venous insufficiency.

sublevels.name: General Surgery
sublevels.description: General surgery is a surgical specialty that focuses on alimentary canal and abdominal contents including the esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, liver, pancreas, gallbladder, appendix and bile ducts, and often the thyroid gland. They also deal with diseases involving the skin, breast, soft tissue, trauma, peripheral artery disease and hernias and perform endoscopic as such as gastroscopy, colonoscopy and laparoscopic procedures.

sublevels.name: Trauma Surgery
sublevels.description: Trauma surgery is a surgical specialty that utilizes both operative and non-operative management to treat traumatic injuries, typically in an acute setting. Trauma surgeons generally complete residency training in general surgery and often fellowship training in trauma or surgical critical care.

sublevels.name: Plastic Surgery
sublevels.description: Plastic surgery is a surgical specialty involving the restoration, reconstruction or alteration of the human body. It can be divided into two main categories: reconstructive surgery and cosmetic surgery.

sublevels.name: Urological Surgery
sublevels.description: Urology (from Greek ????? ouron "urine" and -????? -logia "study of"), also known as genitourinary surgery, is the branch of medicine that focuses on surgical and medical diseases of the urinary-tract system and the reproductive organs.

sublevels.name: Surgical Orthopedics
sublevels.description: Orthopedic surgery, also known as orthopedics, is a branch of surgery dealing with the musculoskeletal system. Orthopedic surgeons use various surgical and non-surgical procedures such a hip replacement surgery and spinal fusion to treat all problems relating to one's bones and joints.

sublevels.name: Colorectal Surgery
sublevels.description: Colorectal surgery is the management of conditions of the colon, rectum, and anus.

sublevels.name: Cardiac Surgery
sublevels.description: Cardiac surgery is surgery on the heart and the large blood vessels in the chest performed by cardiac surgeons and the perioperative management of these patients

sublevels.name: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
sublevels.description: Oral and maxillofacial surgery is a surgical specialty focusing on reconstructive surgery of the face, facial trauma surgery, the oral cavity, head and neck, mouth, and jaws, as well as facial cosmetic surgery/facial plastic surgery including cleft lip and cleft palate surgery.

sublevels.name: Health Care
sublevels.description: Health care is the discipline concerned with the provision and delivery of health services to a patient population by personnel in professional and allied health occupations.

sublevels.name: Nutrition
sublevels.description: Nutrition or Dietetics is the organic process of nourishing or being nourished, including the processes by which an organism assimilates food and uses it for growth and maintenance.

sublevels.name: Food Security
sublevels.description: Food security is the availability of food in a country (or geography) and the ability of individuals within that country (geography) to access, afford, and source adequate foodstuffs.

sublevels.name: Sports Nutrition
sublevels.description: Sports Nutrition is an interdisciplinary field of study concerned with the understanding of the body's use of nutrients during athletic competition (and the need for nutritional supplements), as well as the practical use of proper nutrition and dietary supplements to enhance athletic performance. Works in the field of Sports Nutrition commonly apply knowledge nutrition science, dietology, biochemistry, exercise physiology, cell and molecular biology.
