sublevels.description: Hindu studies is the study of the traditions and practices of the Indian subcontinent (especially Hinduism), and considered as a subfield of Indology. Beginning with British philology in the colonial period, Hindu studies has been practiced largely by Westerners, due in part to the lack of a distinct department for religion in Indian academia.

sublevels.name: Daoism
sublevels.description: Daoists were supporters both of magic and of proto-science; they were the element of Chinese culture most interested in the study of and experiments with nature. Some Daoists believed that spirits pervaded nature (both the natural world and the internal world within the human body)

sublevels.name: Sikhism
sublevels.description: Sikhism, religion and philosophy founded in the Punjab region of the Indian subcontinent in the late 15th century.  It is often described as the “world’s fifth largest religion”

sublevels.name: Sikh Cultural Studies
sublevels.description: Sikh Cultural Studies explores the history, religion, culture, and social practices of the Sikh community, including their contributions to society and contemporary issues.

sublevels.name: Paganism
sublevels.description: Paganism (from classical Latin p?g?nus "rural", "rustic", later "civilian") is a term first used in the fourth century by early Christians for people in the Roman Empire who practiced polytheism, or ethnic religions other than Christianity.

sublevels.name: Confucianism
sublevels.description: Confucianism, also known as Ruism or Ru classicism, is a system of thought and behavior originating in ancient China, and is variously described as a tradition, philosophy, (humanistic or rationalistic) religion, way of governing leading and following, or way of life.

sublevels.name: History of Religion
sublevels.description: history of major religions and other belief systems

sublevels.name: Anthropology of Religion
sublevels.description: Anthropology of religion is the study of religion in relation to other social institutions, and the comparison of religious beliefs and practices across cultures.

sublevels.name: Spirituality
sublevels.description: Spirituality is the way in which a person understands and lives life in view of her or his ultimate meaning, beliefs, and values. It is the unifying and integrative aspect of the person's life and, when lived intentionally, is experienced as a process of growth and maturity.

sublevels.name: Cross-cultural Studies
sublevels.description: Cross-cultural studies, sometimes called holocultural studies or comparative studies, is a specialization in anthropology and sister sciences such as sociology, psychology, economics, political science that uses field data from many societies through comparative research to examine the scope of human behavior and test hypotheses about human behavior and culture.

sublevels.name: Phenomenology of Religion
sublevels.description: The phenomenology of religion concerns the experiential aspect of religion, describing religious phenomena in terms consistent with the orientation of worshippers. It views religion as made up of different components, and studies these components across religious traditions in order to gain some understanding of them.

sublevels.name: Spiritualism
sublevels.description: Spiritualism was a social religious movement in the nineteenth century, according to which an individual's awareness persists after death and may be contacted by the living

sublevels.name: Law and Religion
sublevels.description: Law and religion is the interdisciplinary study of relationships between law, especially public law, and religion.

sublevels.name: History
sublevels.description: History studies the past, including events occurring after the invention of writing systems (dist. 'prehistory'). History relates to past events as well as the memory, discovery, collection, organization, presentation, and interpretation of information about these events.

sublevels.name: Historiography and Method
sublevels.description: Historiography and Method involve the study of historical writing and methodologies, exploring how historians construct narratives, use sources, and interpret past events.

sublevels.name: Memory Studies
sublevels.description: Memory Studies examines the social, cultural, cognitive, political and technological shifts affecting how, what and why individuals, groups and societies remember, and forget.

sublevels.name: Numismatics
sublevels.description: Numismatics is the study of coins, currency, and related objects, including their history, production, and cultural significance.

sublevels.name: Sphragistics
sublevels.description: Sphragistics, also known as sigillography, is the study of seals and signets, including their history, design, and use in authenticating documents and objects.

sublevels.name: Heraldry
sublevels.description: Heraldry studies the design and display of armorial bearings (known as armory).

sublevels.name: Chronology
sublevels.description: Chronology is the science of arranging events in their order of occurrence in time. It contains the methods, and systems of dating historical events, measuring the passage of time. Historiography can thus define temporal relationships between different occurrences.

sublevels.name: Genealogy
sublevels.description: Genealogy is the study of family history and lineage, tracing the ancestry and descent of individuals and families through historical records and genetic information.

sublevels.name: Diplomatics
sublevels.description: Diplomatics is a scholarly discipline centred on the critical analysis of documents – particularly, but not exclusively, historical documents.

sublevels.name: Palaeography
sublevels.description: Palaeography is the study of historical handwriting, focusing on deciphering and interpreting the script, style, and context of written documents to understand their historical significance and dating. It plays a crucial role in deciphering ancient manuscripts and understanding the development of writing systems over time.

sublevels.name: Oral History
sublevels.description: Oral history is the collection and study of historical information about individuals, families, important events, or everyday life using audiotapes, videotapes, or transcriptions of planned interviews. These interviews are conducted with people who participated in or observed past events and whose memories and perceptions of these are to be preserved as an aural record for future generations.

sublevels.name: European History
sublevels.description: European History encompasses the study of the historical development of Europe, including its diverse cultures, political systems, and social transformations from ancient times to the present.

sublevels.name: History of France
sublevels.description: History of France covers the historical development of France, including its ancient origins, medieval period, Renaissance, revolutionary era, and modern political and cultural changes.

sublevels.name: History of World War II and the Holocaust
sublevels.description: History of World War II and the Holocaust studies the events, causes, and consequences of World War II, with a focus on the Holocaust, the genocide of six million Jews and other persecuted groups by Nazi Germany.

sublevels.name: History of Germany and Central Europe
sublevels.description: History of Germany and Central Europe studies the historical development of Germany and its neighboring Central European countries, focusing on political, social, and cultural transformations.

sublevels.name: History of Italy
sublevels.description: History of Italy covers the historical development of Italy, including its ancient civilizations, medieval states, Renaissance achievements, and modern political and social changes.

sublevels.name: History of Modern Europe
sublevels.description: History of Modern Europe studies the period from the late 18th century to the present, including significant events such as the Industrial Revolution, world wars, and the European Union's formation.

sublevels.name: History of Medieval Europe
sublevels.description: History of Medieval Europe studies the period from the fall of the Roman Empire to the beginning of the Renaissance, focusing on the social, political, cultural, and economic developments of the time.

sublevels.name: History of Ancient Europe
sublevels.description: History of Ancient Europe covers the historical development of European civilizations from prehistoric times to the fall of the Western Roman Empire, focusing on cultural, political, and social changes.

sublevels.name: Russian, Soviet, and East European History
sublevels.description: Russian, Soviet, and East European History encompasses the study of the historical development, political systems, social structures, and cultural transformations of Russia, the Soviet Union, and Eastern European countries from ancient times to the present.

sublevels.name: History of Early Modern Europe
sublevels.description: History of Early Modern Europe studies the period roughly from the late 15th century to the late 18th century, focusing on significant events such as the Renaissance, Reformation, and the Enlightenment.

sublevels.name: History of Britain and Ireland
sublevels.description: History of Britain and Ireland covers the historical development of the British Isles, including political, social, and cultural changes from ancient times to the present.

sublevels.name: Church History
sublevels.description: Church History studies the development, organization, and influence of Christian churches and denominations over time, including their theological, social, and cultural impacts.

sublevels.name: History of the Americas
sublevels.description: History of the Americas covers the historical development of North, Central, and South America, including indigenous cultures, colonization, independence movements, and contemporary issues.

sublevels.name: African-American History
sublevels.description: African-American History is the history of Black Americans

sublevels.name: Latin American History
sublevels.description: Latin American History is the study Latin America's past and that of the people who live there, the countries and cultures they have formed, and its relation to world powers.

sublevels.name: US History
sublevels.description: History of the United States of America. It encompasses the precolonial and colonial period. To be distinguished from History of America and History of the Americas, which include South and Central America as well as the Carribean.

sublevels.name: Asian History
sublevels.description: Asian History encompasses the study of the historical development of the Asian continent, including its diverse cultures, political systems, and social transformations from ancient times to the present.

sublevels.name: History of China
sublevels.description: History of China covers the chronological study of China's past, including its dynastic periods, cultural achievements, political developments, and social transformations from ancient times to the modern era.

sublevels.name: History of South Asia
sublevels.description: History of South Asia encompasses the study of the historical developments, events, and processes that have shaped the societies and cultures of South Asia, covering present-day countries such as India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, and Sri Lanka. This field examines the historical dynamics of religion, politics, and socio-economic interactions within and between South Asian societies.

sublevels.name: History of the Middle East
sublevels.description: History of the Middle East covers the historical development of the Middle Eastern region, including its political, social, cultural, and economic changes from ancient times to the present.

sublevels.name: History of Japan
sublevels.description: Japan was settled about 35,000 years ago by Paleolithic people from the Asian mainland. It is not known when humans first settled on the Japanese archipelago. It was long believed that there was no Paleolithic occupation in Japan, but since World War II thousands of sites have been unearthed throughout the country, yielding a wide variety of Paleolithic tools. Legends surrounding the founding of Japan are compiled as history in the Kojiki (Record of Ancient Matters) and the Nihon shoki (Chronicle of Japan). With the adoption of Buddhism as the state religion, its monasteries gain political power.

sublevels.name: History of Korea
sublevels.description: The History of Korea is a field that studies the historical development of the Korean Peninsula, its culture, politics, and society, from prehistoric times to the present.

sublevels.name: History of Southeast Asia
sublevels.description: History of Southeast Asia covers the historical development of the Southeast Asian region, including its diverse cultures, colonial experiences, independence movements, and contemporary issues.

sublevels.name: Social History
sublevels.description: Social History focuses on the experiences, behaviors, and conditions of ordinary people throughout history, including aspects of daily life, social structures, and cultural practices.

sublevels.name: Legal History
sublevels.description: Legal History studies the evolution of legal systems, laws, and legal institutions over time, exploring how they have shaped and been shaped by social, political, and economic factors.

sublevels.name: History of Science
sublevels.description: History of Science examines the development of scientific knowledge, practices, and institutions over time, exploring how science has shaped and been shaped by historical contexts.

sublevels.name: Cultural History
sublevels.description: Cultural history combines the approaches of anthropology and history to look at popular cultural traditions and cultural interpretations of historical experience.

sublevels.name: History of the Book
sublevels.description: History of the Book examines the development, production, distribution, and reception of books throughout history, including the impact of printing technology and the evolution of literary culture.

sublevels.name: History of Ideas
sublevels.description: History of Ideas explores the development and transformation of key concepts, philosophies, and intellectual movements throughout history, examining their impact on culture and society.

sublevels.name: African History
sublevels.description: African History encompasses the study of the diverse historical experiences of the African continent, including ancient civilizations, colonialism, independence movements, and contemporary issues.

sublevels.name: History of Sub-Saharan Africa
sublevels.description: History of Sub-Saharan Africa studies the historical development of the region south of the Sahara Desert, focusing on pre-colonial societies, colonial impact, and post-independence transformations.

sublevels.name: History of North Africa
sublevels.description: History of North Africa examines the historical development of the North African region, including its ancient civilizations, Islamic influence, colonial period, and contemporary issues.

sublevels.name: Military History
sublevels.description: Military History studies the history of armed conflict, including wars, battles, military strategies, and the impact of warfare on societies and cultures.

sublevels.name: Environmental History
sublevels.description: Environmental History studies the interactions between humans and the natural environment over time, focusing on how environmental changes have influenced societies and how human activities have impacted the environment.

sublevels.name: World History, Global and Transnational History
sublevels.description: World History, Global and Transnational History examines historical processes and events from a global perspective, emphasizing cross-cultural interactions, exchanges, and the interconnectedness of different regions.

sublevels.name: Diplomatic and International History
sublevels.description: Diplomatic and International History studies the interactions between states, including diplomacy, treaties, conflicts, and international organizations, from historical perspectives.

sublevels.name: Classical Studies
sublevels.description: Classical Studies, or Classics, is the interdisciplinary study of the ancient Mediterranean world, particularly ancient Greece and Rome. This field investigates the languages, literature, history, art, philosophy, and archaeology of these civilizations, providing insights into their cultural, social, and political development.

sublevels.name: Australian History
sublevels.description: Australian History covers the historical development of Australia, including its indigenous cultures, colonial period, and contemporary social, political, and economic changes.

sublevels.name: Theories of History
sublevels.description: Theories of History explore different frameworks and methodologies for understanding and interpreting historical events, processes, and narratives, including perspectives such as Marxism, postmodernism, and structuralism.

sublevels.name: History of Technology
sublevels.description: History of Technology examines the development and impact of technological innovations throughout history, exploring how technology has shaped and been shaped by human societies.

sublevels.name: Urban History
sublevels.description: Urban History studies the development, growth, and transformation of cities and urban areas, focusing on their social, economic, cultural, and political aspects.

sublevels.name: Intellectual History
sublevels.description: Intellectual History examines the development and influence of ideas, philosophies, and intellectual movements over time, focusing on how they shape and are shaped by historical contexts.

sublevels.name: Imperialism and Colonialism
sublevels.description: Imperialism and Colonialism examine the historical processes and impacts of empire-building and colonization, including the political, economic, and cultural consequences for both colonizers and colonized societies.

sublevels.name: Decolonization
sublevels.description: Decolonisation refers to the process through which colonies become independent from colonial powers, involving the dismantling of colonial structures and ideologies. It's both a political and cultural journey, aiming to reclaim Indigenous identities, autonomy, and governance. It also involves addressing the lingering impacts of colonisation, including social and economic inequalities, and often calls for a re-evaluation of historical narratives and power dynamics.

sublevels.name: Postcolonial Studies
sublevels.description: Postcolonial Studies is an academic field that examines the effects of colonialism on cultures and societies. It looks at the lasting impacts of colonization, such as cultural identity, power dynamics, and economic disparities, and how these legacies continue to shape the world today. This field challenges Eurocentric narratives and highlights the voices and experiences of previously colonized peoples. It's about understanding and addressing historical injustices and their ongoing repercussions.

sublevels.name: Labor History
sublevels.description: Labor History is the study of the working class and labor movements, focusing on the development of labor unions, labor laws, and the socio-economic conditions of workers throughout history.

sublevels.name: Women's History / History of Gender
sublevels.description: Women's History / History of Gender studies the roles, experiences, and contributions of women throughout history, as well as the social and cultural constructions of gender and their impact on society.

sublevels.name: Modern History
sublevels.description: Modern History refers to the study of historical events and developments from the late 15th century to the present, encompassing significant changes in politics, society, economy, and culture.

sublevels.name: Behavioral Sciences and Psychology
sublevels.description: Psychology is a scientific discipline that focuses on understanding mental functions and the behaviour of individuals and groups.

sublevels.name: Cognitive Psychology
sublevels.description: Cognitive psychology is a subfield of psychology that focuses on the study of mental processes, including how people perceive, think, remember, and problem-solve. It examines the internal processes and structures that underlie human cognition and the ways in which individuals acquire, process, store, and use information.

sublevels.name: Cognitivism
sublevels.description: Cognitivism in the field of psychology is a theoretical perspective that focuses on understanding mental processes such as perception, memory, attention, language, and problem-solving. It emphasizes the role of internal mental representations, information processing, and cognitive structures in shaping behavior and thought.

sublevels.name: Motivation
sublevels.description: Motivation, as a field of study within psychology, focuses on understanding the processes, factors, and mechanisms that drive and direct human behavior towards specific goals. It explores why individuals initiate, sustain, and terminate certain behaviors, and how various internal and external factors influence these behaviors. Motivation research in psychology examines the cognitive, emotional, and physiological processes involved in motivation, as well as the role of individual differences, social influences, and cultural factors. It seeks to uncover the underlying mechanisms that determine the intensity, direction, and persistence of behavi

sublevels.name: Learning Psychology
sublevels.description: Learning psychology, in the field of psychology, is a branch that focuses on the study of how individuals acquire, retain, and apply knowledge and skills. It examines the processes, factors, and theories involved in learning, including cognitive, behavioral, and social aspects.

sublevels.name: Learning Theory
sublevels.description: Learning theory as a field of study encompasses the systematic examination, analysis, and exploration of the processes, principles, and mechanisms underlying human learning. It involves the study of how individuals acquire, process, retain, and apply knowledge and skills across different domains and contexts. Learning theory as a field draws from various disciplines, including psychology, education, neuroscience, and cognitive science, to develop and refine theories, models, and frameworks that explain the nature of learning and inform educational practices. Researchers in this field investigate factors that influence learning, such as motivation, cognition, environment, and social interactions, and strive to identify effective instructional strategies, interventions, and approaches that optimize learning outcomes.

sublevels.name: Behaviorism
sublevels.description: Behaviorism is a school of thought in psychology that emphasizes the study of observable behavior rather than internal mental processes. It focuses on understanding how behavior is shaped by the environment through conditioning and reinforcement.

sublevels.name: Intelligence
sublevels.description: Intelligence is a complex psychological construct that refers to a person's ability to learn, reason, problem-solve, think abstractly, comprehend complex ideas, and adapt to new situations. Intelligence has been studied extensively in psychology, with many different theories and models developed to explain its nature and development. Intelligence is typically measured through standardized tests, such as IQ tests, which provide a numerical score that is used to rank individuals in terms of their relative intelligence.

sublevels.name: Learning and Memory
sublevels.description: Learning and memory, in the field of psychology, are interconnected processes that involve acquiring, retaining, and retrieving information. Learning refers to the process of acquiring new knowledge or skills through experience, instruction, or observation, while memory is the ability to store and retrieve information over time. Together, they play a crucial role in cognitive functioning, skill development, and adaptive behavior.

sublevels.name: Cognition
sublevels.description: Cognition in the field of psychology refers to the mental processes and abilities involved in acquiring, processing, storing, and using information. It encompasses various aspects of thinking, including perception, attention, memory, language, problem-solving, and decision-making.

sublevels.name: Creativity
sublevels.description: Creativity in the field of psychology refers to the ability to generate novel and valuable ideas, solutions, or products. It involves the generation of unique and original insights, the ability to think divergently, and the capacity to engage in imaginative and flexible thinking.

sublevels.name: Language Processing
sublevels.description: Language processing in the field of psychology refers to the cognitive and neural processes involved in the comprehension, production, and use of language. It encompasses various aspects such as phonological processing, syntactic processing, semantic processing, and pragmatic processing, which collectively contribute to our ability to understand and communicate through language.

sublevels.name: Language Acquisition and Development
sublevels.description: Language acquisition is the ability to understand a language, using it to communicate with others.   Language acquisition and language development can be understood as synonymous

sublevels.name: Sport Psychology
sublevels.description: Sport Psychologyis is concerned with the preconditions and determining factors of the behaviour and experience of individuals (persons) in sport.  It aims at the adequate unterstanding of the behaviour and the experience of individuals in sport by describing and measuring consistency and variability, by offering explanations, as well as by determining their preconditions and possibilities to predict and shape its future course.  More specifically, Sport Psychology explores the processes of perception and decision making during sports games, the emergence or reduction of emotions (such as fear), the determining factors of an active lifestyle, the impact of sport on the development of children or the personality and group features of successful athletes and teams.

sublevels.name: Emotion
sublevels.description: Emotion in the field of psychology refers to a complex psychological and physiological state that involves subjective experiences, physiological arousal, and behavioral expressions. Emotions are multifaceted responses to internal or external stimuli and play a crucial role in motivation, decision-making, and social interactions.

sublevels.name: Emotion Theory
sublevels.description: Emotion theory in the field of psychology refers to a collection of theoretical frameworks and models that attempt to explain the nature, function, and development of emotions. Emotions are complex psychological phenomena that involve subjective experiences, physiological changes, cognitive appraisals, expressive behaviors, and social interactions. Emotion theory seeks to provide a systematic and comprehensive understanding of emotions by integrating insights from various fields, such as cognitive psychology, neuroscience, social psychology, and developmental psychology.

sublevels.name: Perception
sublevels.description: Perception, in the field of psychology, refers to the process of interpreting and making sense of sensory information received from the environment. It involves the organization, identification, and interpretation of sensory stimuli, allowing individuals to form mental representations of the world around them.

sublevels.name: Psychophysics
sublevels.description: Psychophysics is a field of methodology within psychology concerned with studying the sensation of stimuli. Psychophysics methods typically record the effect of systematic modulation of stimuli on a subject’s perception.

sublevels.name: Language Processing
sublevels.description: Language processing in the field of psychology refers to the cognitive and neural processes involved in the comprehension, production, and use of language. It encompasses various aspects such as phonological processing, syntactic processing, semantic processing, and pragmatic processing, which collectively contribute to our ability to understand and communicate through language.

sublevels.name: Clinical Psychology
sublevels.description: Clinical psychology is a specialized field within psychology that focuses on the assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of mental disorders and psychological distress. Clinical psychologists are trained to work with individuals of all ages, from children to older adults, and they often work in various settings such as clinics, hospitals, private practices, and academic institutions.

sublevels.name: Psychopathology
sublevels.description: Psychopathology is a field of study within psychology that focuses on the study of mental disorders or abnormal behaviors. It involves the examination of the causes, symptoms, development, and treatment of various psychological disorders. Psychopathology seeks to understand the underlying mechanisms and processes that contribute to the manifestation of abnormal behaviors, emotions, and cognitions. Researchers and clinicians in this field aim to identify patterns, assess the impact of mental disorders on individuals' lives, and develop effective interventions to promote mental health and well-being.

sublevels.name: Psychodynamics
sublevels.description: Psychodynamics is a field of study within psychology that focuses on understanding the psychological forces and processes that influence human behavior, emotions, and personality. It explores the interplay between conscious and unconscious aspects of the mind, including childhood experiences, defense mechanisms, and the dynamics of interpersonal relationships. Psychodynamics places emphasis on the role of unconscious motivations, conflicts, and unresolved issues in shaping individuals' thoughts, feelings, and actions.

sublevels.name: Military Psychology
sublevels.description: Military psychology is the application of several branches within psychology to understanding and treating the unique stressors that come with conducting military operations

sublevels.name: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
sublevels.description: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a field of study within psychology that focuses on understanding and addressing the psychological and emotional impact of traumatic experiences. It involves the exploration of the symptoms, causes, and treatment of PTSD, which can occur following exposure to a traumatic event such as war, natural disasters, accidents, or personal assault. Researchers and practitioners in this field aim to better understand the complex nature of PTSD, its effects on individuals, and develop effective interventions to promote healing and recovery.

sublevels.name: Mental Health
sublevels.description: Mental health can be understood as the psychological state of someone who is functioning at a satisfactory level of emotional and behavioural adjustment

sublevels.name: Analytical Psychology
sublevels.description: Analytical psychology is a field of study within psychology that focuses on the theories and practices developed by Swiss psychiatrist Carl Jung. It explores the deep connections between the conscious and unconscious aspects of the human psyche, emphasizing the role of symbolism, archetypes, and individuation. Analytical psychology places particular emphasis on the exploration of the unconscious mind and the integration of its contents into one's conscious awareness. It seeks to understand the complexities of the human psyche, including personality development, psychological disorders, and the process of self-discovery and personal growth. Analytical psychologists utilize various techniques, including dream analysis, active imagination, and the interpretation of symbols, to facilitate the exploration and understanding of the unconscious aspects of the individual. The goal of analytical psychology is to promote self-awareness, psychological well-being, and the development of a harmonious relationship between the conscious and unconscious aspects of the psyche.

sublevels.name: Humanistic Psychology
sublevels.description: Humanistic psychology is a psychological perspective that emphasizes the unique qualities of individuals, their subjective experiences, and their inherent capacity for personal growth and self-fulfillment. It focuses on understanding human behavior in the context of personal meaning, self-actualization, and the pursuit of personal values and goals. Humanistic psychologists emphasize the importance of self-awareness, self-acceptance, and the realization of one's full potential.

sublevels.name: Clinical Social Work
sublevels.description: Clinical social work is a specialized field within social work that focuses on the assessment, diagnosis, and treatment of individuals, families, and communities who are experiencing various mental health and psychosocial issues. Clinical social workers are trained professionals who provide therapeutic interventions, counseling, and support to clients in order to enhance their overall well-being and functioning. They work in diverse settings such as hospitals, clinics, schools, and private practices, collaborating with other professionals to address clients' emotional, behavioral, and social needs. The field of clinical social work integrates principles from social work, psychology, and psychiatry to provide comprehensive and holistic care to individuals and communities.

sublevels.name: Mental Disorder
sublevels.description: In the field of psychology, mental disorder refers to a broad range of conditions characterized by significant disturbances in thoughts, emotions, behaviors, and functioning. Mental disorders are studied within the context of understanding their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. Researchers and clinicians in the field of mental disorders aim to classify and understand these conditions, explore their impact on individuals' well-being and daily functioning, and develop effective interventions and support systems.

sublevels.name: Attention Deficit Disorder
sublevels.description: Attention deficit disorder (ADD), as a field of study in psychology, focuses on understanding the nature, causes, and treatment of attention deficits that significantly impact individuals' daily functioning. It involves examining the cognitive, behavioral, and emotional aspects of attention difficulties, as well as exploring the factors that contribute to the development and persistence of attention deficits. Researchers and clinicians in the field of ADD aim to identify effective strategies and interventions to help individuals with attention deficits improve their attentional control, academic performance, and overall well-being.

sublevels.name: Substance Abuse Disorder
sublevels.description: Substance abuse addiction, also known as substance use disorder, is a field of study in psychology that focuses on understanding and addressing the patterns of excessive and harmful use of substances such as drugs or alcohol. It involves examining the psychological, social, and biological factors contributing to the development and maintenance of addiction, as well as developing effective prevention, intervention, and treatment strategies. The field of substance abuse addiction seeks to understand the underlying mechanisms, risk factors, and consequences associated with substance abuse, and to promote recovery and overall well-being.

sublevels.name: Psychotic Disorder
sublevels.description: Psychotic Disorder, as a field of study in psychology, focuses on understanding and treating severe mental illnesses characterized by significant disturbances in thinking, perception, and behavior. Researchers and clinicians in this field investigate the causes, symptoms, and treatment options for psychotic disorders, such as schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder. They examine biological, psychological, and social factors that contribute to the development and progression of these disorders, and work towards developing effective interventions to alleviate symptoms and improve overall functioning.

sublevels.name: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
sublevels.description: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a field of study within psychology that focuses on understanding and addressing the psychological and emotional impact of traumatic experiences. It involves the exploration of the symptoms, causes, and treatment of PTSD, which can occur following exposure to a traumatic event such as war, natural disasters, accidents, or personal assault. Researchers and practitioners in this field aim to better understand the complex nature of PTSD, its effects on individuals, and develop effective interventions to promote healing and recovery.

sublevels.name: Somatoform Disorder
sublevels.description: Somatoform Disorder is a field of study in psychology that involves the investigation and understanding of a group of mental disorders characterized by physical symptoms that cannot be fully explained by a medical condition or other physiological factors. Individuals with somatoform disorders often experience distress and impairment due to their physical symptoms, which are believed to be influenced primarily by psychological factors.

sublevels.name: Eating Disorder
sublevels.description: Eating disorders, as a field of study in psychology, involves the examination of abnormal eating behaviors and their psychological underpinnings. Researchers and clinicians in this field investigate the complex interplay between biological, psychological, and sociocultural factors that contribute to the development and maintenance of eating disorders. They study various types of eating disorders such as anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, and binge eating disorder, aiming to understand the underlying mechanisms, risk factors, and treatment approaches associated with these conditions. The field of eating disorders encompasses research, assessment, and interventions to support individuals struggling with disordered eating patterns and promote their recovery.

sublevels.name: Sexual Disorder
sublevels.description: Sexual disorders refer to a range of conditions that affect an individual's ability to experience sexual arousal, desire, or function in a way that is satisfactory to them. These disorders can have a significant impact on an individual's quality of life and relationships. The field of study that focuses on the diagnosis, assessment, and treatment of sexual disorders is known as sexual psychology.

sublevels.name: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
sublevels.description: Obsessive compulsive disorder is a psychiatric disease that is characterized by anxiety, fear and repetitive behaviour. Possible symptoms are excessive cleaning, repeated checking or hoarding.

sublevels.name: Schizophrenia
sublevels.description: Schizophrenia is a severe and debilitating psychiatric disorder that involves psychotic symptoms such as hallucinations and delusions, accompanied with regressive behaviour.

sublevels.name: Depression
sublevels.description: Depression refers to a state of low mood that can be accompanied with loss of interest in activities that the individual normally perceived as pleasurable, altered appetite and sleep/wake balance. Its severe form, major depression is classified as a mood disorder.

sublevels.name: Anxiety
sublevels.description: Anxiety is characterized by excessive uneasiness, apprehension or dread. It can be generalized or be directed towards specific, usually imagined or exaggerated threat.

sublevels.name: Bipolar Disorder
sublevels.description: Bipolar disorder is a mood disorder that includes at least one manic episode, characterized by elevated or agitated mood and often reduced need for sleep accompanied by episodes of major depression.

sublevels.name: Personality Disorder
sublevels.description: Personality disorder is a type of mental disorder in which an individual has a persistent and inflexible pattern of behavior, cognition, and inner experience that deviates significantly from cultural and societal expectations. This pattern of behavior is typically evident across a range of personal and social situations, and it often causes significant distress and impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning.

sublevels.name: Rehabilitation Psychology
sublevels.description: Rehabilitation psychology is a field of study that focuses on promoting the psychological well-being, functional independence, and quality of life of individuals with disabilities or chronic health conditions. It involves understanding the impact of physical, cognitive, emotional, and social limitations on individuals' functioning and developing interventions to enhance their adjustment, coping skills, and overall rehabilitation outcomes. Rehabilitation psychologists work collaboratively with individuals, their families, and healthcare professionals to facilitate the recovery process, improve functioning, and optimize participation in daily activities and society.

sublevels.name: Trauma Psychology
sublevels.description: Trauma is a physiological wound, which can be penetrating or nonpenetrating, caused directly or indirectly by external physical force.

sublevels.name: Behavioral Medicine
sublevels.description: Behavioral Medicine is a multidisciplinary field that combines principles and knowledge from psychology, medicine, and behavioral sciences to understand the complex relationship between behavior and health. It focuses on the application of behavioral and psychological principles to prevent and treat illness, promote health, and enhance well-being. Behavioral Medicine recognizes that human behavior plays a crucial role in the development, maintenance, and treatment of various physical and mental health conditions. It integrates psychological interventions, behavior change strategies, and lifestyle modifications with medical treatments to optimize health outcomes and improve quality of life.

sublevels.name: Social Psychology
sublevels.description: Social psychology is a field of psychology that focuses on how individuals' thoughts, feelings, and behaviors are influenced by the presence of others and the social context in which they exist. It explores various aspects of human social interaction, including social perception, attitudes, conformity, group dynamics, and interpersonal relationships.

sublevels.name: Cross-Cultural Psychology
sublevels.description: Cross-cultural psychology is a field of psychology that examines the influence of cultural factors on human behavior, cognition, and development. It explores the similarities and differences in psychological processes across different cultures, aiming to understand the ways in which culture shapes individual and collective behavior.

sublevels.name: Environmental Psychology
sublevels.description: Environmental psychology is a branch of psychology that studies the interactions between individuals and their physical and social environments. It examines how the environment affects human behavior, emotions, and well-being, and how individuals perceive, understand, and respond to their surroundings.

sublevels.name: Cultural Psychology
sublevels.description: Cultural psychology is a field of psychology that focuses on how cultural factors shape and influence individual and collective psychological processes. It examines the ways in which culture, including shared beliefs, values, practices, and symbols, influence human cognition, emotion, perception, and behavior.

sublevels.name: Persuasion
sublevels.description: Persuasion in the field of psychology refers to the deliberate attempt to influence or change someone's attitudes, beliefs, or behaviors through the use of communication and argumentation. It involves understanding the cognitive and social processes that shape people's responses to persuasive messages and employing strategies to effectively sway their opinions or actions.

sublevels.name: Interpersonal Attraction
sublevels.description: Interpersonal attraction in the field of psychology refers to the psychological processes and factors that influence individuals' feelings of liking, interest, or attraction towards others. It encompasses various aspects of human relationships, such as physical attractiveness, similarity, proximity, and social interaction.

sublevels.name: Attitudes
sublevels.description: In the field of psychology, attitudes refer to an individual's evaluations, beliefs, and feelings toward people, objects, or ideas. Attitudes can be positive, negative, or neutral, and they influence our thoughts, emotions, and behaviors.

sublevels.name: Self-efficacy
sublevels.description: Self-efficacy, in the field of psychology, refers to an individual's belief in their own capabilities to successfully execute tasks, achieve goals, and overcome challenges. It is the perception of one's competence and confidence in their abilities to perform specific actions and produce desired outcomes.

sublevels.name: Prejudice
sublevels.description: Prejudice in the field of psychology refers to preconceived opinions, attitudes, or stereotypes about individuals or groups based on their perceived characteristics, such as race, ethnicity, gender, or religion. It involves biased judgments and discriminatory behavior towards others based on these preconceptions.

sublevels.name: Sense of Community
sublevels.description: Sense of community, in the field of psychology, refers to the subjective perception and experience of individuals regarding their connectedness, belongingness, and shared identity within a particular social group or community. It involves feelings of mutual support, trust, and shared values among community members, contributing to a sense of belonging and collective well-being.

sublevels.name: Group Dynamics
sublevels.description: Group dynamics is a field of psychology that focuses on understanding how individuals interact and behave in group settings. It examines the influence of social processes, norms, roles, and relationships on group behavior, decision-making, and productivity.

sublevels.name: Self-serving bias
sublevels.description: Self-serving bias, in the field of psychology, refers to the tendency for individuals to attribute their successes to internal factors while attributing their failures to external factors. It is a cognitive bias that helps maintain and protect one's self-esteem by enhancing positive self-evaluations and minimizing negative ones.

sublevels.name: Social Perception
sublevels.description: Social perception is a field of psychology that focuses on how individuals perceive and interpret social information about others. It examines the cognitive processes involved in forming impressions, making judgments, and attributing meaning to the behavior of others in social interactions. Social perception plays a crucial role in understanding social behavior, interpersonal relationships, and the formation of attitudes and stereotypes.

sublevels.name: Consumer Behavior
sublevels.description: Consumer behavior refers to the study of individuals, groups, or organizations and the processes they use to select, secure, use, and dispose of products, services, experiences, or ideas to satisfy their needs and desires. It is a crucial area of research for management as it helps companies understand their customers better and develop marketing strategies to meet their needs effectively.  Consumer behavior research involves analyzing various factors that influence consumers' buying decisions, including their psychological, social, cultural, and economic factors. It helps companies understand the motivations, attitudes, and preferences of their customers and how these factors influence their buying decisions.  By understanding consumer behavior, companies can create products and services that better meet their customers' needs, develop effective marketing campaigns, and build stronger relationships with their customers. It also helps companies identify potential new markets and opportunities for growth.

sublevels.name: Social Influence
sublevels.description: Social influence, in the field of psychology, refers to the process through which individuals' thoughts, feelings, and behaviors are influenced by the presence, actions, or opinions of others. It examines how social factors and group dynamics shape individuals' attitudes, beliefs, and actions, leading to conformity, compliance, or obedience.

sublevels.name: Aggression
sublevels.description: Aggression, in the field of psychology, refers to behavior that is intended to cause harm or infliction of physical or psychological pain on others. It involves acts such as physical violence, verbal aggression, and hostile behavior. Aggression can be influenced by various factors, including individual differences, social and cultural factors, and situational triggers.

sublevels.name: Prosocial Behavior
sublevels.description: Prosocial behavior in the field of psychology refers to voluntary actions intended to benefit others or promote the well-being of individuals or society as a whole. It involves acts of kindness, empathy, cooperation, and altruism that contribute to positive social interactions and the betterment of communities.

sublevels.name: Cognition
sublevels.description: Cognition in the field of psychology refers to the mental processes and abilities involved in acquiring, processing, storing, and using information. It encompasses various aspects of thinking, including perception, attention, memory, language, problem-solving, and decision-making.

sublevels.name: Creativity
sublevels.description: Creativity in the field of psychology refers to the ability to generate novel and valuable ideas, solutions, or products. It involves the generation of unique and original insights, the ability to think divergently, and the capacity to engage in imaginative and flexible thinking.

sublevels.name: Language Processing
sublevels.description: Language processing in the field of psychology refers to the cognitive and neural processes involved in the comprehension, production, and use of language. It encompasses various aspects such as phonological processing, syntactic processing, semantic processing, and pragmatic processing, which collectively contribute to our ability to understand and communicate through language.

sublevels.name: Language Acquisition and Development
sublevels.description: Language acquisition is the ability to understand a language, using it to communicate with others.   Language acquisition and language development can be understood as synonymous

sublevels.name: Stereotype
sublevels.description: Stereotype, in the field of psychology, refers to a widely held belief or generalization about a particular group or category of people. Stereotypes are cognitive shortcuts that allow individuals to quickly categorize and make assumptions about others based on their group membership. They can be positive, negative, or neutral and often involve oversimplified and exaggerated characteristics or attributes.

sublevels.name: Communication Psychology
sublevels.description: Communication psychology is a field of psychology that focuses on the study of how individuals perceive, interpret, and engage in communication processes. It examines the psychological factors that influence communication effectiveness, including verbal and nonverbal communication, interpersonal dynamics, and the impact of media on human communication.

sublevels.name: Interpersonal Communication
sublevels.description: Interpersonal Communication is the study of direct, often face-to-face or small-group interactions, focusing on relational processes, nonverbal behavior, emotional expression, and the co-construction of meaning between individuals.

sublevels.name: Psychosocial Studies
sublevels.description: Psychosocial Studies examines the social influences on individual behavior. It seeks to investigate the ways in which psychic and social processes can be understood as implicated in each other and mutually constitutive.

sublevels.name: Creativity
sublevels.description: Creativity in the field of psychology refers to the ability to generate novel and valuable ideas, solutions, or products. It involves the generation of unique and original insights, the ability to think divergently, and the capacity to engage in imaginative and flexible thinking.

sublevels.name: Gender and Sexuality
sublevels.description: Gender and sexuality are two distinct but interconnected concepts that play significant roles in shaping individual identities, social structures, and cultural norms. Gender refers to the social, cultural, and behavioral characteristics, roles, expectations, and identities that a given society associates with individuals based on their perceived sex.  Sexuality refers to an individual's sexual orientation, attractions, and experiences. It encompasses who a person is emotionally, romantically, and sexually attracted to.

sublevels.name: Social Cognition
sublevels.description: Social cognition, in the field of psychology, refers to the cognitive processes and mental representations that underlie our understanding of social information and guide our social interactions. It involves how individuals perceive, process, interpret, and remember social cues, such as emotions, attitudes, beliefs, intentions, and social norms, to make sense of others' behavior and make informed social judgments.

sublevels.name: Biological Psychology
sublevels.description: Biological psychology, also known as biopsychology or psychobiology, is a field of study within psychology that examines the biological processes and physiological mechanisms underlying behavior and mental processes. It explores the complex relationship between the brain, the body, and behavior.  It explores how biological factors, such as the structure and functioning of the nervous system, genetics, and hormones, influence human behavior and cognitive processes.

sublevels.name: Evolutionary Psychology
sublevels.description: Evolutionary Psychology is a field of study that seeks to understand human behavior and cognition through the lens of evolutionary theory. It explores how evolutionary processes have shaped our psychological mechanisms, adaptive behaviors, and cognitive abilities. This approach posits that many human behaviors and mental processes are the result of natural selection acting on our ancestors' traits, allowing them to survive and reproduce in their environments. By examining the evolutionary roots of various psychological phenomena, Evolutionary Psychology aims to provide insights into the adaptive functions and evolutionary origins of human behavior, cognition, emotions, and social interactions. It draws upon principles from evolutionary biology, psychology, anthropology, and cognitive science to unravel the evolutionary underpinnings of human nature.

sublevels.name: Sensory Psychology
sublevels.description: Sensory Psychology refers to the study of sensation, which is the process by which our sensory receptors, such as the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin, detect and respond to external stimuli.

sublevels.name: Behavioral Genetics
sublevels.description: Behavioural genetics is the interdisciplinary effort to establish causal links between genes and animal (including human) behavioural traits and neural mechanisms. Methods used include twin studies, quantitative trait mapping by linkage to allelic variants, transgenic animals and targeted gene disruption or silencing.

sublevels.name: Neuropsychology
sublevels.description: A branch of psychology examining how cognition and behavior are related to the brain and the rest of the nervous system. Often focuses on how injuries affect cognitive and behavioral functions.

sublevels.name: Comparative Psychology
sublevels.description: Comparative psychology refers to the scientific study of the behavior and mental processes of non-human animals, especially as these relate to the phylogenetic history, adaptive significance, and development of behavior. Research in this area addresses many different issues, uses many different methods and explores the behavior of many different species from insects to primates

sublevels.name: Cross-species Comparison
sublevels.description: Cross-species comparison is a research approach within psychology that involves studying and comparing behaviors, cognitive processes, and physiological mechanisms across different species. It aims to identify similarities and differences in mental processes and behaviors between humans and other animals, providing insights into evolutionary origins, adaptive functions, and underlying mechanisms of various psychological phenomena.

sublevels.name: Animal Cognition
sublevels.description: Animal cognition is a field within psychology that focuses on the study of mental processes and behaviors in non-human animals. It seeks to understand how animals perceive, learn, think, and solve problems, as well as how they communicate, make decisions, and exhibit social behavior. Animal cognition researchers use various experimental and observational methods to investigate the cognitive abilities and processes of different animal species.

sublevels.name: Educational Psychology
sublevels.description: Educational psychology is a branch of psychology that focuses on understanding how people learn and develop in educational settings. It applies psychological principles and theories to improve teaching methods, enhance learning outcomes, and promote optimal educational experiences. Educational psychologists study various aspects of learning and instruction, including cognitive processes, motivation, memory, assessment, classroom management, and individual differences among learners. They collaborate with educators, administrators, and policymakers to design effective educational interventions, create supportive learning environments, and address the diverse needs of learners.

sublevels.name: Motivation
sublevels.description: Motivation, as a field of study within psychology, focuses on understanding the processes, factors, and mechanisms that drive and direct human behavior towards specific goals. It explores why individuals initiate, sustain, and terminate certain behaviors, and how various internal and external factors influence these behaviors. Motivation research in psychology examines the cognitive, emotional, and physiological processes involved in motivation, as well as the role of individual differences, social influences, and cultural factors. It seeks to uncover the underlying mechanisms that determine the intensity, direction, and persistence of behavi

sublevels.name: Classroom Management
sublevels.description: Classroom management, as a field of study, involves the strategies, techniques, and approaches used by educators to create and maintain an effective learning environment within a classroom setting. It focuses on promoting positive student behavior, engagement, and academic achievement while minimizing disruptions and fostering a supportive and inclusive classroom climate.

sublevels.name: School Psychology
sublevels.description: School psychology is a specialized field of study within psychology that focuses on the assessment, diagnosis, intervention, and support of students' academic, social, emotional, and behavioral needs within educational settings. School psychologists work collaboratively with students, parents, teachers, and other professionals to promote optimal learning and development for students. They apply psychological principles and methods to understand and address various factors that may impact students' educational experience, such as learning disabilities, behavioral issues, social challenges, and mental health concerns.

sublevels.name: Instructional Psychology
sublevels.description: Instructional psychology is a field of study that focuses on understanding and optimizing the processes of teaching and learning. It involves the application of psychological principles, theories, and research to enhance instructional practices and improve educational outcomes. Instructional theorists and psychologists aim to develop and refine instructional models and approaches based on empirical evidence and psychological principles to facilitate effective teaching and maximize students' acquisition of knowledge and skills.

sublevels.name: Self-Regulation
sublevels.description: Self-regulation is a field of study in psychology that focuses on the processes and strategies individuals use to manage and control their thoughts, emotions, and behaviors. It encompasses the ability to set goals, monitor one's progress, and make adjustments in order to achieve desired outcomes. Self-regulation involves a range of cognitive, emotional, and behavioral processes, such as attention control, impulse control, emotion regulation, self-monitoring, and self-reflection.

sublevels.name: Learning Theory
sublevels.description: Learning theory as a field of study encompasses the systematic examination, analysis, and exploration of the processes, principles, and mechanisms underlying human learning. It involves the study of how individuals acquire, process, retain, and apply knowledge and skills across different domains and contexts. Learning theory as a field draws from various disciplines, including psychology, education, neuroscience, and cognitive science, to develop and refine theories, models, and frameworks that explain the nature of learning and inform educational practices. Researchers in this field investigate factors that influence learning, such as motivation, cognition, environment, and social interactions, and strive to identify effective instructional strategies, interventions, and approaches that optimize learning outcomes.

sublevels.name: Psychological Methods
sublevels.description: Psychological methods, as a field of study, encompasses the various techniques, tools, and approaches employed in psychological research and investigation. It focuses on the rigorous and systematic methods used to collect, analyze, and interpret data in order to understand human behavior, cognition, emotions, and mental processes.

sublevels.name: Experimental Psychology
sublevels.description: Experimental psychology is a branch of psychology that focuses on conducting scientific experiments to study and understand human behavior and mental processes. It involves designing and conducting controlled experiments in order to investigate various psychological phenomena, such as perception, memory, learning, cognition, emotion, and motivation. Experimental psychologists use rigorous research methods and statistical analyses to collect and analyze data, which helps them draw conclusions and make inferences about the underlying mechanisms of human behavior. By manipulating independent variables and measuring dependent variables, experimental psychologists aim to establish cause-and-effect relationships and test hypotheses about psychological processes.

sublevels.name: Statistics in Social Sciences, Humanities, Law, Education, Behavorial Sciences, Public Policy
sublevels.description: Statistics is a branch of mathematics that involves the collection, analysis, interpretation, presentation, and organization of data. In the context of social sciences, humanities, law, education, behavioral sciences, and public policy, statistics plays a crucial role in providing a quantitative framework for studying and understanding various phenomena. It involves the application of statistical methods and techniques to examine patterns, relationships, and trends within data, ultimately facilitating evidence-based decision making and drawing valid conclusions.

sublevels.name: Psychometrics
sublevels.description: Psychometrics is a subfield of psychology that deals with the theory and techniques of psychological measurement, including the development, validation, and interpretation of psychological tests and other assessment instruments. It focuses on the measurement of psychological constructs such as intelligence, personality, and attitudes, and the statistical analysis of the data generated by these measures. The goal of psychometrics is to ensure that the tests and instruments used to measure psychological constructs are reliable, valid, and fair.

sublevels.name: Quantitative Psychology
sublevels.description: Quantitative psychology is a subfield of psychology that focuses on the measurement, analysis, and interpretation of psychological data using quantitative methods. It involves the application of statistical and mathematical techniques to gather and analyze data related to human behavior, cognition, and emotions. Quantitative psychologists develop and utilize sophisticated research designs and statistical models to investigate psychological phenomena, test hypotheses, and make empirical conclusions.

sublevels.name: Qualitative Psychology
sublevels.description: Qualitative psychology is an approach within the field of psychology that focuses on understanding and exploring the subjective experiences, meanings, and interpretations of individuals. It emphasizes the use of qualitative research methods to gain in-depth insights into the complexities of human behavior, thoughts, and emotions. Unlike quantitative psychology, which relies on numerical data and statistical analyses, qualitative psychology emphasizes the collection and analysis of non-numerical data, such as interviews, observations, and textual materials.

sublevels.name: Mathematical Psychology
sublevels.description: Mathematical psychology is psychological research that is based on mathematical modeling of perceptual, thought, cognitive and motor processes.

sublevels.name: Psychophysics
sublevels.description: Psychophysics is a field of methodology within psychology concerned with studying the sensation of stimuli. Psychophysics methods typically record the effect of systematic modulation of stimuli on a subject’s perception.

sublevels.name: Community Psychology
sublevels.description: Community psychology is a field of study within psychology that focuses on understanding and promoting the well-being of individuals within their social and cultural contexts. It emphasizes the importance of considering the broader systems and environments in which people live, rather than solely focusing on individual-level factors.

sublevels.name: History of Psychology
sublevels.description: The history of psychology is a field of study that examines the development of psychological thought and practices over time. It involves the critical analysis of the intellectual, social, and cultural factors that have shaped the emergence, evolution, and diversification of psychological theories, concepts, and methods from ancient times to the present. The history of psychology seeks to provide a nuanced and contextualized understanding of the origins, influences, and contributions of key figures and movements in psychology, as well as the broader historical and cultural contexts that have influenced their work.

sublevels.name: Health Psychology
sublevels.description: Health psychology is the study of psychological and behavioral processes in health, illness, and healthcare. It is concerned with understanding how psychological, behavioral, and cultural factors contribute to physical health and illness

sublevels.name: Personality and Differential Psychology
sublevels.description: Personality and Differential Psychology is a subfield of psychology that examines the ways in which individuals differ from one another in their thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. It explores the various factors that contribute to the development of personality traits and how these traits shape an individual's behavior in different situations. It also investigates the role of individual differences in areas such as intelligence, creativity, and mental health. Ultimately, the goal of Personality and Differential Psychology is to understand the unique aspects of individuals and how these aspects relate to their experiences and outcomes in life.

sublevels.name: Intelligence
sublevels.description: Intelligence is a complex psychological construct that refers to a person's ability to learn, reason, problem-solve, think abstractly, comprehend complex ideas, and adapt to new situations. Intelligence has been studied extensively in psychology, with many different theories and models developed to explain its nature and development. Intelligence is typically measured through standardized tests, such as IQ tests, which provide a numerical score that is used to rank individuals in terms of their relative intelligence.

sublevels.name: Personality
sublevels.description: Personality refers to the unique pattern of thoughts, feelings, and behaviors that characterize an individual and distinguish them from others. It encompasses a wide range of psychological traits and characteristics that are relatively enduring over time and across different situations. These traits may include aspects such as emotional stability, sociability, openness to experience, conscientiousness, and agreeableness, among others. Personality can be studied and measured through various psychological tools and assessments, and it plays a crucial role in shaping an individual's behavior, relationships, and overall well-being.

sublevels.name: Personality Disorder
sublevels.description: Personality disorder is a type of mental disorder in which an individual has a persistent and inflexible pattern of behavior, cognition, and inner experience that deviates significantly from cultural and societal expectations. This pattern of behavior is typically evident across a range of personal and social situations, and it often causes significant distress and impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning.

sublevels.name: Gender and Sexuality
sublevels.description: Gender and sexuality are two distinct but interconnected concepts that play significant roles in shaping individual identities, social structures, and cultural norms. Gender refers to the social, cultural, and behavioral characteristics, roles, expectations, and identities that a given society associates with individuals based on their perceived sex.  Sexuality refers to an individual's sexual orientation, attractions, and experiences. It encompasses who a person is emotionally, romantically, and sexually attracted to.

sublevels.name: Industrial and Organizational Psychology
sublevels.description: Industrial and Organizational Psychology (also known as Work and Organizational Psychology, Business Psychology, or I/O Psychology) is the scientific study of human behavior in the workplace. It applies psychological theories and research methods to understand and improve how individuals and organizations function. This field addresses topics such as personnel selection, employee training and development, organizational effectiveness, and the design of healthy and motivating work environments. The ultimate goal of I/O Psychology is to enhance employee well-being, job satisfaction, and productivity while supporting organizational performance and efficiency.

sublevels.name: Personnel Psychology
sublevels.description: A subfield of industrial/organizational psychology that concentrates on the recruitment, selection, and evaluation of personnel, along with employee behavior and relationships in the workplace.

sublevels.name: Organizational Psychology
sublevels.description: Organizational psychology, also known as industrial-organizational (I-O) psychology, is a field of study within psychology that focuses on understanding and improving human behavior in the workplace. It applies psychological theories, principles, and research methods to enhance individual and organizational effectiveness, well-being, and productivity.

sublevels.name: Team Coaching
sublevels.description: Team coaching and management is a field within human resource management that focuses on improving team performance through coaching and training interventions. It involves using coaching techniques to identify and develop team members' strengths and areas for improvement, as well as improving communication and collaboration within the team.  Topics within team coaching and management may include:  Team building Group dynamics Conflict resolution Communication skills Leadership development Performance management Organizational culture Change management Research in this field may explore the impact of team coaching and management on team performance, as well as the effectiveness of different coaching techniques and interventions. It may also examine the role of team coaching and management in promoting employee engagement, retention, and job satisfaction.

sublevels.name: Unemployment
sublevels.description: Unemployment, in the field of psychology, refers to the state of being without a paid job or occupation, despite actively seeking employment. It is a complex socio-economic phenomenon that can have significant psychological effects on individuals, including feelings of stress, anxiety, loss of self-esteem, and reduced well-being. Psychological research on unemployment explores the impact on mental health, coping strategies, job-seeking behaviors, and interventions to support individuals during this challenging period.

sublevels.name: Psychology of Aesthetics
sublevels.description: The psychology of aesthetics is a subfield of psychology that focuses on the study of the cognitive, emotional, and perceptual processes underlying people's aesthetic experiences and preferences. It involves the investigation of how individuals perceive, evaluate, and respond to a wide range of artistic stimuli, including visual, auditory, and other sensory forms of art. The psychology of aesthetics seeks to understand the psychological mechanisms that underlie the creation, production, and consumption of art, as well as the factors that influence individual differences in aesthetic preferences and judgments.

sublevels.name: Media Psychology
sublevels.description: Media psychology is an interdisciplinary subfield of psychology that focuses on the study of the ways in which people interact with and are affected by various forms of media, including television, film, video games, social media, and the internet. It involves the application of psychological theories and methods to the study of media and its impact on individuals, groups, and society as a whole. The field of media psychology aims to understand how people perceive, process, and respond to media messages, how media influences attitudes and behaviors, and how media can be used to promote positive outcomes such as health, education, and social change.

sublevels.name: Cyberpsychology
sublevels.description: Cyberpsychology is a field of psychology that focuses on the study of human behavior and the psychological processes related to the use of technology and the internet. This includes examining how people interact with technology, how they perceive and process information online, and how online behavior and activities impact their psychological well-being. Cyberpsychology also explores the impact of technology and the internet on social and cultural dynamics, as well as ethical considerations related to the use of technology in various contexts. In essence, cyberpsychology seeks to understand the complex interplay between technology and the human mind and behavior.

sublevels.name: Internet Psychology
sublevels.description: Internet psychology is a field of study that focuses on the psychological aspects of online behavior and interactions, including social, cognitive, and emotional processes that occur in digital environments. It examines the ways in which people use the internet, how they perceive and experience online interactions, and the impact of technology on psychological processes and outcomes. Internet psychology draws on various disciplines such as psychology, computer science, sociology, and communication studies to understand topics such as online identity, cyberbullying, social media addiction, online privacy, online learning, and virtual communities. The field aims to inform the design and use of digital technologies, as well as to improve individuals' well-being and quality of life in the online world.

sublevels.name: Psychology of Religion and Spirituality
sublevels.description: The psychology of religion and spirituality is a subfield of psychology that explores the role of religious and spiritual beliefs, practices, and experiences in mental health and well-being. It examines the psychological aspects of religion and spirituality, including how they impact individuals' beliefs, attitudes, behaviors, and relationships. Additionally, it investigates the psychological and emotional effects of religious and spiritual practices, such as prayer, meditation, and mindfulness. The field also examines the cultural and social influences of religion and spirituality, including the role they play in identity formation, socialization, and community building. Finally, the psychology of religion and spirituality examines how religious and spiritual beliefs and practices can be integrated into psychological interventions and therapy.

sublevels.name: Pastoral Psychology
sublevels.description: Pastoral Psychology is a subfield of psychology that focuses on applying psychological principles and practices to spiritual and religious contexts, particularly within the Christian faith. It seeks to provide counseling and guidance to individuals who seek help in dealing with their spiritual and emotional struggles, and to aid them in finding meaning and purpose in their lives. Pastoral psychologists work closely with religious leaders and communities to understand their unique spiritual and psychological needs and provide appropriate support and care. Pastoral psychology draws on a range of psychological theories and techniques, as well as theological and philosophical perspectives, to help individuals achieve greater emotional, spiritual, and relational wellbeing.

sublevels.name: Counseling Psychology
sublevels.description: Counseling psychology is a general practice and health service provider specialty in professional psychology. It focuses on how people function both personally and in their relationships at all ages. Counseling psychology addresses the emotional, social, work, school and physical health concerns people may have at different stages in their lives, focusing on typical life stresses and more severe issues with which people may struggle as individuals and as a part of families, groups and organizations. Counseling psychologists help people with physical, emotional and mental health issues improve their sense of well?being, alleviate feelings of distress and resolve crises. They also provide assessment, diagnosis, and treatment of more severe psychological symptoms.

sublevels.name: Mediation and Conflict Management
sublevels.description: Mediation and conflict management in the field of psychology refer to a collaborative and structured process through which a neutral third-party mediator helps individuals, groups, or organizations to resolve disputes, negotiate agreements, and improve their communication and relationships.

sublevels.name: Coaching
