Engineers use the fundamental principles of mathematics, physics and chemistry to create machines that enable us to travel faster, provide improved medical care, and process more complicated information.

sublevels.name: Electrical and Electronic Engineering
sublevels.description: Electrical and electronic engineering is the branch of engineering that makes use of electricity. Electrical engineering concentrates on systems for generating and transmitting large electrical currents and converting them into other forms of energy, such as mechanical motion. Electronic engineering focusses on lower energy currents for processing and communicating information.

sublevels.name: Control, Robotics, Automation
sublevels.description: Automation is the technology by which a process or procedure is performed with minimum human assistance

sublevels.name: Control and Systems Theory
sublevels.description: Control and systems theory is a branch of engineering and mathematics that deals with the analysis, design, and control of dynamic systems. It provides a theoretical framework for understanding the behavior of systems, developing models, and designing control strategies to achieve desired system performance.

sublevels.name: Stochastic Systems and Control
sublevels.description: Stochastic control a sub field of control theory that deals with the existence of uncertainty either in observations or in the noise that drives the evolution of the system.

sublevels.name: Machine Learning
sublevels.description: Machine learning (ML) is the scientific study of algorithms and statistical models that computer systems use to progressively improve their performance on a specific task. Machine learning algorithms build a mathematical model of sample data, known as "training data", in order to make predictions or decisions without being explicitly programmed to perform the task. The study of mathematical optimization delivers methods, theory and application domains to the field of machine learning. In its application across business problems, machine learning is also referred to as predictive analytics

sublevels.name: Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
sublevels.description: Data mining is a field of study within machine learning, and focuses on exploratory data analysis through unsupervised learning. Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery are two closely related processes in the field of data science and data analysis. They involve extracting meaningful patterns, knowledge, and insights from large datasets to make informed decisions and discover valuable information.

sublevels.name: Automation
sublevels.description: Automation refers to the use of technology and machinery to perform tasks or processes with minimal human intervention. It involves the design, development, and implementation of systems that can operate independently, following predefined instructions or rules.

sublevels.name: Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
sublevels.description: Data mining is a field of study within machine learning, and focuses on exploratory data analysis through unsupervised learning. Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery are two closely related processes in the field of data science and data analysis. They involve extracting meaningful patterns, knowledge, and insights from large datasets to make informed decisions and discover valuable information.

sublevels.name: Automation
sublevels.description: Automation refers to the use of technology and machinery to perform tasks or processes with minimal human intervention. It involves the design, development, and implementation of systems that can operate independently, following predefined instructions or rules.

sublevels.name: System Robustness
sublevels.description: Robustness is the property of a system whose behaviour is relatively insensitive to perturbations either in its environment or in its components. There is often a trade-off between robustness and adaptability.

sublevels.name: Mechatronics
sublevels.description: A multidisciplinary field of engineering that includes a combination of mechanical engineering, robotics, electronics, computer engineering, telecommunications engineering, systems engineering and control engineering

sublevels.name: Robotic Engineering
sublevels.description: Robotics is a branch of mechanical engineering, electrical engineering and computer science that deals with the design, construction, operation, and application of robots, as well as computer systems for their control, sensory feedback, and information processing.

sublevels.name: Automation
sublevels.description: Automation refers to the use of technology and machinery to perform tasks or processes with minimal human intervention. It involves the design, development, and implementation of systems that can operate independently, following predefined instructions or rules.

sublevels.name: Microwaves, RF Engineering and Optical Communications
sublevels.description: Microwaves, RF Engineering, and Optical Communications are interconnected fields of study that deal with the transmission, modulation, and manipulation of electromagnetic waves for various applications

sublevels.name: Communications Engineering
sublevels.description: Communications engineering focuses on  transmitting information efficiently and reliably. I tdeals with the design, development, and implementation of various communication systems, covering analog/digital transmission techniques, such as wireless systems, optical fiber, signal processing, modulation and coding.

sublevels.name: Internet of Things
sublevels.description: The Internet of things (IoT) is the network of physical devices, vehicles, home appliances, and other items embedded with electronics, software, sensors, actuators, and connectivity which enables these things to connect, collect and exchange data

sublevels.name: Computer Networks
sublevels.description: A computer network is a set of computers sharing resources located on or provided by network nodes. Computers use common communication protocols over digital interconnections to communicate with each other. These interconnections are made up of telecommunication network technologies based on physically wired, optical, and wireless radio-frequency methods that may be arranged in a variety of network topologies.

sublevels.name: Wireless and Mobile Communication
sublevels.description: Wireless communication involves the transmission of information over a distance without the help of wires, cables or any other forms of electrical conductors. Mobile Communication is the technology that allows us to communicate with others in different locations without the use of any physical connection (wires or cables).

sublevels.name: Electrical Power Engineering
sublevels.description: generation, transmission, distribution, and utilization of electrical power. It involves the study and application of electrical and electromechanical devices, systems, and networks to ensure the reliable and efficient supply of electricity.

sublevels.name: Energy Grids and Networks
sublevels.description: Energy grids and networks, also known as power grids or electrical grids, refer to the interconnected systems of power generation, transmission, and distribution that deliver electricity from power plants to consumers. These grids and networks enable the efficient and reliable supply of electricity to homes, businesses, and industries

sublevels.name: Electrical Machines
sublevels.description: In electrical engineering, electric machine is a general term for machines using electromagnetic forces, such as electric motors, electric generators, and others. They are electromechanical energy converters: an electric motor converts electricity to mechanical power while an electric generator converts mechanical power to electricity. The moving parts in a machine can be rotating (rotating machines) or linear (linear machines). Besides motors and generators, a third category often included is transformers, which although they do not have any moving parts are also energy converters, changing the voltage level of an alternating current

sublevels.name: Power Electronics
sublevels.description: Power electronics is the application of electronics to the control and conversion of electric power.

sublevels.name: Photovoltaics
sublevels.description: Solar energy and photovoltaic technology is the study of using light from the sun as a source of energy, and the design and fabrication of devices for harnessing this potential. This involves collecting solar radiation for converting to both electricity and heat. Solar energy is carbon-free and renewable.

sublevels.name: Electronics and Microelectronics, Instrumentation
sublevels.description: Electronics and Microelectronics comprise the physics, engineering, technology and applications that deal with the emission, flow and control of electrons in vacuum and matter. They deal with electrical circuits that involve active electrical components such as vacuum tubes, transistors, diodes, integrated circuits, optoelectronics, and sensors, associated passive electrical components, and interconnection technologies.

sublevels.name: Electronic Circuits and Systems
sublevels.description: design, analysis, and implementation of electronic circuits and systems. It involves the study of electronic components, devices, and their interconnections to create functional circuits for various applications.

sublevels.name: Electronics Design and Verification
sublevels.description: Electronics design and verification refer to the processes involved in creating and validating electronic systems, circuits, and components. These processes ensure that the designed electronics meet the desired specifications, functionality, and performance requirements.

sublevels.name: Cyber-Physical Systems
sublevels.description: Embedded systems that are integrated with the Internet and its users. Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) refer to integrated systems where computational elements (cyber) and physical components are tightly interconnected and work together to perform various tasks. These systems combine the capabilities of both the cyber and physical worlds to achieve goals efficiently and effectively. CPS integrate physical processes with computing, communication, and control systems, creating a seamless interaction between the physical and digital domains.

sublevels.name: Embedded Systems
sublevels.description: A programmed controlling and operating system with a dedicated function within a larger mechanical or electrical system

sublevels.name: Signal, Speech, Image and Video Processing
sublevels.description: Signal, speech, image, and video processing is the field that analyzes, transforms, and interprets digital signals—from raw sensor data to human communication—using mathematical and computational methods to extract information, enhance quality, enable recognition, and support intelligent decision?making.

sublevels.name: Digital and Analog Signal Processing
sublevels.description: Digital signal processing (DSP) and analog signal processing are two approaches used to manipulate and process signals in various applications. Digital signal processing involves the manipulation and analysis of signals using digital techniques here analog signals are first converted into a discrete-time representation through a process called analog-to-digital conversion. While Analog signal processing, also known as continuous-time signal processing, involves the manipulation and analysis of signals using continuous or analog techniques here signals remain in their original continuous-time form and are processed using analog electronic circuits.

sublevels.name: Image Processing
sublevels.description: Image processing is manipulation of an image that has been digitised and uploaded into a computer. Software programs modify the image to make it more useful, and can for example be used to enable image recognition.

sublevels.name: Human-Machine Interfaces
sublevels.description: Human-machine interfaces (HMIs) refer to the technologies, systems, and interfaces that allow humans to interact and communicate with machines, computers, or electronic devices. HMIs enable users to control and interact with machines, provide input, receive feedback, and access information.

sublevels.name: Mechanical Engineering
sublevels.description: Mechanical engineering is the branch of engineering that deals with moving machines and their components. A central principle of mechanical engineering is the control of energy: transferring it from one form to another to suit a specific demand. Car engines, for example, convert chemical energy into kinetic energy. Sub-areas such as Process (Chemical) or Industrial Engineering have their roots in Mechanical Engineering.

sublevels.name: Industrial and Production Engineering
sublevels.description: optimization of complex systems, processes, and operations within industries and manufacturing settings

sublevels.name: Industrial Management
sublevels.description: Industrial management is a branch of engineering that deals with industrial design, construction, management, and application of science and engineering principles to improve the entire industrial infrastructure and industrial processes. Industrial Management focuses on the management of industrial processes.

sublevels.name: Engineering Economics
sublevels.description: Engineering economics, previously known as engineering economy, is a subset of economics concerned with the use and "...application of economic principles"[1] in the analysis of engineering decisions

sublevels.name: Logistics
sublevels.description: Logistics is a critical part of supply chain management that involves the planning, implementation, and control of the movement and storage of goods, services, and related information between the point of origin and the point of consumption. In the context of management research, logistics involves the study of various strategies, techniques, and technologies that are used to ensure the efficient and effective flow of goods and services through the supply chain.  Logistics research may involve analyzing different transportation modes, such as air, sea, rail, or road, and evaluating the benefits and drawbacks of each for specific types of goods and services. It may also involve examining various distribution strategies, such as centralized, decentralized, or hybrid systems, and assessing the impact of these strategies on delivery times, inventory costs, and customer satisfaction.  Other areas of logistics research may include inventory management, warehouse design and operations, packaging and labeling, and reverse logistics, which involves the management of returned goods and waste. Overall, logistics research seeks to identify best practices and innovative solutions for optimizing the supply chain and improving organizational performance.

sublevels.name: Security Science and Technology
sublevels.description: Security science and technology refer to the interdisciplinary field that combines scientific principles, theories, and technologies to address security challenges and enhance security measures in various domains. It involves the application of scientific methods, engineering, and technological advancements to develop innovative solutions for preventing, detecting, mitigating, and responding to security threats and risks.

sublevels.name: Machines, Tools, Processes
sublevels.description: should be rephrased to the new term: Machines, Tools, Processes

sublevels.name: Textile Engineering
sublevels.description: Textile engineering is a popular field of engineering that deals with materials like cotton, fibers, yarns, and other materials used in clothing products and accessories. It is primarily concerned with the development and manufacture of textile fabric used in the apparel industry.

sublevels.name: Industrial Automation
sublevels.description: Industrial automation is the use of technologies such as computer software and robotics to control machinery and processes which replace human beings in performing specific functions. The functions are primarily centered on manufacturing, quality control and material handling processes.

sublevels.name: Process Engineering
sublevels.description: Process engineering focuses on the design, operation, control, optimization and intensification of chemical, physical, and biological processes

sublevels.name: Environmental Process Engineering
sublevels.description: Environmental process engineering, also known as environmental technology or environmental systems engineering, refers to the application of engineering principles and technologies to address environmental challenges and develop sustainable solutions. It involves the design, implementation, and optimization of processes and systems to manage and mitigate environmental issues, such as pollution control, waste treatment, water and air quality management, and sustainable resource utilization.

sublevels.name: Bioprocess Engineering
sublevels.description: Bioprocess engineering is a field of study that combines principles from engineering, biology, and chemistry to develop and optimize processes for the production of biological products, such as pharmaceuticals, biofuels, food, and chemicals. It involves the application of engineering principles and techniques to design, analyze, and control processes that use living cells or their components.

sublevels.name: Thermal Process Engineering
sublevels.description: Thermal engineering is a specialized sub-discipline of mechanical engineering that deals with the movement of heat energy and transfer. The energy can be transferred between two mediums or transformed into other forms of energy.

sublevels.name: Mechanical Process Engineering
sublevels.description: Mechanical process engineering refers to the application of mechanical engineering principles and techniques to the design, analysis, and optimization of industrial processes and systems. It involves the study and development of mechanical equipment, machinery, and systems used in various industries to transform raw materials, control processes, and produce desired products efficiently and reliably.

sublevels.name: Chemical Process Engineering
sublevels.description: Chemical Process Engineering deals with the design, optimization, and operation of industrial chemical processes. It focuses on the practical implementation of chemical transformations in manufacturing environments, emphasizing efficiency, scalability, and troubleshooting of production systems.

sublevels.name: Machinery and Machine Elements
sublevels.description: Machinery and Machine Elements refer to the components, systems, and mechanisms that make up machines and equipment. They play a crucial role in various industries and applications, providing the necessary functionality, motion, and force transmission

sublevels.name: Engineering Design
sublevels.description: Engineering Design refers to the process of creating and developing new products, systems, or structures that meet specific requirements and solve practical problems. It is a systematic approach that combines technical knowledge, creativity, and problem-solving skills to conceive, plan, and implement innovative solutions.

sublevels.name: Materials Engineering
sublevels.description: Materials Engineering includes the development, processing, characterization, and application of materials. It involves understanding the structure, properties, performance, and behavior of materials, and using this knowledge to design and optimize materials for specific applications.

sublevels.name: Metallurgy
sublevels.description: Metallurgy is the branch of science and engineering concerned with the properties of metals and their production, processing, and performance. It involves: Extracting metals from ores  Refining and alloying metals to achieve desired properties Shaping and treating metals through processes like casting, forging, rolling, and heat treatment Studying the structure and behavior of metals at the atomic and microscopic levels to improve strength, durability, corrosion resistance, etc.

sublevels.name: Mechanical Power Engineering
sublevels.description: Engineering focussed on developing power facilities.

sublevels.name: Power Stations
sublevels.description: A power station, also referred to as a power plant and sometimes generating station or generating plant, is an industrial facility for the generation of electric power.

sublevels.name: Mechanical and Thermal Energy Storage
sublevels.description: Thermo-mechanical energy storage systems are based on transformations between mechanical and thermal energy. Internally, thermal energy storage might be combined with mechanical energy storage. The storage components are combined with standard components such as heat exchangers, compressors or turbines.

sublevels.name: Nuclear Energy
sublevels.description: Nuclear energy is a form of energy released from the nucleus, the core of atoms, made up of protons and neutrons. This source of energy can be produced in two ways: fission – when nuclei of atoms split into several parts – or fusion – when nuclei fuse together.

sublevels.name: Fossil Fuel
sublevels.description: A fossil fuel is a hydrocarbon-containing material such as coal, oil, and natural gas, formed naturally in the Earth's crust from the remains of dead plants and animals that is extracted and burned as a fuel. Fossil fuels may be burned to provide heat for use directly, to power engines, or to generate electricity.

sublevels.name: Renewable Energy
sublevels.description: Renewable energy is energy that comes from sources that are readily replenishable on short-timescales. Examples of these are solar radiation, wind, and biomass.

sublevels.name: Wind Energy
sublevels.description: Wind power or wind energy describes the process by which the wind is used to generate mechanical power or electricity. This mechanical power can be used for specific tasks (such as grinding grain or pumping water) or a generator can convert this mechanical power into electricity.

sublevels.name: Geothermal Energy
sublevels.description: Geothermal energy is thermal energy extracted from the Earth's crust. It combines energy from the formation of the planet and from radioactive decay.

sublevels.name: Engineering Thermodynamics, Heat and Mass Transfer
sublevels.description: Engineering Thermodynamics, Heat Transfer, and Mass Transfer are three closely related fields in engineering that deal with the transfer and conversion of energy and matter in various systems. Engineering thermodynamics focuses on the application of thermodynamic principles to engineering systems, Heat transfer deals with the mechanisms and rates of thermal energy transfer between objects or regions, Mass transfer involves the transport of mass (e.g., gases, liquids, or solids) within or between phases.

sublevels.name: Vehicle Engineering
sublevels.description: Automotive/Vehicle engineering, along with aerospace engineering and naval architecture, is a branch of vehicle engineering, incorporating elements of mechanical, electrical, electronic, software, and safety engineering as applied to the design, manufacture and operation of motorcycles, automobiles, and trucks and their respective engineering subsystems.

sublevels.name: Aerospace Technology and Astronautics
sublevels.description: Aerospace engineering is the branch of engineering that designs and builds machines for flight. This includes craft used both inside (aeronautical engineering) and outside (astronautical engineering) the Earth’s atmosphere. Aerospace engineering combines an understanding of fluid dynamics, robust but lightweight materials and the chemistry and thermodynamics of engines.

sublevels.name: Engine Technology
sublevels.description: An engine is a machine designed to convert one form of energy into mechanical energy, in particular to propel vehicles.

sublevels.name: Automotive Engineering
sublevels.description: Design, manufacture and operation of motorcycles, automobiles, and trucks and their respective engineering subsystems

sublevels.name: Marine Engineering
sublevels.description: Marine engineering includes the engineering of boats, ships, and any other marine vessel or structure, as well as oceanographic engineering. Not to be confused with Offshore Engineering (Civil Engineering).

sublevels.name: Rail Vehicles
sublevels.description: Locomotives, railway cars and wagons, as well as combinations such as trains or trams, including monorails.

sublevels.name: Biological and Physical Engineering
sublevels.description: 1. Application of technology to biological systems 2. Creating technologies from biological methods

sublevels.name: Nanoengineering
sublevels.description: Nanoengineering is a discipline that focuses on the design, synthesis, manipulation, and application of materials and devices at the nanoscale level. It involves the use of nanotechnology principles to create functional structures and systems with unique properties and functionalities. Nanoengineering encompasses a wide range of scientific and engineering fields, including physics, chemistry, materials science, electrical engineering, and biomedical engineering.

sublevels.name: Photonics and Optical Engineering
sublevels.description: study, manipulation, and application of light and its properties. Photonics involves the generation, transmission, detection, and utilization of photons, while Optical Engineering encompasses the design, development, and optimization of optical systems and devices.

sublevels.name: Optical Metrology
sublevels.description: Optical metrology is using light to set the standards that define units of measurement and for other high-precision research. Optical clocks, for example, have the potential to define the unit of time — the second — to a more precise degree than is possible in the atomic clocks used at present.

sublevels.name: Laser Technology
sublevels.description: A laser is a device that emits light through a process of optical amplification based on the stimulated emission of electromagnetic radiation.

sublevels.name: Optofluidics
sublevels.description: Optofluidics is the use of light to control the flow of fluids, particularly at the micrometre scale. A notable application of this technology is in so-called lab-on-a-chip devices: miniature systems for analysing and sorting particles and cells. Optofluidics also uses liquids to guide the flow of light.

sublevels.name: Fibre Optics
sublevels.description: Fibre optics and optical communications is the use of thin strands of glass for sending information encoded into light over long distances. Total internal reflection prevents light inserted into one end of the fibre from escaping through the sides. Transferring information optically in this way enables much higher transmission rates than using an electrical signal..Optical fibres are flexible, transparent fibers made by drawing glass (silica) or plastic. They are used most often as a means to transmit light between the two ends of the fiber and find wide usage in fiber-optic communications, where they permit transmission over longer distances and at higher bandwidths than electrical cables. Fibers are used instead of metal wires because signals travel along them with less loss; in addition, fibers are immune to electromagnetic interference, a problem from which metal wires suffer excessively. Fibers are also used for illumination and imaging, and are often wrapped in bundles so they may be used to carry light into, or images out of confined spaces, as in the case of a fiberscope. Specially designed fibers are also used for a variety of other applications, some of them being fiber optic sensors and fiber lasers.

sublevels.name: Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering
sublevels.description: Application of engineering principles and design concepts to medicine and biology for healthcare purposes

sublevels.name: Neuroengineering
sublevels.description: Engineering techniques to understand, repair, replace, enhance, or otherwise exploit the properties of neural systems

sublevels.name: Bioinspired Technologies
sublevels.description: Development and application of technologies that are inspired by or mimic biological systems, processes, or principles found in nature

sublevels.name: Biomechanical Analysis and Modeling
sublevels.description: Biomechanical analysis and modeling involve studying the mechanical behavior and properties of biological systems, such as cells, tissues, organs, and organisms. These approaches combine principles of engineering, physics, and biology to understand how forces and mechanics influence biological structures and functions. Biomechanical analysis and modeling play a crucial role in various fields, including biomechanics, sports science, orthopedics, rehabilitation, and biomedical engineering.

sublevels.name: Mechanobiology
sublevels.description: Cell signalling is the mechanism by which stimuli are transmitted via a signalling cascade to effector molecules that orchestrate the appropriate response. Types of cell signalling pathways include checkpoint signalling, lipid signalling, growth signalling, nutrient signalling, insulin signalling, stress signalling, morphogen signalling, Hippo signalling, TOR signalling and integrin signalling.

sublevels.name: Mechanobiological Cell Signaling
sublevels.description: Cell signalling is the mechanism by which stimuli are transmitted via a signalling cascade to effector molecules that orchestrate the appropriate response. Types of cell signalling pathways include checkpoint signalling, lipid signalling, growth signalling, nutrient signalling, insulin signalling, stress signalling, morphogen signalling, Hippo signalling, TOR signalling and integrin signalling.

sublevels.name: Biomedical Devices and Instrumentation
sublevels.description: Biomedical devices and instrumentation refer to the tools, equipment, and systems used in the field of biomedical engineering and healthcare to diagnose, monitor, treat, or assist in the management of medical conditions. These devices and instruments are designed to interface with biological systems, provide accurate measurements, deliver therapeutic interventions, or aid in the analysis of biological samples.

sublevels.name: Medical Imaging
sublevels.description: Medical imaging is the technique and process of imaging the interior of a body for clinical analysis and medical intervention, as well as visual representation of the function of some organs or tissues (physiology). Medical imaging seeks to reveal internal structures hidden by the skin and bones, as well as to diagnose and treat disease. Medical imaging also establishes a database of normal anatomy and physiology to make it possible to identify abnormalities.  (Although imaging of removed organs and tissues can be performed for medical reasons, such procedures are usually considered part of pathology instead of medical imaging.)

sublevels.name: Radiography
sublevels.description: Radiography is the use of X-rays or gamma rays to examine non-uniformly composed material; images are recorded on a sensitized surface, such as photographic film or a digital detector. Medical radiography includes examination of any part of the body for diagnostic purposes, such as detecting fractures or a bowel obstruction.

sublevels.name: Tomography
sublevels.description: Tomography is a technique whereby a subject is imaged in 'slices' or sections. Typically the imaging modality is X-ray radiography, and the slices can be viewed separately or in combination. Except for health sciences and medicine the method is also used in other areas of science, such as archaeology, biology, atmospheric science, geophysics, oceanography, plasma physics, materials science and astrophysics.

sublevels.name: Nuclear Medicine
sublevels.description: Nuclear medicine is a specialized area of radiology that uses very small amounts of radioactive materials, or radiopharmaceuticals, to examine organ function and structure. Nuclear medicine imaging is a combination of many different disciplines. These include chemistry, physics, mathematics, computer technology, and medicine. This branch of radiology is often used to help diagnose and treat abnormalities very early in the progression of a disease, such as thyroid cancer.

sublevels.name: Medical and Health Technologies
sublevels.description: Health technology is defined as the "application of organized knowledge and skills in the form of devices, medicines, vaccines, procedures, and systems developed to solve a health problem and improve quality of lives". This includes pharmaceuticals, devices, procedures, and organizational systems used in the healthcare industry, as well as any technology, including medical devices, IT systems, algorithms, artificial intelligence (AI), cloud and blockchain, designed to support healthcare organizations.

sublevels.name: e-Health
sublevels.description: eHealth describes healthcare services which are supported by digital processes, communication or technology such as electronic prescribing, Telehealth, or Electronic Health Records.

sublevels.name: Rehabilitation Robotics
sublevels.description: Rehabilitation robotics is a field of research dedicated to understanding and augmenting rehabilitation through the application of robotic devices.

sublevels.name: Engineering Acoustics
sublevels.description: Engineering Acoustics, also known as Acoustical Engineering, is a branch of engineering that deals with the study, design, and application of sound and vibration in various engineering systems and environments. It involves the manipulation, control, and understanding of sound and vibration phenomena to achieve desired outcomes.

sublevels.name: Psychoacoustics
sublevels.description: Psychoacoustics is the branch of psychophysics involving the scientific study of sound perception and audiology—how human auditory system perceives various sounds. More specifically, it is the branch of science studying the psychological responses associated with sound (including noise, speech, and music). Psychoacoustics is an interdisciplinary field of many areas, including psychology, acoustics, electronic engineering, physics, biology, physiology, and computer science.

sublevels.name: Underwater Acoustics
sublevels.description: Underwater acoustics or hydroacoustics is the study of the propagation of sound in water and the interaction of the mechanical waves that constitute sound with the water, its contents and its boundaries. The water may be in the ocean, a lake, a river or a tank.

sublevels.name: Aeroacoustics
sublevels.description: Aeroacoustics is a branch of acoustics that studies noise generation via either turbulent fluid motion or aerodynamic forces interacting with surfaces. It is centrally concerned with the generation and propagation of sound through a fluid.

sublevels.name: Architectural Acoustics
sublevels.description: design, analysis, and optimization of sound within buildings and other architectural spaces. It involves the application of scientific principles and engineering techniques to create spaces that have desirable acoustic properties, such as appropriate sound insulation, noise control, and optimal sound quality for specific purposes.

sublevels.name: Electroacoustics
sublevels.description: The science of the interaction and interconversion of electric and acoustic phenomena. Electroacoustics refers to the study and application of the relationship between electrical signals and acoustic sound waves. It encompasses the science and technology of generating, processing, transmitting, and reproducing sound using electrical and electronic devices.

sublevels.name: Ultrasonics
sublevels.description: Ultasonics are technological methods utilizing ultrasound. Ultrasound is sound waves with frequencies higher than the upper audible limit of human hearing.

sublevels.name: Noise Control
sublevels.description: Noise control studies strategies to reduce noise pollution or to reduce the impact of that noise outdoors and indoors.

sublevels.name: Microsystems and MEMS
sublevels.description: miniaturized systems and devices that integrate mechanical, electrical, and sometimes optical components on a microscale. They involve the fabrication, design, and application of miniature systems and structures that can sense, control, and interact with the surrounding environment.

sublevels.name: Energy Harvesting
sublevels.description: Energy harvesting (also known as power harvesting or energy scavenging) is the process in which energy is captured from a system's environment and converted into usable electric power. It is the conversion of ambient energy present in the environment into electrical energy for use in powering autonomous electronic devices or circuits.

sublevels.name: Microfluidics
sublevels.description: Microfluidics is the engineering or use of devices that apply fluid flow to channels smaller than 1 millimetre in at least one dimension. Microfluidic devices can reduce reagent consumption, allow well controlled mixing and particle manipulation, integrate and automate multiple assays (known as lab-on-a-chip), and facilitate imaging and tracking.

sublevels.name: Civil Engineering
sublevels.description: Civil engineering is a professional engineering discipline that deals with the design, construction, and maintenance of the physical and naturally built environment, including works such as roads, bridges, canals, dams, airports, sewerage systems, pipelines, and railways

sublevels.name: Surveying
sublevels.description: Surveying or land surveying is the technique, profession, and science of determining the terrestrial or three-dimensional positions of points and the distances and angles between them

sublevels.name: Building Construction and Design
sublevels.description: Application of engineering principles and technology to building design and construction

sublevels.name: Mechanical Statics and Structures
sublevels.description: Mechanical statics and structures are branches of engineering that deal with the analysis and design of stationary structures and the equilibrium of forces acting on them. It is essential for designing and analyzing various engineering structures, including buildings, bridges, mechanical components, and industrial machinery.

sublevels.name: Light-weight Construction, Steel and Timber Construction
sublevels.description: Lightweight construction, steel construction, and timber construction are three different approaches to building structures that offer specific advantages and considerations. Lightweight construction involves the use of materials that are lighter in weight compared to traditional construction materials. These materials often include lightweight concrete, gypsum boards, and lightweight steel or aluminum framing systems. While Steel construction utilizes structural steel elements as the primary load-bearing components of the building.  It allows for the creation of large open spaces, offers design flexibility, and provides excellent fire resistance. And Timber construction involves the use of wood as the primary material for structural elements, such as beams, columns, and frames. Wood is a renewable resource, and timber construction offers advantages such as environmental sustainability, aesthetic appeal, and good thermal insulation.

sublevels.name: Solid Construction
sublevels.description: "Solid construction" refers to a construction technique or approach that emphasizes strength, stability, and durability in building structures. It typically involves using robust and sturdy materials, employing sound engineering principles, and following established construction practices to create buildings with a strong and long-lasting foundation.

sublevels.name: Sustainable Architecture/Green Buildings
sublevels.description: A green or sustainable building is a building that, because of its construction and features, can maintain or improve the quality of life of the environment in which it is located.

sublevels.name: Construction Management
sublevels.description: overseeing and managing all aspects of a construction project, from the initial planning and design phase to the final completion and delivery of the project. It involves coordinating various activities, resources, and stakeholders to ensure the successful execution of a construction project within defined constraints of time, cost, quality, and safety.

sublevels.name: Transportation Technology and Traffic Engineering
sublevels.description: design, operation, and management of transportation systems to facilitate the movement of people and goods efficiently and safely.

sublevels.name: Offshore Engineering
sublevels.description: design, construction, operation, and maintenance of structures and systems in offshore environments, typically in or near bodies of water. It involves the application of engineering principles to address the unique challenges and conditions presented by the offshore environment, such as strong waves, currents, corrosive seawater, and harsh weather conditions.

sublevels.name: Building Materials
sublevels.description: Building materials are substances or products used in the construction or renovation of structures such as houses, buildings, bridges, roads, and infrastructure projects. These materials serve various purposes, including providing structural support, insulation, protection from the elements, and aesthetic finishes.

sublevels.name: Concrete
sublevels.description: Concrete is a versatile construction material widely used in building and infrastructure projects. It is a composite material composed of cement, aggregates (such as sand and gravel or crushed stone), and water.

sublevels.name: Timber
sublevels.description: The term timber refers specifically to unprocessed wood fiber, such as cut logs or standing trees that have yet to be cut. Timbers are large squared lengths of wood used for building a house or a boat. In British English, timber is also used as a synonym for lumber.

sublevels.name: Steel, Light Metal
sublevels.description: Steel and light metals are two different categories of metals commonly used in various applications. Steel is an alloy primarily composed of iron and carbon, with the carbon content typically ranging between 0.2% and 2.1% by weight. Light metals refer to a group of metals with relatively low densities compared to steel and other heavy metals.

sublevels.name: Asphalt, Bitumen
sublevels.description: Asphalt and bitumen are related materials commonly used in the construction and maintenance of roads, pavements, and waterproofing applications. Asphalt is a mixture of aggregates (such as crushed stone, sand, or gravel) and a binder.  Bitumen is a generic term that refers to a group of highly viscous and sticky hydrocarbon materials. It is a naturally occurring substance derived from crude oil, coal, or natural deposits

sublevels.name: Building Repair and Maintenance
sublevels.description: Building repair and maintenance refer to the activities undertaken to keep a building in good condition, ensure its functionality, and address any issues that may arise. Regular maintenance and timely repairs are crucial for the longevity, safety, and efficiency of a building.

sublevels.name: Facility Management
sublevels.description: Facility Management, also known as Facilities Management, is a multidisciplinary field that involves the management and maintenance of buildings, facilities, and infrastructure to ensure their efficient and effective operation. It encompasses a range of activities aimed at optimizing the functionality, sustainability, and usability of physical assets.

sublevels.name: Fire Science, Hazard Control, Building Safety
sublevels.description: Fire Science, Hazard Control, and Building Safety are interconnected fields that focus on understanding and mitigating fire-related risks in buildings and other structures. They involve the study, prevention, and control of fires, as well as the implementation of safety measures to protect people and property.

sublevels.name: Building Law for Engineers and Architects
sublevels.description: Building laws and regulations play a crucial role in ensuring the safety, functionality, and compliance of structures designed and constructed by engineers and architects.

sublevels.name: Building Physics, HVAC
sublevels.description: Building physics is the scientific study of the physical behavior of buildings. It involves understanding and controlling the interactions between a building and its surrounding environment, including heat, air, moisture, and light. They are closely related fields that deal with the design, analysis, and optimization of buildings' thermal performance and indoor environmental quality.

sublevels.name: Environmental Civil Engineering
sublevels.description: Environmental Civil Engineering deals with the those aspects of the environment that are directly affecting Civil Engineering, i.e.soil, water, noise protection, waste. In contrast to Process Engineering (e.g. air treatment). (rephrased by MM).

sublevels.name: Disposal Technology and Management
sublevels.description: Disposal technology and management refer to the methods, techniques, and processes used for the safe and efficient disposal of various types of waste and the overall management of waste streams. It involves the planning, implementation, and monitoring of waste disposal practices to minimize environmental impact and protect human health.

sublevels.name: Soil and Water Protection
sublevels.description: Soil and Water Protection is the description of different techniques used for the conservation of soil and water. Structures for soil and water conservation can be fences, terraces, water harvesting, cut-off drains, and gully repair.

sublevels.name: Geotechnical Engineering
sublevels.description: Geotechnical engineering is an area of civil engineering that focuses on the engineering behaviour of earth materials. Using the principles of soil and rock mechanics, it applies knowledge from geology, geophysics, hydrology, and related fields. Typical projects include embankments, tunnels, levees, wharves, landfills, and other structures that are built in or supported by soil and rock.

sublevels.name: Soil and Rock Mechanics
sublevels.description: The subject soil and rock mechanics is the theoretical and applied science of the mechanical behavior of soils and rocks and their application.

sublevels.name: Hydraulic Engineering
sublevels.description: Concerned with the flow and conveyance of fluids, principally water and sewage. Includes the design of bridges, dams, channels, canals, and levees.

sublevels.name: Mining and Exploration
sublevels.description: Mining and exploration are two distinct yet interconnected processes involved in the extraction and discovery of mineral resources from the Earth's crust.

sublevels.name: Underground Engineering and Tunnel Construction
sublevels.description: Underground construction refers to the construction of underground tunnels, shafts, chambers, and passageways, it is also sometimes used to describe the portion of traditional construction that takes place below grade. The method of tunnel construction depends on such factors as the ground conditions, the ground water conditions, the length and diameter of the tunnel drive, the depth of the tunnel, the logistics of supporting the tunnel excavation, the final use and shape of the tunnel and appropriate risk management. Tunnel construction is a subset of underground construction. Underground construction and tunnel engineering is truly an interdisciplinary practice, involving knowledge and skills primarily in civil engineering, geological engineering and mining engineering and, to a lesser extent, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, geophysics, geology and others.

sublevels.name: Foundation Engineering
sublevels.description: Application of soil mechanics and rock mechanics  in the design of foundation elements of structures.

sublevels.name: Climate Engineering
sublevels.description: Climate Engineering (also called Geoengineering) involves deliberate and purposeful interventions with the aim of mitigating anthropogenic effects on the earth systems. It includes a wide array of technologies centered around, e.g. reflecting sunlight back into space (solar radiation management) or removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.

sublevels.name: Mathematical and Computational Engineering Applications
sublevels.description: Mathematical and Computational Engineering Applications refers to the use of mathematical modeling, analysis, and computational techniques to solve engineering problems and develop innovative solutions. It involves the application of mathematical methods, algorithms, and computer simulations to various branches of engineering, such as mechanical, civil, electrical, chemical, and aerospace engineering, among others.

sublevels.name: Engineering Mechanics
sublevels.description: Engineering Mechanics is a branch of engineering that applies principles of physics and mathematics to study and analyze the behavior of physical systems and structures. It focuses on understanding and predicting the response of objects and systems to external forces and loads.

sublevels.name: Engineering Fluid Dynamics
sublevels.description: The behavior, motion, and interactions of fluids (liquids and gases) in engineering applications. It encompasses the principles and techniques used to understand and predict fluid flow phenomena, such as pressure distribution, velocity profiles, turbulence, and fluid forces.

sublevels.name: Solid Mechanics
sublevels.description: new term from PMCs: "Continuum Mechanics & Mechanics of Materials" + "Structural Mechanics"

sublevels.name: Multibody Systems and Mechanical Vibrations
sublevels.description: Multibody Systems and Mechanical Vibrations are two related fields within the realm of mechanical engineering. Multibody systems involve the analysis and simulation of mechanical systems consisting of multiple interconnected bodies or bodies with multiple degrees of freedom. Mechanical vibrations deal with the study of oscillatory motions in mechanical systems. These vibrations occur when a system oscillates around an equilibrium position due to the application of external forces or disturbances.

sublevels.name: Applied Dynamical Systems
sublevels.description: Applied Dynamical Systems aims to analyze and understand the behavior of dynamical systems and apply this knowledge to real-world problems. It involves the use of mathematical techniques, computational simulations, and experimental observations to study the dynamics and predict the long-term behavior of systems in various scientific and engineering domains.

sublevels.name: Computational Intelligence
sublevels.description: Computational Intelligence is a subset of Artificial Intelligence (AI) based on Soft Computing techniques. Different to AI (with its foundations in Mathematics and Computer Science) its main roots are in Engineering (Fuzzy Logic, Evolutionary Computation) and Physics (Neural Networks).

sublevels.name: Data Engineering
sublevels.description: Data Engineering is the aspect of Data Science that focuses on practical applications of data collection and analysis. Methods used usullay belong to the spectrum of Computational Intelligence techniques.

sublevels.name: Engineering Mathematics
sublevels.description: Engineering Mathematics is a branch of mathematics that focuses on the application of mathematical principles, methods, and techniques to solve engineering problems. It provides the foundation for understanding and analyzing the mathematical aspects of engineering systems and phenomena.

data.name: Mathematics and Computing
data.description: Mathematics and computing is the study and analysis of abstract concepts, such as numbers and patterns. Mathematics is the language of choice for scientifically describing and modelling the universe and everything that happens within it. Computing enables these mathematical problems to be solved in an efficient and automated way.

sublevels.name: Mathematics
sublevels.description: Pure mathematics uses mathematics to explore abstract ideas, mathematics that does not necessarily describe a real physical system. This can include developing the fundamental tools used by mathematicians, such as algebra and calculus, describing multi-dimensional space, or better understanding the philosophical meaning of mathematics and numbers themselves.

sublevels.name: Probability Theory
sublevels.description: Probability theory is the branch of mathematics concerned with probability. It treats the concept in a rigorous mathematical manner by expressing it through a set of axioms. Typically these axioms formalise probability in terms of a probability space, which assigns a measure taking values between 0 and 1, termed the probability measure, to a set of outcomes called the sample space. Any specified subset of these outcomes is called an event.In probability theory a stochastic or random process is a mathematical object usually defined as a collection of random variables. Historically the random variables were associated with or indexed by a set of numbers, usually viewed as points in time, giving the interpretation of a stochastic process representing numerical values of some system randomly changing over time. Stochastic processes are widely used as mathematical models of systems and phenomena that appear to vary in a random manner. They have applications in many disciplines

sublevels.name: Markov Process
sublevels.description: Markov processes are stochastic processes, traditionally in discrete or continuous time, that have the Markov property, which means the next value of the Markov process depends on the current value, but it is conditionally independent of the previous values of the stochastic process. In other words, the behavior of the process in the future is stochastically independent of its behavior in the past, given the current state of the process. Markov processes form an important class of stochastic processes and have applications in many areas

sublevels.name: Applied Probability
sublevels.description: Applied probability is the application of probability theory to statistical problems and other scientific and engineering domains

sublevels.name: Ecological Modelling
sublevels.description: Ecological modelling is the construction and analysis of mathematical models of ecological processes, including both purely biological and combined biophysical models. Models can be analytic or simulation-based and are used to understand complex ecological processes and predict how real ecosystems might change.

sublevels.name: Sustainability
sublevels.description: Sustainability is essentially the ability to endure, for example by exploiting resources in a way that does not deplete their future availability or unduly damage the wider environment. This concept has been incorporated in the idea of sustainable development.

sublevels.name: Queueing Theory
sublevels.description: Queueing theory is a field of management research and practice that focuses on the study of waiting lines, or queues, and the mathematical models used to analyze them. The goal of queueing theory is to understand the behavior of queues, how to design systems that minimize wait times and improve efficiency, and how to make informed decisions regarding system improvements and resource allocation.  Queueing theory considers various factors that impact queue performance, such as the arrival rate of customers or requests, the service rate of the system, the number of servers or service points available, and the behavior of customers while they wait. By analyzing these factors, queueing theory provides managers and analysts with the tools to optimize system performance, identify bottlenecks, and evaluate system trade-offs.  Queueing theory has broad applications in many fields, including telecommunications, transportation, healthcare, finance, and manufacturing. It is used to design call centers, hospitals, factories, and other systems that require efficient resource utilization and customer service. In addition, queueing theory is also used to study the behavior of customers and employees, providing insights into their decision-making processes and the factors that influence their behavior.

sublevels.name: Probability and Statistics in Computer Science
sublevels.description: Probability and Statistics for Computer Science treats the most common discrete and continuous distributions, showing how they find use in decision and estimation problems, and constructs computer algorithms for generating observations from the various distributions.

sublevels.name: Biostatistics
sublevels.description: Biostatistics is the application of statistical methods in studies in life and health sciences, and encompasses the design of experiments, the collection of data from them, and the analysis and interpretation of data. The data come from a wide range of sources, including genomic studies, experiments with cells and organisms, and clinical trials.

sublevels.name: Mathematical Statistics
sublevels.description: Mathematical statistics is the application of probability theory, a branch of mathematics, to statistics, as opposed to techniques for collecting statistical data. Specific mathematical techniques which are used for this include mathematical analysis, linear algebra, stochastic analysis, differential equations, and measure theory

sublevels.name: Stochastic Analysis
sublevels.description: In probability theory and related fields, stochastic analysis encompasses the mathermatical tools to study stochastic processes. These mathematical objects are usually defined as a sequence of random variables, where the index of the sequence has the interpretation of time or space.

sublevels.name: Stochastic Calculus
sublevels.description: Stochastic calculus is a branch of mathematics that operates on stochastic processes. It allows a consistent theory of integration to be defined for integrals of stochastic processes with respect to stochastic processes. It is used to model systems that behave randomly

sublevels.name: Distribution Theory
sublevels.description: possible values and probabilities for a random variable within a given range

sublevels.name: Multivariate Analysis
sublevels.description: involves evaluating multiple variables (more than two) to identify any possible association among them

sublevels.name: Stochastic Processes
sublevels.description: In probability theory and related fields, a stochastic or random process is a mathematical object usually defined as a collection of random variables

sublevels.name: Stochastic Systems and Control
sublevels.description: Stochastic control a sub field of control theory that deals with the existence of uncertainty either in observations or in the noise that drives the evolution of the system.

sublevels.name: Machine Learning
sublevels.description: Machine learning (ML) is the scientific study of algorithms and statistical models that computer systems use to progressively improve their performance on a specific task. Machine learning algorithms build a mathematical model of sample data, known as "training data", in order to make predictions or decisions without being explicitly programmed to perform the task. The study of mathematical optimization delivers methods, theory and application domains to the field of machine learning. In its application across business problems, machine learning is also referred to as predictive analytics

sublevels.name: Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
sublevels.description: Data mining is a field of study within machine learning, and focuses on exploratory data analysis through unsupervised learning. Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery are two closely related processes in the field of data science and data analysis. They involve extracting meaningful patterns, knowledge, and insights from large datasets to make informed decisions and discover valuable information.

sublevels.name: Automation
sublevels.description: Automation refers to the use of technology and machinery to perform tasks or processes with minimal human intervention. It involves the design, development, and implementation of systems that can operate independently, following predefined instructions or rules.

sublevels.name: Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
sublevels.description: Data mining is a field of study within machine learning, and focuses on exploratory data analysis through unsupervised learning. Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery are two closely related processes in the field of data science and data analysis. They involve extracting meaningful patterns, knowledge, and insights from large datasets to make informed decisions and discover valuable information.

sublevels.name: Automation
sublevels.description: Automation refers to the use of technology and machinery to perform tasks or processes with minimal human intervention. It involves the design, development, and implementation of systems that can operate independently, following predefined instructions or rules.

sublevels.name: Stochastic Modelling
sublevels.description: "Stochastic" means being or having a random variable. Stochastic modelling is the development of mathematical models for non-deterministic physical systems, which can adopt many possible behaviours starting from any given initial condition. Monte-Carlo simulations, for example, consist of exploring the various possible states of a complex probabilistic system. A stochastic model is a tool for estimating probability distributions of potential outcomes by allowing for random variation in one or more inputs over time. through random sampling of initial conditions and repeated computer simulations.

sublevels.name: Stochastic Networks
sublevels.description: The analysis of stochastic networks and their applications includes modelling, stability analysis, control, performance analysis and design of stochastic networks. Such analysis requires the bringing together of ideas and methodologies from a range of mathematical disciplines, including applied probability, stochastic processes, operational research, combinatorics and graph theory. Stochastic networks are networks that vary over time with non-binary vertices that represent a probability for a link between two nodes. Statistical approaches or computer simulations are often necessary to explore how such networks evolve, adapt or respond to external intervention

sublevels.name: Machine Learning
sublevels.description: Machine learning (ML) is the scientific study of algorithms and statistical models that computer systems use to progressively improve their performance on a specific task. Machine learning algorithms build a mathematical model of sample data, known as "training data", in order to make predictions or decisions without being explicitly programmed to perform the task. The study of mathematical optimization delivers methods, theory and application domains to the field of machine learning. In its application across business problems, machine learning is also referred to as predictive analytics

sublevels.name: Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
sublevels.description: Data mining is a field of study within machine learning, and focuses on exploratory data analysis through unsupervised learning. Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery are two closely related processes in the field of data science and data analysis. They involve extracting meaningful patterns, knowledge, and insights from large datasets to make informed decisions and discover valuable information.

sublevels.name: Automation
sublevels.description: Automation refers to the use of technology and machinery to perform tasks or processes with minimal human intervention. It involves the design, development, and implementation of systems that can operate independently, following predefined instructions or rules.

sublevels.name: Graph Theory in Probability
sublevels.description: probability distributions over graphs can be also referred as random graph. OR The application of graph theory concepts and techniques to analyze probabilistic systems and phenomena. It involves using graph representations to model and study probabilistic events, random processes, and their interconnections.

sublevels.name: Bayesian Network
sublevels.description: A Bayesian network, belief network or directed acyclic graphical model is a probabilistic graphical model that represents a set of random variables and their conditional independence with a directed acyclic graph (DAG). For example, a Bayesian network could represent the probabilistic relationships between diseases and symptoms.

sublevels.name: Computational Mathematics and Numerical Analysis
sublevels.description: Computational mathematics and numerical analysis are branches of mathematics that focus on developing and implementing algorithms and numerical methods to solve mathematical problems using computers. These fields play a crucial role in scientific and engineering applications where analytical solutions may be difficult or impossible to obtain.

sublevels.name: Mathematical Modeling and Industrial Mathematics
sublevels.description: Industrial mathematics is a branch of applied mathematics. It focusses on problems which come from industry and aims for solutions which are relevant to industry, including finding the most efficient (i.e., cost-effective) way to solve the problem. A mathematical model is a description of a system using mathematical concepts and language. The process of developing a mathematical model is termed mathematical modeling. Mathematical models are used in the natural sciences and engineering disciplines

sublevels.name: Numerical Analysis
sublevels.description: Numerical analysis is the study of algorithms that use numerical approximation (as opposed to general symbolic manipulations) for the problems of mathematical analysis (as distinguished from discrete mathematics). Numerical analysis naturally finds application in all fields of engineering and the physical sciences, but in the 21st century also the life sciences, social sciences, medicine, business and even the arts have adopted elements of scientific computations

sublevels.name: Computational Science and Engineering
sublevels.description: Computational science and engineering (CSE) deals with the development and application of computational models and simulations, often coupled with high-performance computing, to solve complex physical problems arising in engineering analysis and design (computational engineering) as well as natural phenomena (computational science).

sublevels.name: Computational Neuroscience
sublevels.description: Computational neuroscience includes both the study of the information processing functions of the nervous system, and the use of digital computers to study the nervous system. It is an interdisciplinary science that links the diverse fields of neuroscience, cognitive science and psychology, electrical engineering, computer science, physics and mathematics. Computational neuroscience is the field of study in which mathematical tools and theories are used to investigate brain function. It can also incorporate diverse approaches from electrical engineering, computer science and physics in order to understand how the nervous system processes information.

sublevels.name: Dynamical Systems
sublevels.description: Dynamical systems describe an ensemble of particles whose state varies over time and thus obeys differential equations involving time derivatives. In order to make a prediction about the system’s future behavior, an analytical solution of such equations or their integration over time through computer simulation is realized..In mathematics dynamical systems refer to dynamical systems theory, an area of mathematics used to describe the behavior of the complex dynamical systems, usually by employing differential equations or difference equations. This theory deals with the long-term qualitative behavior of dynamical systems, and studies the nature of, and when possible the solutions of, the equations of motion of systems that are often primarily mechanical or otherwise physical in nature, such as planetary orbits and the behaviour of electronic circuits, as well as systems that arise in biology, economics, and elsewhere. Much of modern research is focused on the study of chaotic systems

sublevels.name: Time Series Analysis
sublevels.description: A time series is a sequence of measurements performed at successive points in time. Time series can be used to derive models to predict future values based on previously observed values. Time series are used in statistics, signal processing, pattern recognition, econometrics, mathematical finance, weather forecasting, earthquake prediction, electroencephalography, control engineering, astronomy, communications engineering, and largely in any domain of applied science and engineering which involves temporal measurements

sublevels.name: Algorithms
sublevels.description: In mathematics and computer science, an algorithm is an unambiguous specification of how to solve a class of problems. Algorithms can perform calculation, data processing, and automated reasoning tasks.

sublevels.name: Mathematical Software
sublevels.description: Mathematical software is software used to model, analyze or calculate numeric, symbolic or geometric data.

sublevels.name: Quantum Computing
sublevels.description: Quantum computing is computing using quantum-mechanical phenomena, such as superposition and entanglement. The relative device is called quantum computer.

sublevels.name: Data and Information Visualization
sublevels.description: Data and information visualization is the practice of designing graphic or visual representations of otherwise difficult-to-understand information. It helps to understand, communicate and explore a certain field of expertise or study or other structures or correlations. It is not primarily used for imaging scientific findings, but to facilitate the comprehension and communication of these findings.

sublevels.name: Applications of Mathematics
sublevels.description: practical utilization of mathematical concepts, techniques, and tools to solve real-world problems and address various fields of study. Mathematics has wide-ranging applications in numerous disciplines, including science, engineering, finance, computer science, economics, statistics, and many others

sublevels.name: Computational Biology
sublevels.description: Computational biology, which includes many aspects of bioinformatics, is the science of using biological data to develop algorithms or models in order to understand biological systems and relationships.

sublevels.name: Population Genetics
sublevels.description: Population genetics is a subfield of genetics that deals with genetic differences within and between populations, and is a part of evolutionary biology. Studies in this branch of biology examine such phenomena as adaptation, speciation, and population structure. Traditionally a highly mathematical discipline, modern population genetics encompasses theoretical, lab, and field work. Population genetic models are used both for statistical inference from DNA sequence data and for proof/disproof of concept.Population genetics is the study of genetic variation within populations, and involves the examination and modelling of changes in the frequencies of genes and alleles in populations over space and time. (University of Leicester).Population genetics is the study of the genetic composition of populations, including distributions and changes in genotype and phenotype frequency in response to the processes of natural selection, genetic drift, mutation and gene flow.

sublevels.name: Computational Neuroscience
sublevels.description: Computational neuroscience includes both the study of the information processing functions of the nervous system, and the use of digital computers to study the nervous system. It is an interdisciplinary science that links the diverse fields of neuroscience, cognitive science and psychology, electrical engineering, computer science, physics and mathematics. Computational neuroscience is the field of study in which mathematical tools and theories are used to investigate brain function. It can also incorporate diverse approaches from electrical engineering, computer science and physics in order to understand how the nervous system processes information.

Stochastic networks are networks that vary over time with non-binary vertices that represent a probability for a link between two nodes. Statistical approaches or computer simulations are often necessary to explore how such networks evolve, adapt or respond to external intervention

sublevels.name: Medical Imaging
sublevels.description: Medical imaging is the technique and process of imaging the interior of a body for clinical analysis and medical intervention, as well as visual representation of the function of some organs or tissues (physiology). Medical imaging seeks to reveal internal structures hidden by the skin and bones, as well as to diagnose and treat disease. Medical imaging also establishes a database of normal anatomy and physiology to make it possible to identify abnormalities.  (Although imaging of removed organs and tissues can be performed for medical reasons, such procedures are usually considered part of pathology instead of medical imaging.)

sublevels.name: Radiography
sublevels.description: Radiography is the use of X-rays or gamma rays to examine non-uniformly composed material; images are recorded on a sensitized surface, such as photographic film or a digital detector. Medical radiography includes examination of any part of the body for diagnostic purposes, such as detecting fractures or a bowel obstruction.

sublevels.name: Tomography
sublevels.description: Tomography is a technique whereby a subject is imaged in 'slices' or sections. Typically the imaging modality is X-ray radiography, and the slices can be viewed separately or in combination. Except for health sciences and medicine the method is also used in other areas of science, such as archaeology, biology, atmospheric science, geophysics, oceanography, plasma physics, materials science and astrophysics.

sublevels.name: Nuclear Medicine
sublevels.description: Nuclear medicine is a specialized area of radiology that uses very small amounts of radioactive materials, or radiopharmaceuticals, to examine organ function and structure. Nuclear medicine imaging is a combination of many different disciplines. These include chemistry, physics, mathematics, computer technology, and medicine. This branch of radiology is often used to help diagnose and treat abnormalities very early in the progression of a disease, such as thyroid cancer.

sublevels.name: Population Dynamics
sublevels.description: Population dynamics is the branch of life sciences that studies the size and age composition of populations as dynamical systems, and the biological and environmental processes driving them. It is the study of how and why populations change in size and structure over time. Important factors in population dynamics include rates of reproduction, death and migration. Population dynamics has traditionally been the dominant branch of mathematical biology

sublevels.name: Signal, Speech, Image and Video Processing
sublevels.description: Signal, speech, image, and video processing is the field that analyzes, transforms, and interprets digital signals—from raw sensor data to human communication—using mathematical and computational methods to extract information, enhance quality, enable recognition, and support intelligent decision?making.

sublevels.name: Digital and Analog Signal Processing
sublevels.description: Digital signal processing (DSP) and analog signal processing are two approaches used to manipulate and process signals in various applications. Digital signal processing involves the manipulation and analysis of signals using digital techniques here analog signals are first converted into a discrete-time representation through a process called analog-to-digital conversion. While Analog signal processing, also known as continuous-time signal processing, involves the manipulation and analysis of signals using continuous or analog techniques here signals remain in their original continuous-time form and are processed using analog electronic circuits.

sublevels.name: Image Processing
sublevels.description: Image processing is manipulation of an image that has been digitised and uploaded into a computer. Software programs modify the image to make it more useful, and can for example be used to enable image recognition.

sublevels.name: Human-Machine Interfaces
sublevels.description: Human-machine interfaces (HMIs) refer to the technologies, systems, and interfaces that allow humans to interact and communicate with machines, computers, or electronic devices. HMIs enable users to control and interact with machines, provide input, receive feedback, and access information.

sublevels.name: Signal Transduction

HMIs enable users to control and interact with machines, provide input, receive feedback, and access information.

sublevels.name: Biostatistics
sublevels.description: Biostatistics is the application of statistical methods in studies in life and health sciences, and encompasses the design of experiments, the collection of data from them, and the analysis and interpretation of data. The data come from a wide range of sources, including genomic studies, experiments with cells and organisms, and clinical trials.

sublevels.name: Actuarial Mathematics
sublevels.description: Actuarial science is the discipline that applies mathematical and statistical methods to assess risk in insurance, finance and other industries and professions. Actuarial Mathematics refers to research for these mathematical methods

sublevels.name: Insurance
sublevels.description: The insurance industry is a field of business and management research that focuses on the study of the insurance sector. This includes the analysis of various types of insurance products such as life insurance, health insurance, property and casualty insurance, and other specialized insurance products. Research in this field covers a range of topics, including the regulation of the industry, risk management, underwriting, claims processing, and actuarial science. Additionally, research may examine the impact of emerging technologies on the industry, the use of big data and analytics, and the role of insurance in broader economic and social contexts.

sublevels.name: Investments and Securities
sublevels.description: The Investments and Securities industry is a field of business and management research that focuses on the analysis, management, and trading of financial instruments such as stocks, bonds, options, and other securities. The field encompasses a wide range of topics, including portfolio management, risk management, financial analysis, asset pricing, trading strategies, and market microstructure. It involves understanding the behavior of financial markets and the factors that influence their movements, as well as developing models and tools to help investors make informed decisions about their investments. Research in this field often involves the use of quantitative methods and may draw upon insights from economics, finance, and mathematics.

sublevels.name: Mathematics of Planet Earth
