Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery are two closely related processes in the field of data science and data analysis. They involve extracting meaningful patterns, knowledge, and insights from large datasets to make informed decisions and discover valuable information.

sublevels.name: Theory of Computation
sublevels.description: Theory of computation (TOC) is concerned with how problems can be solved using algorithms and how efficiently they can be solved.

sublevels.name: Computer Science Logic and Foundations of Programming
sublevels.description: Includes verification, temporal logic, automated reasoning, logic programming, description logics, finite model theory, programming logic, model checking, formal methods, type systems, algebraic semantics, categorical semantics, program analysis, program verification, abstraction

sublevels.name: Computational Complexity
sublevels.description: Computational comlexity studies the minimal resources required to solve a computational problem, It includes complexity classes, proof complexity, interactive proof systems. It deals with the study of the resources required to solve computational problems. Computational complexity provides valuable insights into the inherent difficulty of problems and helps classify them based on their tractability or intractability.

sublevels.name: Models of Computation
sublevels.description: Includes computability, concurrency, hybrid models, abstract machines, quantum computing, abstract machines. Models of Computation refer to abstract, mathematical, or theoretical frameworks used to study the capabilities and limitations of computation. These models help computer scientists and mathematicians analyze and understand different computational problems and algorithms in a formal and rigorous manner.

sublevels.name: Quantum Computing
sublevels.description: Quantum computing is computing using quantum-mechanical phenomena, such as superposition and entanglement. The relative device is called quantum computer.

sublevels.name: Theory and Algorithms for Application Domains
sublevels.description: Includes machine learning theory (models of learning, reinforcement learning, Markov decision processes, inductive inference, online learning theory, support vector machines), algorithmic game theory and mechanism design (market equilibria, network games, auctions), theory of random search heuristics

sublevels.name: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
sublevels.description: Includes graph algorithms, approximation algorithms, mathematical optimization, online algorithms, parameterized complexity, streaming algorithms, parallel algorithms, distributed algorithms, design and analysis of data structures (data compression, pattern matching, sorting, searching), algorithm design techniques

sublevels.name: Information Model
sublevels.description: An information model in software engineering is a representation of concepts and the relationships, constraints, rules, and operations to specify data semantics for a chosen domain of discourse.

sublevels.name: Formal Languages and Automata Theory
sublevels.description: Includes grammars and context-free languages, tree languages, formalisms. It studies the formal languages and abstract machines used to describe and recognize patterns and structures in strings and sequences. It  have practical applications in various areas of computer science, including compiler design, programming language design, parsing, pattern matching, and natural language processing

sublevels.name: Computational Geometry
sublevels.description: Computational geometry is a branch of computer science devoted to the study of algorithms which can be stated in terms of geometry

sublevels.name: Theoretical Computer Science
sublevels.description: Theoretical computer science or TCS studies the fundamental mathematical principles of computation, the .mathematical principles, theories, and techniques. It encompasses the mathematical foundations of algorithms, data structures, computational models, and computational complexity.

sublevels.name: Coding and Information Theory
sublevels.description: Coding and information theory are closely related fields within computer science and mathematics. Coding theory deals with the design and analysis of error-correcting codes, which are used to transmit data reliably over noisy channels. Information theory, on the other hand, focuses on quantifying and measuring information and communication.

sublevels.name: Symbolic and Algebraic Manipulation
sublevels.description: The study and development of algorithms and software for manipulating mathematical expressions and other mathematical objects.

sublevels.name: Discrete Mathematics in Computer Science
sublevels.description: Discrete mathematics plays a fundamental role in computer science. It provides the theoretical foundation and mathematical tools necessary for analyzing and solving problems in various areas of computer science, including algorithms, data structures, cryptography, logic, and computer networks

sublevels.name: Graph Theory
sublevels.description: In mathematics, graph theory is the study of graphs, which are mathematical structures used to model pairwise relations between objects. A graph in this context is made up of vertices, nodes, or points which are connected by edges, arcs, or lines

sublevels.name: Graph Theory in Probability
sublevels.description: probability distributions over graphs can be also referred as random graph. OR The application of graph theory concepts and techniques to analyze probabilistic systems and phenomena. It involves using graph representations to model and study probabilistic events, random processes, and their interconnections.

sublevels.name: Bayesian Network
sublevels.description: A Bayesian network, belief network or directed acyclic graphical model is a probabilistic graphical model that represents a set of random variables and their conditional independence with a directed acyclic graph (DAG). For example, a Bayesian network could represent the probabilistic relationships between diseases and symptoms.

sublevels.name: Probability and Statistics in Computer Science
sublevels.description: Probability and Statistics for Computer Science treats the most common discrete and continuous distributions, showing how they find use in decision and estimation problems, and constructs computer algorithms for generating observations from the various distributions.

sublevels.name: Computer and Information Systems Applications
sublevels.description: Computer and Information Systems Applications refer to the practical use and application of computer technology and information systems in various domains. It involves utilizing computer software, hardware, networks, and databases to solve problems, streamline processes, and support decision-making.

sublevels.name: Computer Application in Administrative Data Processing
sublevels.description: The use of computer systems and software to manage and process administrative data in various organizational settings. These applications streamline and automate administrative tasks, improving efficiency, accuracy, and data accessibility.

sublevels.name: Business Information Systems
sublevels.description: Business Information Systems (BIS) is a field of study that focuses on the effective and efficient use of technology and information systems to support the operations, management, and decision-making processes of businesses. BIS combines elements of computer science, management science, and business administration to develop and implement systems that improve business performance.  Some of the major topics in BIS include:  Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP): ERP systems integrate and automate key business processes, such as accounting, inventory management, and customer relationship management.  Customer Relationship Management (CRM): CRM systems are used to manage customer interactions and improve customer satisfaction and loyalty.  Supply Chain Management (SCM): SCM systems optimize the flow of materials, information, and finances across the supply chain to improve efficiency and reduce costs.  Business Intelligence and Analytics: BIS helps businesses to collect and analyze data to support decision-making processes.  E-commerce: E-commerce systems enable businesses to conduct transactions online and reach a global audience.  Knowledge Management: Knowledge management systems help businesses to capture, store, and share knowledge and expertise within the organization.  Cybersecurity: BIS focuses on the protection of business information systems from cyber threats, such as hacking and data breaches.  Overall, BIS aims to align technology with business goals and objectives to create a competitive advantage for the organization.

sublevels.name: Enterprise Architecture
sublevels.description: Enterprise Architecture (EA) is a field of business and management research and practice that focuses on the design and implementation of a coherent and integrated set of business and IT capabilities that support an organization's goals and objectives. It involves the development of a comprehensive understanding of an organization's current and desired states, and the identification of the gaps and opportunities for improvement.  The following are major topics within the field of Enterprise Architecture:  Business Architecture: Business Architecture defines the organization's business strategy, goals, processes, and organizational structure. It aims to provide a clear understanding of the organization's operations and how they can be optimized.  Information Architecture: Information Architecture defines the organization's information strategy, including the data, information, and knowledge assets required to support the business processes. It ensures that information is available, secure, and usable by the organization's stakeholders.  Application Architecture: Application Architecture focuses on the design and implementation of software applications that support the organization's business processes. It includes the development of application standards, guidelines, and best practices.  Technology Architecture: Technology Architecture defines the organization's technology strategy, including the hardware, software, and network infrastructure required to support the business processes. It ensures that the technology is aligned with the organization's goals and objectives.  Governance: Governance refers to the establishment of policies, standards, and procedures to ensure that the Enterprise Architecture is consistent with the organization's goals and objectives. It ensures that the organization's resources are used effectively and efficiently.  Change Management: Change Management refers to the process of managing the changes to the Enterprise Architecture. It involves the development of a plan to manage the implementation of new systems, applications, or processes, and the communication of the changes to stakeholders.  Risk Management: Risk Management involves identifying, assessing, and managing risks associated with the implementation of the Enterprise Architecture. It ensures that the organization's assets are protected and that the risks are managed effectively.  Overall, the goal of Enterprise Architecture is to provide a holistic and integrated view of the organization, its processes, and its resources.

sublevels.name: Business Process Management
sublevels.description: Business Process Management (BPM) is a discipline within the field of management and information technology that focuses on designing, modeling, executing, monitoring, and optimizing business processes. BPM seeks to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of business operations by aligning them with the strategic goals of an organization. Major topics within BPM include: Process modeling: This involves documenting and representing business processes using diagrams and other visual aids. Process modeling helps stakeholders to understand the flow of activities, inputs, and outputs in a process, and to identify potential bottlenecks and inefficiencies. Process automation: This involves using technology to automate routine or repetitive tasks within a process. Process automation can help to reduce errors, improve consistency, and free up human resources to focus on more complex or strategic activities. Process optimization: This involves identifying areas for improvement within a process and implementing changes to streamline and improve its performance. Process optimization can help to reduce costs, increase customer satisfaction, and improve overall business performance. Process monitoring: This involves tracking the performance of a process over time, using metrics and other indicators to identify trends and areas for improvement. Process monitoring can help to identify bottlenecks, inefficiencies, and other issues that may be affecting the performance of a process. Process governance: This involves establishing policies, procedures, and guidelines for the management of business processes within an organization. Process governance helps to ensure that processes are consistent, compliant, and aligned with the strategic goals of the organization. Process innovation: This involves exploring new and innovative ways to design, execute, and manage business processes. Process innovation can help to drive business growth, create competitive advantage, and improve overall organizational performance.

sublevels.name: Health Informatics
sublevels.description: Health informatics  is a multidisciplinary field that uses health information technology in delivery, management and planning  of health care services. It deals with the resources, devices, and methods required to optimize the acquisition, storage, retrieval, and use of information in health and bio-medicine.

sublevels.name: Geographical Information System
sublevels.description: A Geographic Information System (GIS) is a system designed to capture, store, manipulate, analyze, manage, and present spatial or geographic data. GIS applications are tools that allow users to create interactive queries (user-created searches), analyze spatial information, edit data in maps, and present the results of all these operations.

sublevels.name: Remote Sensing and Photogrammetry
sublevels.description: Remote sensing collects data in the form of light and color. By detecting different wavelengths of light radiation, it can generate maps. Instead of measuring wavelengths of radiation, on the other hand, photogrammetry uses imagery to measure coordinates in space. Photogrammetry is the science and technology of obtaining reliable information about physical objects and the environment through the process of recording, measuring and interpreting photographic images and patterns of electromagnetic radiant imagery and other phenomena.

sublevels.name: Computer-Aided Engineering (CAD, CAE) and Design
sublevels.description: Computer-aided engineering (CAE) is the broad usage of computer software to aid in engineering analysis tasks.  By simulating performance, product designs are improved and optimized. CAE primarily uses computer-aided design (CAD) next to computer-aided manufacturing (CAM). It is often summarized in the collective abbreviation "CAx".

sublevels.name: Computer Modelling
sublevels.description: Computer modelling consists of writing a computer program version of a mathematical model for a physical or biological system. Computer simulations that are run according to such programs can produce knowledge out of reach of mathematical analysis or natural experimentation. Computational models are mathematical models used to numerically study the behaviour of complex systems by means of a computer simulation. A computational model can be used to make predictions of the system's behaviour under different conditions, often for cases in which intuitive analytical solutions are not available.

sublevels.name: Building Information Modeling
sublevels.description: Meaning information modeling for buildings; used in architecture / civil engineering for maintaining and communicating information systems and data related to buildings

sublevels.name: Complex Systems
sublevels.description: Complex systems is a scientific field that studies the common properties of systems considered complex in nature, society, and science. It is also called complex systems theory, complexity science, study of complex systems and/or sciences of complexity. The key problems of such systems are difficulties with their formal modeling and simulation. From such perspective, in different research contexts complex systems are defined on the base of their different attributes. As an interdisciplinary domain, complex systems draws contributions from many different fields, such as the study of self-organization from physics, that of spontaneous order from the social sciences, chaos from mathematics, adaptation from biology, and many others

sublevels.name: Computational Social Sciences
sublevels.description: Computational social science refers to the academic sub-disciplines concerned with computational approaches used to model, simulate, and analyze social phenomena. It focuses on investigating social and behavioral relationships and interactions through social simulation, modeling, network analysis, and media analysis.Social Networks aim to analyze the structure of whole social entities as well as a variety of theories explaining the patterns observed in these structures. The study of these structures uses social network analysis to identify local and global patterns, locate influential entities, and examine network dynamics.

sublevels.name: Media Design
sublevels.description: A mixed discipline between design and information-development which is concerned with how media communicate with people.

sublevels.name: Digital Humanities
sublevels.description: e-Humanities, Computing in the Humanities or Digital Humanities means the systematic use of digital resources in the humanities, as well as the analysis of their application.

sublevels.name: User Interfaces and Human Computer Interaction
sublevels.description: Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) is an interdisciplinary domain that involves the development and deployment of technologies centered on users, the field emphasizes user experience and accessibility. Related topics include user research; interface design; human factors such as emotion; and human control mechanisms using speech, haptics, or gesture.

sublevels.name: Bioinformatics
sublevels.description: Bioinformatics involves using approaches from computer science and statistics to analyze biological data. Tools include pattern recognition, visualization, machine learning, and data mining, Application domains include genomics, proteomics, drug discovery, and systems biology.

sublevels.name: Product Design and Prototyping
sublevels.description: Product Design is the process of conceptualizing, designing, testing, and refining products,  digital services, or experiences to solve user problems

sublevels.name: Database Management System
sublevels.description: A Database Management System (DBMS) is software that enables the creation, organization, management, and retrieval of data from a database.

sublevels.name: Information Storage and Retrieval
sublevels.description: The process of storing and accessing information in a structured and efficient manner. It involves the organization, indexing, and retrieval of data and documents to meet users' information needs

sublevels.name: Database Management
sublevels.description: A database is one or more sets of data, for example numbers, characters and images, bundled together with software that enables data to be added, removed or retrieved. Databases can be used to store research data, for example in protein databases and genetic databases, and they organise data into standard formats so that information can readily be obtained.

sublevels.name: Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
sublevels.description: Data mining is a field of study within machine learning, and focuses on exploratory data analysis through unsupervised learning. Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery are two closely related processes in the field of data science and data analysis. They involve extracting meaningful patterns, knowledge, and insights from large datasets to make informed decisions and discover valuable information.

sublevels.name: Programming Language
sublevels.description: A programming language is a set of symbols whose strings are governed by rules apt to communicate instructions to a particular machine. Such strings may be concatenated into longer code and implement abstract algorithms in the form of programs specific to actual computing devices.

sublevels.name: Java
sublevels.description: Java is a high-level, class-based, object-oriented programming language that is designed to have as few implementation dependencies as possible. It is a general-purpose programming language intended to let programmers write once, run anywhere (WORA) meaning that compiled Java code can run on all platforms that support Java without the need to recompile.

sublevels.name: Python
sublevels.description: Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language. Its design philosophy emphasizes code readability with the use of significant indentation via the off-side rule

sublevels.name: C++
sublevels.description: C++ is a widely used programming language that is known for its versatility and efficiency. It is an extension of the C programming language and supports both procedural and object-oriented programming paradigms.

sublevels.name: Lisp
sublevels.description: Lisp programming language, Common Lisp. Lisp, short for "List Processing," is a high-level programming language known for its unique and distinctive syntax and its powerful support for symbolic data manipulation and functional programming.  It was designed to be a practical tool for artificial intelligence (AI) research, and its strong emphasis on symbolic computation and recursion made it an ideal choice for processing symbolic data and solving complex problems.

sublevels.name: Perl
sublevels.description: Perl is a high-level, general-purpose programming language known for its versatility, flexibility, and powerful text-processing capabilities. Perl stands for "Practical Extraction and Reporting Language," but it is also known as the "Pathologically Eclectic Rubbish Lister" due to its various and eclectic features.

sublevels.name: JavaScript
sublevels.description: JavaScript is a high-level, interpreted programming language primarily used to create interactive and dynamic content on websites. It runs in web browsers and enables features like animations, form validation, and real-time updates.

sublevels.name: Rust
sublevels.description: Rust is a general purpose programming language designed for safety, speed, and concurrency. It eliminates typical programming errors like memory leaks and data races.

sublevels.name: Computer Hardware
sublevels.description: Hardware refers to the external and internal devices and equipment that enables to perform major functions such as input, output, storage, communication, processing, and more.

sublevels.name: Logic Design
sublevels.description: Logic design is a field of engineering that focuses on the design and implementation of digital circuits and systems using logic gates and Boolean algebra. It involves the process of transforming a set of specifications or requirements into a logical representation that can be implemented using digital components and technologies.

sublevels.name: Control Structures and Microprogramming
sublevels.description: Control structures are programming constructs that enable the execution of different sections of code based on certain conditions or criteria. They determine the flow and order of program execution and allow for decision-making and repetition. While Microprogramming is a low-level design technique used in computer architecture to implement complex instructions and control the behavior of a processor. It involves breaking down complex instructions into a sequence of microinstructions that can be executed by the processor's control unit.

sublevels.name: Robotics
sublevels.description: Design of robots and the respective control systems, engineering, programming and teaching-in. study, design, and development of robots and autonomous systems. Robots are machines or mechanical devices that can perform tasks autonomously or semi-autonomously, either by following pre-programmed instructions or through artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms.

sublevels.name: Brain-machine Interface
sublevels.description: A brain–machine interface (BMI) is a device that translates neuronal information into commands capable of controlling external software or hardware such as a computer or robotic arm. BMIs are often used as assisted living devices for individuals with motor or sensory impairments.

sublevels.name: Computer Memory Structure
sublevels.description: The memory structure of a computer refers to those hardware elements that store the data elements and the related information during program execution

sublevels.name: Processor Architectures
sublevels.description: A processor architecture attempts to compromise between the needs of programs hosted on the architecture and the performance attainable in implementing the architecture.

sublevels.name: Maker
sublevels.description: Arduino, Raspberry Pi, sensor networks, sensors, xbee, 3D printing

sublevels.name: Register-Transfer-Level Implementation
sublevels.description: a design abstraction which models a synchronous digital circuit in terms of the flow of digital signals (data) between hardware registers, and the logical operations performed on those signals.

sublevels.name: Input/Output and Data Communications
sublevels.description: Input and output, as the process names suggest is the data communication going in and out of a machine. More specifically, input is the name given to digital signals and data incoming, while output is the outgoing data. The process of input/output involves input/output operations.

sublevels.name: Hardware Performance and Reliability
sublevels.description: Hardware performance and reliability are two critical aspects of computing systems that directly impact their functionality, efficiency, and user experience

sublevels.name: Arithmetic and Logic Structures
sublevels.description: An arithmetic and logic structures is the part of a central processing unit that carries out arithmetic and logic operations on the operands in computer instruction words. In some processors, the ALU is divided into two units: an arithmetic unit (AU) and a logic unit (LU)

sublevels.name: Data and Information Security
sublevels.description: Data security is the process of safeguarding digital information throughout its entire life cycle to protect it from corruption, theft, or unauthorized access

sublevels.name: Cryptology
sublevels.description: Cryptology is the study and implementation of techniques for secure communication in the presence of adversaries. Cryptography involves constructing and analyzing protocols that prevent third parties or the public from reading private messages. Cryptanalysis involves trying to break these cryptographic approaches. Related topics include: Encryption; Decryption; Key Management; Public-Key Cryptography, Public-Key Encryption, Asymmetric Cryptography, Digital Signatures; Elliptic Curve Cryptography; Symmetric Cryptography, Hash Functions, Block Ciphers, Stream Ciphers, Message Authentication Codes (MACs); Cryptanalysis, Cryptanalytic Attacks; Confidentiality; Data Integrity; Authentication; Smartcards; Passwords; Privacy; Quantum Cryptography; Ciphers; Random-Oracle Model; Cryptocurrencies; Cryptographic Hardware; Side-Channel Attacks; Untraceability; Pseudo-Random Sequences; Multiparty Computation; Lattice Algorithms, Lattice-Based Cryptography; Provable Security; Post-Quantum Cryptography; and supporting foundational and mathematical concepts from Computational Complexity Theory, Computational Number Theory, Information Theory.

sublevels.name: Computer Crime
sublevels.description: Computer Crime is a generic designation of a type of crime that involves or exploits weaknesses in computers and computer networks. This may also mean that a computer or electronic device may have been used in the commission of a crime. Common targets include: electronic devices such as a computer or cellphones; ATMs; individuals; companies; national security, finance, or healthcare systems; or critical infrastructure such as power grids, dams, or electricity-generating plant. Related topics include: audit trails; botnets; computer forensics; computer fraud; computer immunology; computer virus; computer virology; critical infrastructure protection (CIP); critical national infrastructure (CNI); cryptoworm; cryptovirology; cyber attacks or cyberattacks; cyber crime or cybercrime; cyber stalking or cyberstalking; cyber terrorism or cyberterrorism; cyber war or cyberwar; data recovery; data remanence; data theft; digital blackmail; digital evidence; digital extortion; digital forensics; firewall; hacking; honeypot; intrusion-detection systems (IDS); kleptography; malware; network intrusion; ransomware; security logs; spam; steganography; Trojans.

sublevels.name: IT Risk Management
sublevels.description: Risk management is the identification, evaluation, and prioritization of risks (defined in ISO 31000 as the effect of uncertainty on objectives) followed by coordinated and economical application of resources to minimize, monitor, and control the probability or impact of unfortunate events or to maximize the realization of opportunities

sublevels.name: Security Services
sublevels.description: A processing or communication service that enhances the security of the data processing systems and the information transfers of an organization. These services are intended to counter security attacks, and they make use of one or more security mechanisms to provide the service.

sublevels.name: Mobile and Network Security
sublevels.description: set of technologies that protects the usability and integrity of a company's infrastructure by preventing the entry or proliferation within a network of a wide variety of potential threats.

sublevels.name: Principles and Models of Security
sublevels.description: The basic tenets of information security are confidentiality, integrity and availability. Every element of the information security program must be designed to implement one or more of these principles. Together they are called the CIA Triad.

sublevels.name: Blockchain
sublevels.description: A blockchain is a dynamic list of records called blocks that are linked over time. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, a timestamp and transaction data. By design, a blockchain is resistant to modification of its data. The concept of a blockchain was invented to serve as the public transaction ledger of the cryptocurrency Bitcoin. For use as a distributed ledger, a blockchain is typically managed by a peer-to-peer network collectively adhering to a protocol for inter-node communication and for validating new blocks. Although blockchain records are not unalterable, blockchains may be considered secure by design and exemplify a distributed computing system with high Byzantine fault tolerance. Associated concepts include: Ethereum, smart contracts, Byzantine protocol, decentralized control.

sublevels.name: Digital Privacy
sublevels.description: Digital privacy is the ability to protect information about an individual or group. Related concepts include human, societal, and economic aspects of information security privacy; privacy-preserving data mining and information retrieval, and related usability tradeoffs; differential privacy and other cryptography and information security approaches to defining and quantifying privacy loss; legal frameworks such as GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) in the context of information privacy and data protection; privacy-preserving authentication; privacy-enhancing technologies and privacy by design; and end-to-end security and encryption.

sublevels.name: Computer Imaging, Vision, Pattern Recognition and Graphics
sublevels.description: Computer imaging, vision, pattern recognition, and graphics are interdisciplinary fields that involve the analysis, understanding, and manipulation of visual data using computers. Computer imaging refers to the acquisition, processing, and manipulation of digital images using computers,  Computer vision aims to enable computers to gain a high-level understanding of visual information from images or video sequences, Pattern recognition involves the automated identification and classification of patterns or regularities in data, Computer graphics deals with the creation, manipulation, and rendering of visual content using computers.

sublevels.name: Biometrics
sublevels.description: It involves the use of biological traits to verify and recognize individuals, providing a more secure and reliable method compared to traditional identification methods such as passwords or ID cards.

sublevels.name: Computer Vision
sublevels.description: Computer vision is a field of artificial intelligence (AI) that enables computers and systems to derive meaningful information from digital images, videos and other visual inputs — and take actions or make recommendations based on that information.

sublevels.name: Medical Imaging
sublevels.description: Medical imaging is the technique and process of imaging the interior of a body for clinical analysis and medical intervention, as well as visual representation of the function of some organs or tissues (physiology). Medical imaging seeks to reveal internal structures hidden by the skin and bones, as well as to diagnose and treat disease. Medical imaging also establishes a database of normal anatomy and physiology to make it possible to identify abnormalities.  (Although imaging of removed organs and tissues can be performed for medical reasons, such procedures are usually considered part of pathology instead of medical imaging.)

sublevels.name: Radiography
sublevels.description: Radiography is the use of X-rays or gamma rays to examine non-uniformly composed material; images are recorded on a sensitized surface, such as photographic film or a digital detector. Medical radiography includes examination of any part of the body for diagnostic purposes, such as detecting fractures or a bowel obstruction.

sublevels.name: Tomography
sublevels.description: Tomography is a technique whereby a subject is imaged in 'slices' or sections. Typically the imaging modality is X-ray radiography, and the slices can be viewed separately or in combination. Except for health sciences and medicine the method is also used in other areas of science, such as archaeology, biology, atmospheric science, geophysics, oceanography, plasma physics, materials science and astrophysics.

sublevels.name: Nuclear Medicine
sublevels.description: Nuclear medicine is a specialized area of radiology that uses very small amounts of radioactive materials, or radiopharmaceuticals, to examine organ function and structure. Nuclear medicine imaging is a combination of many different disciplines. These include chemistry, physics, mathematics, computer technology, and medicine. This branch of radiology is often used to help diagnose and treat abnormalities very early in the progression of a disease, such as thyroid cancer.

sublevels.name: Automated Pattern Recognition
sublevels.description: process of developing algorithms and systems that can automatically identify patterns or regularities in data without human intervention. It involves the use of machine learning, artificial intelligence, and statistical techniques to train computer systems to recognize and classify patterns in various types of data, including images, sounds, texts, and numerical data

sublevels.name: Virtual and Augmented Reality
sublevels.description: Virtual reality (VR) is a simulated experience that employs pose tracking and 3D near-eye displays to give the user an immersive feel of a virtual world. Augmented reality (AR) is an interactive experience that combines the real world and computer-generated content. The content can span multiple sensory modalities, including visual, auditory, haptic, somatosensory and olfactory.

sublevels.name: Computer Graphics
sublevels.description: Computer graphics deals with generating images and art with the aid of computers. Digital artwork, pictures, and animations are all examples that fall into this broad umbrella term.

sublevels.name: Image Processing
sublevels.description: Image processing is manipulation of an image that has been digitised and uploaded into a computer. Software programs modify the image to make it more useful, and can for example be used to enable image recognition.

sublevels.name: Computer Engineering
sublevels.description: Computer Engineering deals with the design and development of computers and digital systems encompassing system engineering that focusses on the design and management of computer integration and networks. These  fields often intersect and collaborate, as computer systems require an integrated system to communicate and function effectively.

sublevels.name: Internet of Things
sublevels.description: The Internet of things (IoT) is the network of physical devices, vehicles, home appliances, and other items embedded with electronics, software, sensors, actuators, and connectivity which enables these things to connect, collect and exchange data

sublevels.name: Servers
sublevels.description: A computer or computer program which manages access to a centralized resource or service in a network. servers are powerful computers or hardware devices designed to provide various services, resources, or functionalities to other computers, devices, or users over a network. Servers play a crucial role in managing and distributing data, applications, and other resources across the internet or local networks. They typically have higher processing power, memory, and storage capacity compared to regular personal computers.

sublevels.name: Computer Networks
sublevels.description: A computer network is a set of computers sharing resources located on or provided by network nodes. Computers use common communication protocols over digital interconnections to communicate with each other. These interconnections are made up of telecommunication network technologies based on physically wired, optical, and wireless radio-frequency methods that may be arranged in a variety of network topologies.

sublevels.name: Special Purpose and Application-Based Systems
sublevels.description: To aid the user in doing specified tasks by giving a platform that employs computing resources (i.e., hardware, firmware, and optionally software) that are physically embedded in, dedicated to, or necessary in real time for the performance of the system's mission.

sublevels.name: Cyber-Physical Systems
sublevels.description: Embedded systems that are integrated with the Internet and its users. Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) refer to integrated systems where computational elements (cyber) and physical components are tightly interconnected and work together to perform various tasks. These systems combine the capabilities of both the cyber and physical worlds to achieve goals efficiently and effectively. CPS integrate physical processes with computing, communication, and control systems, creating a seamless interaction between the physical and digital domains.

sublevels.name: Computer System Implementation
sublevels.description: Computer system implementation refers to the process of deploying and integrating a computer system into an organization or environment. It involves the installation, configuration, testing, and rollout of hardware, software, and network components to ensure the smooth operation of the system

sublevels.name: System Performance and Evaluation
sublevels.description: The performance of any computer system can be evaluated in measurable, technical terms, using one or more of the metrics namely: Short response time for a given piece of work, High throughput (rate of processing work), Low utilization of computing resource(s), Fast (or highly compact) data compression and decompression, High availability of the computing system or application, High bandwidth, Short data transmission time.

sublevels.name: Cloud Computing
sublevels.description: The  delivery of computing services over the internet, allowing users to access and utilize various resources and applications without the need for local infrastructure or hardware. It involves the provision of on-demand computing resources, such as storage, processing power, and software applications, through remote servers hosted in data centers

sublevels.name: Computing Milieux
sublevels.description: Computing milieux refers to the environments or contexts in which computing and computer-related activities take place. It encompasses the various domains, communities, and ecosystems related to computing.

sublevels.name: The Computer Industry
sublevels.description: Companies and individuals in this industry design, develop, and sell computer hardware and software technologies and solutions. Related publications describe how the industry is organized, and how it provides ideas, solutions, products, and services across all aspects of information technology.

sublevels.name: Computers and Education
sublevels.description: The integration of computers in education for instructional delivery, enhanced access to information and resources, and transformed the learning experience.

sublevels.name: The Computing Profession
sublevels.description: This relates to how people in the domain of Computer Science organize and act to develop the field. Stakeholders include researchers, developers, user communities, educational establishments, specialist professional organizations, and regulatory and governmental bodies. Their activities include research and development, teaching, funding, managing academic conferences and trade shows, and publishing related academic, professional, and user documents such as journal articles, conference papers, textbooks, monographs, and user manuals. Examples of organizations include the ACM (Association for Computing Machinery) and the IEEE (Institution of Electrical and Electronics Engineers).

sublevels.name: Personal Computing
sublevels.description: Personal computing means utilizing a computer at home or office where the input or output of data is conducted for personal or general use.

sublevels.name: Legal Aspects of Computing
sublevels.description: Legal aspects of computing are concerned with the legal aspects of digital information and software, as well as the legal aspects of the Internet.

sublevels.name: History of Computing
sublevels.description: The History of Computing involves the history of computing hardware technologies and computer software, the history of the ideas that support computational and information science approaches, and the history of the key actors in these developments such as people, organizations, and communities.

sublevels.name: Digital Society
sublevels.description: Digital Society adresses all aspects of the transformation of societies that are a direct or indirect consequence of digitalisation, in particular how we interact, work, and communicate.

sublevels.name: Computer Ethics
sublevels.description: Computer ethics, also known as cyberethics, is a branch of applied ethics that focuses on the ethical issues and dilemmas arising from the use of computers, digital technologies, and information systems. It deals with the moral principles and guidelines that govern the behavior and actions of individuals and organizations in the digital realm. Computer ethics address a wide range of ethical concerns related to privacy, security, data protection, intellectual property, digital rights, and the impact of technology on society as a whole.

sublevels.name: Automation
sublevels.description: Automation refers to the use of technology and machinery to perform tasks or processes with minimal human intervention. It involves the design, development, and implementation of systems that can operate independently, following predefined instructions or rules.

sublevels.name: Software Engineering
sublevels.description: Software is a set of computer instructions and can refer to executable programs, scripts and libraries. Or Software Engineering is a discipline that focuses on the systematic design, development, testing, and maintenance of software systems. It involves applying engineering principles and practices to create reliable, efficient, and high-quality software solutions that meet user requirements and satisfy specific objectives.

sublevels.name: Web Development
sublevels.description: Web development is the work involved in developing a website for the Internet (World Wide Web) or an intranet (a private network).[1] Web development can range from developing a simple single static page of plain text to complex web applications, electronic businesses, and social network services. A more comprehensive list of tasks to which Web development commonly refers, may include Web engineering, Web design, Web content development, client liaison, client-side/server-side scripting, Web server and network security configuration, and e-commerce development.

sublevels.name: Mobile Computing
sublevels.description: Mobile technologies are led by Apple’s iOS SDK for iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch development using the Swift programming language and by Google’s Android platform for various smartphones, tablets and smart watches, using Java APIs and now the Open JDK. Our books provide practical iOS and Android app development content for indie as well as for corporate app developers.

sublevels.name: Microsoft
sublevels.description: Microsoft Corporation is an American multinational technology corporation. It's best-known software products are the Windows line of operating systems, the Microsoft Office suite, and the Internet Explorer and Edge web browsers.

sublevels.name: .NET
sublevels.description: Software development framework from Microsoft, part of Visual Studio. .NET is a free, open-source, cross-platform framework developed by Microsoft that serves as a platform for building and running a wide range of applications.

sublevels.name: Windows
sublevels.description: Proprietary client and server operating system from Microsoft with desktop. "Windows" refers to the Microsoft Windows operating system, which is a family of operating systems developed and marketed by Microsoft Corporation. Windows is one of the most widely used and recognizable operating systems in the world, providing a graphical user interface (GUI) and support for various applications and hardware devices.

sublevels.name: Apple and iOS
sublevels.description: iOS is the mobile operating system developed by Apple specifically for its mobile devices, including the iPhone, iPad, and iPod Touch. It is a closed-source operating system known for its user-friendly interface, security features, and seamless integration with other Apple devices and services. iOS provides a platform for running applications, which are available through the Apple App Store.

sublevels.name: Open Source
sublevels.description: Open-source software is computer software that is released under a license in which the copyright holder grants users the rights to use, study, change, and distribute the software and its source code to anyone and for any purpose.

sublevels.name: Game Development
sublevels.description: Develop 2D and 3D games for desktop, mobile, web, console, smart watch and smart/connected TV game apps, using game engines such as Unity, Unreal, and GameMaker and languages such as C++, C#, JavaScript, Swift, and Java.

sublevels.name: Programming Techniques
sublevels.description: Programming techniques refer to various methods, strategies, and approaches used in software development to solve problems, optimize performance, improve code quality, and enhance maintainability. These techniques provide guidelines and best practices for writing efficient, readable, and maintainable code.

sublevels.name: Software Testing
sublevels.description: Software testing is an activity conducted in the software development life-cycle to verify that the software is accurate and works according to the requirements

sublevels.name: Operating Systems
sublevels.description: An operating system (OS) is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources, and provides common services for computer programs. Also, it serves as the point of communication or interface between a user and the computer's hardware.

sublevels.name: Compilers and Interpreters
sublevels.description: A compiler is a special program that translates a programming language's source code into machine code while An interpreter is a program that directly executes the instructions in a high-level language, without converting it into machine code.

sublevels.name: Software Management
sublevels.description: Software Management is a field of business and management research and practice that focuses on managing the development, delivery, and maintenance of software products and services. It encompasses the coordination of software development teams, the allocation of resources, and the creation of processes and methodologies for software development.  Major topics within the field of Software Management include:  Software Development Methodologies: These are frameworks used to manage the development of software projects. Examples include Agile, Waterfall, and DevOps.  Project Management: This involves the planning, organizing, and managing of resources to achieve specific software development goals within a given time frame and budget.  Software Testing: This involves the process of evaluating software products or services to ensure they meet quality standards and user requirements.  Software Maintenance: This involves the ongoing process of updating and improving existing software products or services to ensure they remain functional and relevant.  Software Metrics and Measurements: This involves the use of quantitative data to measure and track the progress of software development projects and assess their success.  Software Quality Assurance: This involves the process of ensuring that software products or services meet established quality standards and requirements.  Risk Management: This involves identifying, assessing, and managing risks that could impact the success of software development projects.  Software Architecture: This involves the design and organization of software components and systems to ensure they are scalable, maintainable, and meet user requirements.  Team Management: This involves managing software development teams to ensure they are effective and efficient in achieving project goals.

sublevels.name: Business Informatics
sublevels.description: Business informatics (BI) is a discipline combining economics, economics of digitization, business administration, information technology (IT), and concepts of computer science.

sublevels.name: Business IT Infrastructure
sublevels.description: Business IT infrastructure refers to the set of hardware, software, and networking components that support the flow of information within and between organizations. It is a critical component of modern business operations, as it enables organizations to efficiently store, process, and share data, and to communicate with customers, partners, and suppliers. As a field of business and management research and practice, business IT infrastructure encompasses a wide range of topics, including: IT strategy and planning: This involves developing a comprehensive IT strategy and aligning it with the organization's overall business goals and objectives.  Network design and management: This involves designing and managing the organization's computer networks, including local area networks (LANs), wide area networks (WANs), and virtual private networks (VPNs). Data storage and management: This involves managing the organization's data storage systems, including databases, data warehouses, and data centers. Security and privacy: This involves implementing measures to protect the organization's information assets from unauthorized access, theft, or loss, as well as ensuring compliance with data privacy regulations. Cloud computing: This involves leveraging cloud-based services to reduce IT costs, improve scalability and agility, and enhance collaboration and data sharing. IT governance and compliance: This involves establishing policies and procedures to ensure that IT resources are used in a responsible and ethical manner and comply with relevant laws, regulations, and industry standards. Emerging technologies: This involves monitoring and evaluating new and emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, and the Internet of Things (IoT), to identify opportunities for innovation and competitive advantage.

sublevels.name: Multimedia Information Systems
sublevels.description: Multimedia Information Systems (MIS) couple data management capabilities (effective and efficient methods for storage, indexing, querying, and retrieval) with media management (media representation, data compression, standardization, and transmission).

sublevels.name: IT Operations
sublevels.description: IT Operations includes Outsourcing, Management of Computing and Information Systems as well as Maintenance, releasing, updating server os, databases and applications, monitoring and providing services and applications supporting the business processes

sublevels.name: Software Management
sublevels.description: Software Management is a field of business and management research and practice that focuses on managing the development, delivery, and maintenance of software products and services. It encompasses the coordination of software development teams, the allocation of resources, and the creation of processes and methodologies for software development.  Major topics within the field of Software Management include:  Software Development Methodologies: These are frameworks used to manage the development of software projects. Examples include Agile, Waterfall, and DevOps.  Project Management: This involves the planning, organizing, and managing of resources to achieve specific software development goals within a given time frame and budget.  Software Testing: This involves the process of evaluating software products or services to ensure they meet quality standards and user requirements.  Software Maintenance: This involves the ongoing process of updating and improving existing software products or services to ensure they remain functional and relevant.  Software Metrics and Measurements: This involves the use of quantitative data to measure and track the progress of software development projects and assess their success.  Software Quality Assurance: This involves the process of ensuring that software products or services meet established quality standards and requirements.  Risk Management: This involves identifying, assessing, and managing risks that could impact the success of software development projects.  Software Architecture: This involves the design and organization of software components and systems to ensure they are scalable, maintainable, and meet user requirements.  Team Management: This involves managing software development teams to ensure they are effective and efficient in achieving project goals.

sublevels.name: Business Information Systems
sublevels.description: Business Information Systems (BIS) is a field of study that focuses on the effective and efficient use of technology and information systems to support the operations, management, and decision-making processes of businesses. BIS combines elements of computer science, management science, and business administration to develop and implement systems that improve business performance.  Some of the major topics in BIS include:  Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP): ERP systems integrate and automate key business processes, such as accounting, inventory management, and customer relationship management.  Customer Relationship Management (CRM): CRM systems are used to manage customer interactions and improve customer satisfaction and loyalty.  Supply Chain Management (SCM): SCM systems optimize the flow of materials, information, and finances across the supply chain to improve efficiency and reduce costs.  Business Intelligence and Analytics: BIS helps businesses to collect and analyze data to support decision-making processes.  E-commerce: E-commerce systems enable businesses to conduct transactions online and reach a global audience.  Knowledge Management: Knowledge management systems help businesses to capture, store, and share knowledge and expertise within the organization.  Cybersecurity: BIS focuses on the protection of business information systems from cyber threats, such as hacking and data breaches.  Overall, BIS aims to align technology with business goals and objectives to create a competitive advantage for the organization.

sublevels.name: Business Process Management
sublevels.description: Business Process Management (BPM) is a discipline within the field of management and information technology that focuses on designing, modeling, executing, monitoring, and optimizing business processes. BPM seeks to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of business operations by aligning them with the strategic goals of an organization. Major topics within BPM include: Process modeling: This involves documenting and representing business processes using diagrams and other visual aids. Process modeling helps stakeholders to understand the flow of activities, inputs, and outputs in a process, and to identify potential bottlenecks and inefficiencies. Process automation: This involves using technology to automate routine or repetitive tasks within a process. Process automation can help to reduce errors, improve consistency, and free up human resources to focus on more complex or strategic activities. Process optimization: This involves identifying areas for improvement within a process and implementing changes to streamline and improve its performance. Process optimization can help to reduce costs, increase customer satisfaction, and improve overall business performance. Process monitoring: This involves tracking the performance of a process over time, using metrics and other indicators to identify trends and areas for improvement. Process monitoring can help to identify bottlenecks, inefficiencies, and other issues that may be affecting the performance of a process. Process governance: This involves establishing policies, procedures, and guidelines for the management of business processes within an organization. Process governance helps to ensure that processes are consistent, compliant, and aligned with the strategic goals of the organization. Process innovation: This involves exploring new and innovative ways to design, execute, and manage business processes. Process innovation can help to drive business growth, create competitive advantage, and improve overall organizational performance.

sublevels.name: Business Analytics
sublevels.description: Business analytics is the process of transforming data into insights to improve business decisions. Data management, data visualization, predictive modeling, data mining, forecasting simulation, and optimization are some of the tools used to create insights from data.
